ResponsesInList.Title: Modernizing questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Questionnaire needs some love. This popular Moodle plugin has been in use since the early days of Moodle; close to 20 years. As such, it has collected a lot of technical debt. In order to continue to maintain this plugin effectively, it requires a refactoring of the code. This refactoring will: bring it up to current Moodle coding standards, separate function into maintainable classes, significantly reduce the amount of code, improve performance, set the path for future maintainability. In order to achieve this, I need to dedicate time and resources. I have set up a sponsorship page on Github to help fund this work. I will also create a project with defined tasks, allowing other developers to join in if they wish. More details will be posted as I have them.

ResponsesInList.Title: Modernizing questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Update - I am setting up a project on Github to track this work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Way to Export All Form Responses Across Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I hope you're doing well. As a Moodle 4.5 Administrator, I'm looking for an efficient way to export responses from all forms (Questionnaire activities ) across all courses, without having to open each course individually. Does anyone know if this is possible — either via a plugin, report, or a backend solution? Thanks in advance for your help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Way to Export All Form Responses Across Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry, I have no suggestions for existing questionnaires. But but if it helps for future Questionnaires that you build, there's a "Public" option for Setting up a questionnaire . Then you can keep all your questionnaire data in 1 course instead of running around gathering that data from wheverever the questions are located. From the docs: "Public - can be shared among courses. Create various "Public" Questionnaires in a course where students are not located. Once they have been created with the "public" setting, then you may use those "public" questionnaires in other courses where students are enrolled -- the number of settings available to such questionnaires is limited and you cannot edit its questions nor view the responses in the course where the students attempt the questionnaire, but the data will push to the course where the Public Questionnaire(s) was created. Example: If a public questionnaire has been created in course A, it can be "used" in courses B, C, ... All the responses from courses A, B, C, ... are collected in the public questionnaire created in course A (the original course where it was created) and are viewable there by the person (admin or teacher) who originally created it."

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire release 4.1.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ihor, Again, please ask only ONE question per post...😉 Question #1 Generating Reports for Each Questionnaire There is currently no option in the Questionnaire plugin to hide unselected questions in the branching scenario. If you have admin rights on your Moodle site (or if your Moodle site admin agrees), simply add a CSS rule in your current Moodle theme, for example: Current theme = Boost Go to Tab:Advanced settings In Raw initial SCSS insert this rule: #page-mod-questionnaire-myreport .qn-container:has(.qn-number .unselected) { display: none; } Here is the demonstration When students view their own responses they only see those questions that they responded to. Hope that helps. Edit .- You can use CSS to take this even further by inserting this set of rules: #page-mod-questionnaire-myreport .qn-container .unselected, #page-mod-questionnaire-myreport .qn-info:has(.unselected), #page-mod-questionnaire-myreport .qn-container img.req { display: none; } This will hide not only the unanswered questions but also the unselected choices (in multiple choice questions). It will also hide the un-necessary "required" red icon. As per this screenshot: Question #2. Merging Reports into One Final Summary " At the end of the learning process, participants complete all four questionnaires within the same thematic context. Is there a way to combine all four reports into a single final report? " Simple answer is No. But you might be able to produce such a combination of x reports by exporting the reports to Excel (or similar software) and write routines to do this. Sorry, can't help with this procedure. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Make slider question require ... or not
ResponsesInList.Text: " Is this like it suppose to work? " Yes! This is not weird at all, given the very nature of the slider question type. Suppose the slider question is: "How much do you like tea?" and the following options are made available on a 1 to 10 scale: Not at all / A lot. By default the slider displays the middle index, i.e. 5. This means that the following 2 situations are equivalent: a) the student does not reply or b) the student selects the middle index: both situations result in the middle index (5) being given as an answer. The only problem is the case where a student unwillingly oversees that slider question and thus is supposed to have replied "5" when in fact they love tea and would have liked to select index "10".

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding excessive info from the report
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joseph,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding excessive info from the report
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Marina, 1/ You can hide the "All participants diagrams" with CSS . 
```text
#page-mod-questionnaire-myreport  #cvs2 {


display:none


}
```
 Add this code in Site administration > Appearance > Themes > Boost, "Advanced settings" tab in "Raw SCSS" box (if you use the Boost theme). 2/ The HTML template of the report page is built with "reportpage.mustache" file in the templates Questionnaire plugin directory.. In this file, remove the line 83 : 
```text
{{#responses}}{{{.}}}{{/responses}}
```
 to remove the responses in the report

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: getting & instead &
ResponsesInList.Text: Yeah questionnaire encodes the labels on everything to prevent you from putting in html or scripts. It's actually the mustache templating system that does it. you have to modify the /mod/questionnaire/templates/question_drop.mustache template. Instead of {{label}} it has to read {{{label}}} (e.g. three curly brackets instead of two. not very intuitive.) If you're not able edit files on the server then you're out of luck with the ampersands or other glitchy encodings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Using score as a dependency
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd like to be able to use the score/value of a previous question response as a dependency for subsequent questions. E.g. show a question if you scored X or above on a previous response.  I had been thinking of having extra score options representing less than, equal or greater than, and a score value enabled when one of those options is selected. I can emulate this with some question types (e.g. choice, choices, yesno, etc) by using multiple optional dependencies on each possible answer. This is not currently possible on the Rate question type (which is primarily where I want to use it). I can emulate a rate question using multiple radio button questions but it's not possible to display multiple questions in a table like the Rate does. I also looked into extending Rate to list all options (e.g. question+choice+degree) but the database doesn't have anywhere to store the extra context value needed to select a rank degree (and listing mulltidimensional data isn't great in a select box, as shown below). I shoehorned some code into the plugin/db to give it a go but it's not pretty. If I wanted a question or label to appear because in my Rate I selected any item above 2 in a 1-5 scale for any of 5 answer choices, I'd have to add 20 optional dependencies. If I wanted a question to appear because I chose a degree above 2 in all choices in the parent question, then I'm stuffed, whereas if the degrees had a value (score) and choices summed the scores, I could at least figure out the value meant that certain degrees had all been selected. Hence the need for a score.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Personality test: using more than one counter in answers by Fabio Roman
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Carlos, I also have a similar scenario as you do. I need to make a personality test in which the answers can have their own counters. So far I haven't found a solution. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Personality test: using more than one counter in answers by Fabio Roman
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Adlan, I'm afraid this is not going to work, quite simply because your questionnaire is incorrectly built. For testing personality traits, you should ask questions where the answers are the opposite of each other. For instance, if you want to test the “Detail-Oriented” vs. “Delegates Details” Personality Trait, you should ask questions like the following: (taken from this site ) Q1 a. I like projects made up of many small tasks (0) b. I like to look at the big picture and develop new projects (1) Q2 a. I can see patterns in complex problems quickly (1) b. I enjoy research projects that allow me to hunt for specifics and spot errors (0) Q3 a. I am good with numbers, including positions in accounting and finance (0) b. I am good at strategic thinking and being creative (1) ... To test Extrovert vs. Introvert: (taken from this site ) Q4 a. I get more excited by ideas than by external activities . (0) b. I am primarily interested in and concerned with the external world. (1) Q5 a. I prefer a few deep, close relationships to many casual ones. (0) b. I prefer talking with someone rather than sitting alone and thinking. (1) ... Subsequent analysis of the responses would look like this: Respondent #1 Q1 to Q3 : score 0 = "Detail-Oriented" personality score 3 = "Delegates Details" personality I hope this makes sense. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Identifying the Parent Questionnaire

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Identifying the Parent Questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: There actually is no easy way ... definitely an oversight. In the database , you can find the parent questionnaire using: SELECT q.* FROM mdl_questionnaire q INNER JOIN mdl_questionnaire_survey s ON s.id = q.sid WHERE s.realm = 'public' AND s.courseid = q.course This will return all public surveys where the course id's are the same in the questionnaire table and the survey table. That is, the parent questionnaire. The child questionnaires will similarly be:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recurring questionnaires, when are they re-opened

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Recurring questionnaires, when are they re-opened
ResponsesInList.Text: They are all based on the user's last attempt time compared with date format codes . So if daily, the current "numeric day of the year" must be greater than the last attempt's "numeric day of the year" (format code 'z'). If weekly, the current "numeric week of the year" must be greater than the last attempt's "numeric week of the year" (format code 'W'). If monthly, the current "numeric month of the year" must be greater than the last attempt's "numeric month of the year" (format code 'n').

If a student uses a period, no problem, his answer is accepted and recorded.  In the example below, three students that used a comma as a delimiter see that they answered the questionnaire, but those answers are NOT visible from the teacher's perspective, only three other responses using periods are shown: I've tried changing the course language to see if this would change anything, no dice. How can I fix this? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Numerical questions do not accept commas
ResponsesInList.Text: You are correct, the Questionnaire numeric question type only accepts the dot/fullstop character as decimal separator. This matter of different decimal separators often comes up on the Quiz (and Lesson ) Moodle forums and causes no end of problems. How I wish the dot/full stop character were adopted as an international standard! It's already the de facto separator used on most calculators and computer numeric keyboards. The only solution I can see in your situation is to instruct your questionnaire respondents to use the dot/full stop in their answer. By the way, I can't remember when the decision was taken to introduce decimals in that numeric question type in questionnaire. I expect it's rarely used if at all. I'm curious to find out what you need it for, if you don't mind telling us.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Numerical questions do not accept commas
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joseph, I met with the teacher who reported the problem. He was adapting his questionnaire to a rating scale used by his department, he wanted to use a 1 to 10 scale based on a 1 to 100 scale, so decimals were required to give, say, a 8.7 (or 87%) rating in the context of a peer evaluation.

ResponsesInList.Title: The confusing "public" option
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a great tool, but the different options "Private" "Template" and "Public" semms to be confusing to our users. Many seem to think this, or they understand some of it but not all: "Private" means it becomes a private template, which they can use anywhere in the system "Template" becomes a template anyone can use "Public" also becomes a template anyone can use. The big issue is the "Public" option, which almost everyone think is a like a community template that any teacher can use, in any course. The teacher A creating it thinks he makes a template for anyone to use in their own course The teacher B using it thinks he's creating a new questionnaire for his own course The teacher B doesn't understand that the students answers are being sent elsewhere, and thinks the questionnaire is faulty The student answering doesn't know his answers are sent into another course The student can see his own answers, and tells the teacher he has answered the questionnaire. Still the teacher B cannot se the answers, and there is no way to tell which public questionnaire he copied to begin with, when he is looking att the settings. The teacher A originally creating the questionnaire are suddenly getting a lot of answers in his questionnaire - more than he has participants in his course, actually... and he cannot see in the settings of his questionnaire where they are coming from. I suggest some development: A permissions setting to USE public questionnaires, like there already is a permissions setting to CREATE them (we didn't react on this confusion fast enough, and our system now have several hundred public questionnaires floating around being mistaken for templates) An option to make system wide actual templates , that anyone can create their own questionnaire from to use in their course without sending the answers elsewhere. The option for administrators to easily administrate (find, change, move, delete) both public questionnaires and the suggested system wide templates It would also be great to be able to sort these system wide templates into categories.

ResponsesInList.Text: There was never anything wrong with the data. The only problem was in how it was displayed. If you are seeing an issue in the data stored in the database , that is some other problem. Note, that the response data was fixed so that previous data for rates which would have been stored as 0-4, are now stored as 1-5. ResponsesInList.Title: View All Responses Security Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Setting Students can view ALL responses to NEVER does not prevent students from accessing the View All Responses report of a questionnaire. The setting seems to only remove the hyperlink from the student role and not prevent access. This is a big security issue since, under certain scenarios, a student could easily figure out how to access the view all responses report without that hyperlink. One example is if a course uses 2 types of questionnaires where 1 questionnaire View all responses is set to never and another questionnaire where View all responses is set to visible. It wouldn't take much for a student to figure out that changing the instance parameter from the questionnaire where view all responses is visible will take you to another questionnaire and the View all set to never will not restrict the student from viewing the report. The security problem was first reported back in 2011 here https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=166492 .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: View All Responses Security Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Question - was the setting changed to "never" before or after a student submitted a response? I did a test on my 3.5 system -- I created a questionnaire, set the View all Responses setting to 'Never,' and then logged in as a sample student to submit  a response. There was no "view all" link, but when I attempted to use the teacher URL see the "view all" (when logged in as a test student), and i got the message that I dont have the permission to View all responses. However, in a separate test, I created the another questionnaire, left the View all Responses setting set to 'immediately after submission', then I submitted a  response as a test student , then I logged in as the teacher and changed the "view all" setting to "Never". When I logged back in as a student, that "Never" setting was not respected -- the test student could still see and view the responses with the teacher URL as you have noted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: View All Responses Security Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, I investigated this a little more and I was able to replicate your first test and got the same result with the Don't have permission to view all responses message. However it seems that the reason you got a different result on your second test is that you submitted a response. To test this I created a brand new questionnaire from a template with the View all responses set to N ever from the get go. These are the steps I took: I made a submission with Student A -- -> Then I logged in as Student B and pasted the view all link copied from teacher's role and I got the permission error you described -- -> I then made a submission with Student B and pasted the same view all link that gave me a permission error but this time I got through and could see all responses. The only variable from getting a permission error and getting through to view the View all report was that I made a submission. For now the only way to prevent this seems to manually set the role permissions for each questionnaire to prevent viewing all responses from the student role.

ResponsesInList.Title: Negative degrees for rate questions in personality test
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I would like to use the Questionnaire plugin to create a test of the type called The Big Five. Example: https://sites.temple.edu/rtassessment/files/2018/10/Table_BFPT.pdf For this I'm using Rate (scale 1..5) questions with Normal type of rate scale and possible answers like: 1=Disagree 2=Slightly disagree 3=Neutral 4=Slightly agree 5=Agree It works great for a half of the questions, but one feature of this test is that when calculating the score, some response values should be subtracted rather than added (see page 5 of the doc for reference). For example, for the question "I don't talk a lot." when one chooses Disagree, then one has to subtract 1 from the total sum. I tried to put (-1)=Disagree (-2)=Slightly disagree or -1=Disagree -2=Slightly disagree But the plugin doesn't recognize such values. Is there any way to encode negative degrees for some questions in the current version of the plugin? If not, could you advice which function(s) in the plugin files is responsible for adding values, so that I could try to complement it with recognizing negative values? I'm a JS developer, not PHP, but I would like to try to figure this out and contribute to the plugin if it works out well Thanks in advance!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Negative degrees for rate questions in personality test
ResponsesInList.Text: Your post caught my eye.   I wanted to do something like this years ago for a personality test. I tried to figure it out with a lesson , quiz and questionnaire modules.  I could not do it. There are two problems: grouping questions to calculate a score for individual groups of questions, and the negative numbers.  Maybe someone has a better solution.  Here is my rethink. If you gave 5 quizzes or 5 questionnaires, you could group scores.  Each of the questions relates to only 1 of the 5 personality qualities.  Somebody has to have research about randomizing questions about personality qualities get "more accurate" scores than grouping questions.  Since this is an art form, I would not give any pre test clues about the groups to my students.  You could be clever and mix in a few questions from other qualities and give them a zero score for any answer.  Perhaps you can code a way to jump between 5 different questionaires, always landing on the next unanswered question. The negative numbers issue has a math solution. Change all the numbers to positive and there is no negative issue !  The difference between -5 and 5 is 10.  The difference between 0 and 10 is also 10. Negative thinkers always bother me, why can't they put things in just a positive framework? They would have less trouble in the real world I used the numbers in the link you provided for the "Extroversion" scores.  I put them in an Excel spreadsheet and did the math.    I put another column and added the sum of the scores.  I added 10 to each of the scores in the first column and found the sum.  Then I added 20 to the first column sum of the scores and 10 to the other column.  I ended up with the same 10 of 40 possible points.    Just to make sure it worked, I changed all the minus numbers to -1 in both scoring methods.  I ended up with 26 of 40 points using both methods. Positive creative thinking provides a solution once again. Thank you for your post.   You helped me think through how I am going to create a tool for an academic readiness class I am teaching for the first time.  Hope this helps you as well.  Good luck. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Negative degrees for rate questions in personality test
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is the spreadsheet.  Probably easier to understand than words.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Negative degrees for rate questions in personality test
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris! Thank you very much for your response. Your math solution looks perfect to me! I didn't think of this approach! A few notes from me: 1. "If you gave 5 quizzes or 5 questionnaires, you could group scores." It is possible to group scores within a single questionnaire by adding questions to different "Feedback sections " as a part of the plugin. The questions can be in random order. 2. I think this solution requires a particular initial number for each section to even the total scores, same as in the standard calculation method provided in the example doc. The reason is that each section (column) has a different number of "negative" questions, so the total sum will not be equal for each of them. The solution I came up with later was inspired by another questionnaire's scoring method (attached). The negative questions in there are reverse scored. " To reverse score an item, change 1 to 5, 2 to 4, 4 to 2, and 5 to 1. " This way it doesn't require initial number for each column (I guess). I tested this approach by completing my questionnaire and the one by Open-Source Psychometrics Project at the same time, assuming that their test uses the standard method of subtracting negative questions. The result of my questionnaire was quite accurate when compared to theirs, but not totally equal. Thank you again for sharing your solution! I will try it out as it seems to provide more accurate result than mine Have a nice day! Regards, Marta

The answer would determine what percentage of 10 the person scored. For example 10% would be the equal of a -5. ResponsesInList.Title: Problem with "Delete ALL Responses" and public questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm having a pretty specific issue with Questionnaire on Moodle 3.5 and 3.6 using Nginx and PostgreSQL on Gentoo machines - I've been able to replicate it on two machines so far. Both machines are running the latest version of Questionnaire - 2018121000. To replicate the issue: 1. Create three courses - we'll refer to them as Questionnaire Home, Questionnaire Outpost 1, and Questionnaire Outpost 2. 2. Make a questionnaire in the Questionnaire Home course, set it as a Public questionnaire. Give it at least one question. 3. Make a questionnaire on the two "Outpost" courses, using the content from the questionnaire on the "Questionnaire Home" course. 4. Submit responses on the two questionnaires in the "Outpost" courses, so that you end up with two responses visible in the "Home" questionnaire. 5. Attempt to use the "Delete ALL Responses" control in the "Home" questionnaire to delete the responses. You'll get a blank white screen, with no error messages in any log I was able to find, even with debugging at maximum. You can get around the error by submitting at least one response in the "Home" questionnaire - then "Delete ALL Responses" will work. This leads me to think that the error happens when you try to use "Delete ALL Responses" in a questionnaire that has responses, but all of those responses come from questionnaires other than the one you're using the "Delete ALL Responses" control on.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with "Delete ALL Responses" and public questionnaires

ResponsesInList.Title: Default Read response summaries, subject to open times permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: I would just like to raise an issue that has caused a problem within our organisation. The students were able to complete a questionnaire with comments sections that had personal information. It seems as though the default setting for 'Read response summaries, subject to open times' allows students to view each others responses and this has caused some problems. My question is should this be the default and can I change it if so?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Default Read response summaries, subject to open times permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: I suppose that by "comment sections" you mean your questionnaire contained "Essay box" questions. The idea behind the "View all responses" feature is to enable individual students to compare their questionnaire answers with those of their fellow students. That's why the feature is default-enabled for the student role in Questionnaire. Please note that when a student views all their fellow-students' responses, their names are not displayed. Which means that "personal information" cannot normally be related to the actual respondents' identity. However, if you create a questionnaire that contains Essay box questions and you do not want the answers to such questions to be displayed, then the only way to do this, for that specific questionnaire only, is to set the desired permissions in that questionnaire's permissions. See the steps below.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic model content synchronization within questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Yannick, I don't think what you describe can be done in a Questionnaire activity, without a leot of modification to it's code. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade Moodle 2.5 to 3.4
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - There are many changes in function and data structure from the 2.5 version, so you should definitely upgrade with your Moodle installation. If you upgrade your Moodle to sub versions, you should also upgrade your plugins to those stop points. So, if your Moodle goes from 2.5 to 2.9 and then to 3.4, upgrade your plugins to their 2.9 versions as well. The questionnaire uses Moodle's standard upgrade process, which is designed to manage the data and ensure no loss or corruption. So as long as you do things properly with the upgrade process, you should be fine. That said, it is software, ans surprises can happen. You should always do a test upgrade on a non-production copy of your site first, and then verify everything went fine. Then make sure you keep a backup of your production data before you do the main upgrade. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Classroom course evalation
ResponsesInList.Text: I have done this since 2006 with the questionaire module.  If you are not doing a blended course, you need to make a course. We run a F2F semester long program with 30 to 100 evaluations.  We have two standard evals.  One for academic subjects and one for each food service week. We also put PDFs and exams  in the Moodle course.  When the course repeats, we use a backup of the old without student data and restore it to a new course. We also have 3 or 4 day F2F courses, that may run once or twice a year.  We use the same course, copy the old eval activity and give it a new name (add a date like Spring 2017) so when we do a summary we see the date.    Ditto with the exam. We hide the old eval and exam,  We change the password to get into the course. Hope those two ideas help you figure out a system that works for you.  You could also add a certificate using the same techniques. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Conditional OR branching
ResponsesInList.Text: So...Feedback and Questionnaire are very similar.  Feedback is part of core; Questionnaire is a third party plugin. They do a lot of the same things but are not the same. Feedback can do branching (and does branching better than old versions of Questionnaire--but it sounds like newer versions of Questionnaire have stepped it up).  I'm using 2.8, so I can't really say much about newer Feedback. That may be the confusion? Quiz is, essentially, a test. It doesn't do branching.  Feedback lets you do evaluations, inventories, etc and does do branching and is part of all Moodle installations.  Questionnaire lets you do evaluations, inventories, etc and does do branching but is not part of all Moodle installations--it has to be specially installed. Instructions for Questionnaire issues won't work for either Quiz or Feedback.

ResponsesInList.Title: How is the weekly period defined?

It doesn't seem to be based off the start date of the course, and I can't find any setting which makes it teacher-configurable. A teacher-configurable week would actually be my preference, though I respect that's probably a significant change. My use cases work off the assumption that a faculty member wants a questionnaire filled out once per calendar week. If it's defined by the student's behavior, there's the potential for cascading procrastination. (If you don't fill out this week's survey until Friday, then you can't fill it out the next week's survey until next Friday. You'll never be able to dig yourself out.) Of course, sometimes that's how the world works and maybe you should learn that lesson sooner rather than later. But I hate it when a system imposes "life's tough, get a helmet" pedagogy on a class.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade issue to moodle 3.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andreas - The upgrade to 3.3 changes the 'username' field from a character field to an integer field and renames it to 'userid'. It has always been used to store the Moodle userid and has only been named 'username' from an old legacy conversion. The error message you posted indicates that the 'username' field contains the value 'Anonymous'. The 3.3 upgrade will not work in this case, as it expects to find only numeric values in the 'username' field. I have looked back through the code, all the way back to the 1.9 version, and can find nothing that would have put 'Anonymous' into that field. My thoughts are that one of the following must be true: Your version of questionnaire was customized at some point to put 'Anonymous' instead of the 'userid' into that field; probably when the questionnaire was an anonymous one. Someone actively manipulated the database field to set those values. Unlikely though. The code prior to 1.9, put 'Anonymous' into that field for an anonymous questionnaire. Have you been running questionnaire from the days before 1.9? If this is true, I will need to add a step that modifies that field to a numeric value before doing the conversion. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bypass "Answer the Questions..." Screen
ResponsesInList.Text:
If
you want to completely skip the "Answer the questions..." page, I think the best
solution would be moving your questionnaire to a topic that isn't displayed but
still accessible (I don't know of a good way to do that, but you can see a
workaround described here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=62201 ). Then, open the questionnaire and click
the "show more answers" text, so that the form is displayed. Now copy
the url of the page (it should end with "&resume="), and add a
web-page link resource (using the url you just copied) where the questionnaire
activity was before you moves it. If anyone knows of a better way to make
an activity invisible to the users yet accessible via a direct link, I would love
to hear about it. Anyway - I hope this helps anyone who has the same problem and comes across this thread.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bypass "Answer the Questions..." Screen
ResponsesInList.Text:
Correction - what
you have to keep an eye for isn't the "&resume=" but the "complete.php"
instead of "view.php". One problem with this method is that
you'll have to re-create the whole system if you want to copy the course
(because you will want to refer to the copied quizzes, rather than the original
ones). If that isn't possible for you - I
found an even better, and easier, solution: In the questionnaire settings, there is a Description field - you can use it to
bypass the opening screen. First - you'll have to make sure that you don't have the "Display
description on course page Help with Display description on course page" -
if you must display the description on your course page ignore this method, as
it won't be of use for you. You'll now want to edit the description
- make sure it is empty to begin with (since it won't be displayed on the
course page, and we are skipping the "answer questions" page, there
will not be anywhere to see it anyway) Go into html editing mode (for that you'll have to press the show more buttons
option, and then the HTML option - which's logo looks like this <>). Now - simply paste the following code: <script> var x = document.URL; x=x.replace
("view", "complete"); x+="&resume="; console.log("you
were redirected to: "+x); window.location.href
=x; </script> I hope that helps you or whoever else
wants to skip this screen!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bypass "Answer the Questions..." Screen
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you Yaniv . That did the trick perfectly ...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bypass "Answer the Questions..." Screen
ResponsesInList.Text: That's great to hear! In my reply I suggested that it is impossible to both skip the "Answer the Questions" screen, and display a questionnaire description in the course page. On a second thought that's incorrect - you can use this code: <script> var x = document.URL; if (x.indexOf("questionnaire")!=-1) { x=x.replace ("view", "complete"); x+="&resume="; console.log("you were redirected to: "+x); window.location.href =x; } </script> After you paste this code in the html editor, you can go back to the normal rich text editor mode, and add your description (which will be displayed in the course page, if you check the "Display description on course page" option) - without causing any errors. I really doubt you, or anyone else for that matter, would like to do that, but just in case...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Existing questionnaires and responses missing after upgrade
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Please follow these below steps of Upgrading in Moodle docs : ------   Move your old Moodle software program files to another location. Do NOT copy new files over the old files. Unzip or unpack the upgrade file so that all the new Moodle software program files are in the location the old files used to be in on the server .
```text
Note: There was an exception for Activity modules. In the past, activity modules used $module-> instead of $plugin-> in their version.php files. The $plugin-> notation support for activity modules was added in Moodle 2.5 (
MDL-38121
) and became recommended. Support for legacy $module-> was dropped in Moodle 3.0 (
MDL-43896
).
```
 So the $module format still works in 2.5 (and did when all of that was tested). I searched through the code for Moodle version 2.5.9, and it definitely is looking for "module->" for activity plugins first. Are you sure your Moodle code is all 2.5.9? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire response order after adding responses in dropdown
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a know issue with questionnaire. Care should always be taken when modifying the questions of questionnaires that have already been completed by some users. When it was developed, it was assumed that questions would remain mostly static, so that response reports made sense. The problem with changing choices in a drop down (for example), is there is no easy way to determine if a change is being made to the text of an existing choice, if a choice is being removed, or if a choice is being added. The code assumes position is important, and assumes that if the text changed for an existing position, then that choice's text changed. If the list gets shorter, choices are deleted from the end of the list. If the list gets longer, choices are added to the end of the list. What needs to happen is that there needs to be a more extensive choice editor, so that selections can be made from defined choices. It is not a small change. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to create 2 Questionnaire  1 for Student Role and 1 for any other user role.
ResponsesInList.Text: I think, what you are asking, is how to assign roles to specific instances of a questionnaire? This is the same for any module. You need to assign specific roles to the specific module instance's context (see - https://docs.moodle.org/32/en/Assign_roles#Activity_Module_context ). ResponsesInList.Title: How is anonymity technically assured when using the questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear community, we use the questionnaire tool for course evaluations and to ensure anonymity, we set the r espondent t ype to "a nonymous". One of our students (who has an IT background) now asked us how Moodle technically assures this anonymity, does anybody know? Kind regards, Astrid

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How is anonymity technically assured when using the questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - An "anonymous" questionnaire is not "truly" anonymous. There are data tracks that can allow someone with access to the database to determine who responded. However, an anonymous questionnaire will not reveal who submitted the response through any of the standard UI elements. So, a teacher in a course cannot see who the respondents are if they are reviewing the responses. And, if a questionnaire has been set to "anonymous", and responses have been submitted, it cannot be set to be "not anonymous". Information identifying the respondent with the response is still stored in the database. This allows an anonymous questionnaire to still allow "one response per user" for example. Data still exists, identifying the user in the "questionnaire_attempts" and "questionnaire_response" tables as well as the Moodle logs. But, you would need to access the database via mechanisms other than the questionnaire UI to extract that information. I have created issue CONTRIB-6135 to discuss the possible need for more anonymity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How is anonymity technically assured when using the questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle does not assure any anonymity and it is a good idea if people assume that nothing on the internet or web is truly anonymous from someone who really wants to track them.  You might get "more anonymity" from one set of code than another (e.g. where it did not require a user to be logged in), but  in the final analysis you will not be entirely anonymous. Read through what Mike has written and his links for more information as I noticed he is the Questionnaire maintainer, so knows what he is talking about.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How is anonymity technically assured when using the questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Astrid, Good point.  Mike and Marcus are spot on.   As your IT student probably knows, not much is truly hidden from everybody when it comes to a internet/intranet traffic or the interaction between a browser and a program like Moodle. I would be cautious as an expert researcher because there are no guarantees that a specific student actually filled out a specific questionnaire.   Only that someone apparently filled it out with a specific user id. The world is filled with potential uncertainties Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How is anonymity technically assured when using the questionnaire?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How is anonymity technically assured when using the questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, in the case of questionnaire, the "anonymous" option is intended to prevent anyone from seeing who submitted the questionnaire, including teachers. It prevents any user identifiers from being displayed in the questionnaire UI anywhere. But, there are still ways for a suitably privileged and motivated user to identify what submission goes with what user. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How "risky" is this plug-in?
ResponsesInList.Text: This a good question to ask, and one I would hope any admin asks before installing a new plugin. One can actually break it down a bit more: Does this code introduce any security holes? Does this code introduce any performance issues? Does this code have any accessibility issues? Will an upgrade to this plugin exist when I want to upgrade to the next version of Moodle? Working those out yourself is hard, so there is an alternate proxy set of questions you can ask that are much easier to answer: Has anyone else reviewed this plugin and published the results? Who are the people who created this plugin? How many other Moodle sites are known to run it? For recent Moodle versions, has a compatible version of this plugin been made available quickly? For the questionnaire module, those questions have good answers: Yes. E.g. it is on the list of plugins that Moodlerooms are happy to install for their clients: https://en-us.help.blackboard.com/Moodlerooms/Administrator/010_Get_Started/About_Moodlerooms/Plugin_Matrix#community It is maintained by Remote Learner, who were a Moodle Partner Company for many years, so know what they are doing with Moodle code: https://github.com/remotelearner/moodle-mod_questionnaire . 8000+ other sites are using it https://moodle.org/plugins/stats.php?plugin=mod_questionnaire . (That includes us at the Open University. We've been running it happily for years.) Yes. Scroll down https://moodle.org/plugins/mod_questionnaire to the Awards, and note that 3.0- and 3.1-compatible versions were ready early. Do maintainers communicate clearly about the fix? Do they keep transparent record of the fixed issues? How do they respond to bug reports or feature suggestions? In my experience, this developer-user human relations are even more important than the technical quality of the code itself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can I add further questions once students have started responding?
ResponsesInList.Text: I would like to gather information from my students at various intervals as their course progresses over the academic year.  Once students have responded to early questions, can I add further questions so that at the end of the year I have one cumulative body of data rather than many smaller ones?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I add further questions once students have started responding?
ResponsesInList.Text: You can add more questions to a questionnaire after users have responded. Its usually not a good idea, as it makes the overall data inconsistent. But, once a user has submitted a questionnaire, they cannot change it. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I add further questions once students have started responding?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks.  By "inconsistent", do you mean that users would be able to go back and change their previous answers? Janet

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I add further questions once students have started responding?
ResponsesInList.Text: Users cannot change their previous answers once a questionnaire has been submitted. If they save a work in progress, they can change answers until they submit it. But the results are not available to anyone else until they submit. By "inconsistent", I mean the overall data results. If some users have answered one set of questions, and then you change or add/delete questions, the users who answer after that have different structured data. That makes it difficult to do any kind of analysis on the overall results. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Internal Server Error
ResponsesInList.Text: I ran into this problem with the Questionnaire module just recently after upgrading my Moodle from 2.6 to 2.8.  The link that Joseph provided above was no longer available, so I am reporting an edited version of what my website support person described to me about my problem and how to solve the problem of internal server errors when using the Questionnaire module after an apparently successful installation. This seems to be a simple matter of a file or directory being over-permissioned--with directories "writeable by group" My questionnaire directory was permissioned wide open, with full 777 write permissions set by owner group and public. The highest that any PHP file, or directory that contains them, should be set to is 755, with 644 being the most common. The website support person found some odd, and indeed errant permission settings on all of the PHP files within. The files were all set with the public write bit set to on, so indeed, even if the /questionnaire directory was properly set, then none of the PHP scripts would run correctly. The website support person advised setting my /questionnaire directory to 755. Then set the PHP files within it to either 755 or 644. I followed this advice and my questionnaire module seems to be working within Moodle 2.8. Regards, Tim

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Edit Feedback Table
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tom, Just be aware that when you change this, anywhere else in Moodle that uses "All participants" will be changed too. As admin go to Administration > Site administration > Language > Language customisation. Select your language then Open language pack for editing. Once the pack has loaded, click Continue. In the Show strings of these components list box, select moodle.php. In the Only strings containing box, type All participants, then click on Show strings. In the Local customisation text box, type in your desired change then click on Save changes to the language pack. When asked Do you wish to save these changes to your local language pack, click on Continue. The change should show up next time you visit or reload that page.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students Visualizing Other Answers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hannah - There are two ways to control who can see the responses for a questionnaire. The first control is through capabilities. You can control capabilities per role, per user and per instance in the standard Moodle way. I have attached a screenshot of the specific capabilities that control response availability for questionnaire below: The "Read all responses any time" capability is required to be able to view all of the responses regardless of other settings. The "Read own responses" is required to even see your own. If you want to ensure that a certain user or role can never see any of the responses, make sure they do not have any of the response capabilities assigned. For the case above, the "student" role is only able to see their own response. The other way to control response access is through the specific questionnaire's settings. These options are as follows: That allows you to control when a student who can access responses is allowed to see them. From what you are asking, I believe you want to use capability restrictions. mike

So the procedure is (: Set "Display charts for "Personality Test" feedback" to "Yes" in Questionnaire settings (Site administration-->Plugins-->Activity modules-->Questionnaire) After that create new Questionnaire and when adding questions set the "Response is required" to "Yes", because this data will be used in charts. IF NOT SET TO REQUIRED: you will not see the advanced settings as described below. When all questions are entered, go to Yours Questionnaire "Advanced settings" and look there for "Feedback options". There You can set up a chart and various ways how to show results. Pay attention that if you use 1 feedback, then there will be only charts with single column available. If use 2 or more, then another charts will be available to use. More detailed information is in Questionnaire Personality test .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change reply to address in Questionnaire response email
ResponsesInList.Text: @Brian, No, I was not missing your point, but now at last you've made it clear so I can understand. To sum up: you set up your questionnaire so that when your students submit their responses you will receive an email containing their responses. Upon receiving that email you want to reply to the students, with remarks ("notes") about their submission. I am a little doubtful about what you call "corrections". The Questionnaire activity in Moodle is a survey-like type of activity meant to gather information, opinions, etc. from respondents. Responses to Questionnaire questions are - in standard usage - never "correct" or "incorrect". This is quite different from e.g. the Lesson or the Quiz activities , whose goal is to test the students' knowledge, and usually results in a score or grade. Anyway, here is how you might hack the email function of Questionnaire (version for moodle 2.3) to suit your purposes. In file /mod/questionnaire/locallib.php, around line 1510, replace this line: `if (email_to_user($userto, $userfrom, $subject, $altbody, $body_html)) {` with `if (email_to_user($userto, $userfrom, $subject, $altbody, $body_html, '', '', '', $USER->email)) {` This will put the user (i.e. the student)'s email address in the "Reply to" field of the email that is sent to you. Please note that this supposes that your questionnaire is NOT set to "anonymous", of course. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire PHP 7 Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: As a temporary fix, you can open  ...yourmoodle/mod/questionnaire/questiontypes/questiontypes.class.php and comment out line 297 with two forward slashes, so that you have: //break; // Out of the case. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Selection order scrambled after course restore
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a known issue with backup and restore, and it can be quite subtle to detect, for reasons I will explain. The problem is that backup does not normally guarantee the order in which things are written to the backup file. It just does SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE ..., and according to the SQL standard, that is allowed to return records in any order. However, in practice, with a new DB, the records will be returned in the order the were inserted, for a while at least. ... Problems only start to occur after some rows get deleted from the table, and then the database maintenance functions (e.g. VACUUM in Postgres ) run to compact things. Then the record order becomes random. So, the solution is to override the SQL used by the backup system, to do ORDER BY id. E.g. https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/backup/moodle2/backup_stepslib.php#L2130 or https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/backup/moodle2/backup_qtype_plugin.class.php#L61 Except, even that is not the only problem. ORDER BY id does not work either, if you are running ORACLE in clustered mode, since then ids may not be allocated in order. See MDL-43447 for the gory details. So, really, if you care about order, you should probably use your own sequence field.

ResponsesInList.Title: Guest access for questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: In response to quite a few requests on this forum I have started to tackle this feature, for a future release of Questionnaire (2.7). But first I need some help from those who are interested in using that feature. I would welcome some descriptions of use cases. Why do you need the feature? Who would create the questionnaire? Who would use the responses data? (I mean which role , probably Admin, since a teacher cannot access a questionnaire on a Moodle site's front page . Would you need questionnaires available to guests and located not on the site front page but inside a course "open to guests"? (with or without a password?) What kind of questions would you ask? I mean, mostly MCQ , or text answers as well, etc. In brief, try to convince me that you desperately need a "guest questionnaire". Is it OK if the same "visitor" answers your front page questionnaire several times? What is the value of the responses data in that case? Or do you need a way to prevent multiple answers? A workaround I am contemplating is using the visitor's IP address to tell them "you have already answered this questionnaire", but that is neither easy to implement nor totally fool-proof. Do you want a "guest questionnaire" to be available ONLY to guests or to logged in users as well? (Not sure this is desirable nor possible to implement). Thanks for your valuable input, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Guest access for questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Ciao Giancarlo, I'm sorry if this discussion gave you a false hope. My last attempt to adding a "guest submission" feature to the Questionnaire activity is described in that other discussion: One man one vote ... no more . Considering all the responses and warnings (especially regarding security) I got in that other discussion I came to the conclusion that "guest submission" to the Questionnaire is not a good idea after all, and I will definitely not implement it. See my conclusion here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=245802#p1066606 . Here are my answers to your 3 reasons for wanting a "guest submission" to Questionnaire. 1.- For registered users, make the responses anonymous. Of course, as an admin, you may breach that anonymity, but that is a matter of trust between you and your moodle site users. If the users of a moodle site do not trust their admin, then that is a serious problem, but outside of the scope of this discussion. 2.- If you need to "ask opinions from people who do not have an account" on your moodle site, then there is no need to use a moodle activity. In fact, a moodle site is really meant to be used by registered users, not by "guests", although it can be open to guests so they can browse some activities. For instance, it is not possible for a guest to submit answers to a quiz. I suggest, as I always do in those cases, to use the excellent LimeSurvey software. 3.- Again, using a non-moodle survey such as LimeSurvey is the ideal solution. I have used it myself on a number of similar occasions. Finally, as suggested by Mary, if you absolutely need/want to use a Moodle activity for guests, you can always use the Feedback activity. All the best, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Youtube videos in Questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Mary, sorry to keep bugging you, but I noticed all of your badges, including the documentation one. I was thinking that the "My embedded video is too big/small. How can I change its display size?" section of the Media FAQ could be a little more clear. I wrote some changes, and was hoping you could cast an "editor's eye" on them, rather than me just implementing them without asking anyone: My embedded video is too big/small. How can I change its display size? Changing the size of an embedded video depends on whether you're u sing Moodle's Multimedia plugins filter or if you're either embedding a video from another source using something like an iframe (for example, embedding a video from YouTube using the embed code they provide). If you're using Moodle's Mulimedia plugins filter, your video will appear to you in the html editor as a hyperlink. Whether it's a video hosted elsewhere (ie Vimeo or Youtube) or a file you've uploaded yourself, it will still appear as a hyperlink. After you've saved this html, Moodle's Multimedia filter will turn that hyperlink into an embedded video. In order to change the video's size you need to: Click the HTML code icon: [same picture that's already in the Docs after this step] Find the <a href...> code for the video you want to change. In the href="LINK" section of your code, place your cursor right before the last quotation mark. Type "?d=100x200" where you're replacing "100" with your desired width and "200" with your desired height. For example, if you want a video that's 600 x 325, you would type ?d=600x325." [SAME PICTURE THAT'S ALREADY THERE FOR THIS STEP] Your <a> tag should now look something like the following If you're working with a file you've uploaded yourself: <a href="https://yourschool.edu/draftfile.php?file=/135/user/draft/617331337/Module%.mp4?d=425x234"> If you're working with an externally hosted file: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TubRpuaNVT4d?600x135"> Click "update" in the HTML source editor screen, and save your changes. Your video should now be the new size. If you're using an embed code, such as an iframe, it's a little easier: Click the HTML code icon, as above. Locate the <iframe> tag or equivalent. Inside that iframe should be "width" and "height" variables, which you can adjust as needed. [SAME PICTURE THAT'S ALREADY THERE FOR THIS STEP] Click "update" in the HTML source editor screen, and save your changes. Your video should now be the new size. Thanks for your eyes on that, Mary!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2.7.3: Questionaire - Response option: allow branching
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Monica, For the scenario you describe, only the first question HAS to be named. Each of the questions you want to be answered has to list the NO side of the first questions name as its Parent. If you do not, then someone who answers yes will see any question not listing the NO side of the first question as its parent. Also note that when you use parent this way, the questionnaire module is going to automatically stick a page break in between each question and they cannot be deleted. Where do I set the name of the Parent question/branching? When you make all your no branch questions, click the down arrow for Parent Question and select the No side of the first questions name. How do I set the end page the my Yes response? No need to really as they will just go directly to a page with Previous Page and Submit questionnaire buttons, but you could put a label question type as your very last question. If you do add a label you will need to set its Parent Question to the yes side of the first questions name. HTH , AL

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students can see the replies of others - where did the "never" option go?
ResponsesInList.Text: To answer your first question... the "never" option didn't really work properly.  You need to use the mod/questionnaire:readallresponses capability instead.  If you do not allow this capability, users will not be able to see other people's responses. The other capability to look at is m od/questionnaire:readownresponses, which controls whether users can see their own responses or not. If this survey is different to the majority on your site, you may want to override the capability at the activity level - setting it to prevent will block access even if the default is to allow. On your other question - have you purged the moodle caches after editing the language string?  They are cached at the server side, not in your local browser, unless you have the langcache config setting (in site admin > language settings) disabled .

ResponsesInList.Title: Should the Questionnaire title default to empty?
ResponsesInList.Text:
I've run into an annoyance with questionnaire that I think can be fixed fairly easily. When duplicating a questionnaire it brings the name and title filled in already with the same value. So to change what the questionnaire is called, you have to change both values, on two different forms. The title is defaulting to the name, but it seems to actually copy the 'name' value to 'title'. A different approach would be to allow the title to be empty and default it to the name when it's used. For example, in the print_survey_start function there is a line: echo '

'.s($this->survey->title).'

'; that could be changed to echo '

'.s((strlen($this->survey->title)>0?$this->survey->title:$this->survey->name).'

'; You would also have to make the title field not a required field. This would solve the problem above such that unless you specified a custom title, you would only have to change the name to get it to display correctly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should the Questionnaire title default to empty?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nate, Which versions of Moodle and Questionnaire are you using? Which method do you use to "duplicate" a questionnaire? Let's take an example, using Moodle 2.6 or latest 2.7. I have a questionnaire Named "Questionnaire 01" and entitled "Course evaluation". In Teacher Edit mode, I click the Edit link and, in the menu, I click the Duplicate link. Once my Questionnaire 01 has been duplicated, it is displayed in my course's list of activities under the same name, Questionnaire 01. So I click the little pen icon next to that name, and change this to Questionnaire 02. The title of the questionnaire remains unchanged ("Course evaluation"). You write "[...] to change what the questionnaire is called [...]". This is not clear, please refer to Name and Title, not "is called" which is ambiguous. I agree that it may seem unnecessary and confusing to have both a Name and a Title for a Questionnaire instance, but I do not quite understand why you see this as a problem. Please explain. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should the Questionnaire title default to empty?
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry for leaving some holes.  We're currently using Moodle 2.6.3 and Questionnaire 2014041801.  We're using the duplicate function from the Edit dropdown. Here's our problem.  Our users don't generally have a difference between the name and the title.  In fact our support person didn't realize there was a title field.  When they first setup the Questionnaire and fill in the name, field, that value is copied to the title field in the database (automatically).  When they later come and duplicate the questionnaire and rename it, they need to go to both fields in order to rename it completely (which they haven't done because they didn't know the title field existed). I propose an alternative to copying the value of the name field to the title field when the questionnaire is created.  Allow the title field to be left blank and when displaying the title field, the plugin should check to see if the field has been given an explicit value and if not it should display the name field.  In this way, when users make a copy of the questionnaire without realizing there are two fields, they will only have to change the name of the Questionnaire once, in the name field, and the title field will inherit that value implicitly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should the Questionnaire title default to empty?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the clarification, Nate. I have opened an issue in the tracker and might adopt your "fix" in a further version of Questionnaire. CONTRIB-5274 . Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Should the Questionnaire title default to empty?
ResponsesInList.Text: After thinking this over, I've decided not to take any action. Indeed, when a Questionnaire instance is duplicated, it may be desirable to keep the same "title". Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Manager role forces a user to be a potential respondent on questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: Apologies if this is a known issue, but in searching the forum and bug tracker I have not seen it mentioned... I've found that, on our installation, by giving a user account the "Manager" role (default configuration) at the system level, her account displays as a potential respondent in all questionnaires across the site (Moodle v. 2.7.1+, Build: 20140807 ; Questionnaire v 2.7.0, Build: 2014070401). This issue arose when a teacher sent a reminder (via questionnaire/show_nonrespondents.php ) to all of the non-respondents to an anonymous questionnaire, generating an email (Moodle internal messaging is disabled on our system) to the staff member with Manager role. The staff Manager is not "enrolled" with any role in the course in question. Given the questionnaire's anonymity, the teacher could not see the staff member as being on the list, but my subsequent testing on other questionnaires/courses with demo accounts confirms that apparently any account with the Manager-role appears as a potential respondent or non-respondent, as the case may be, regardless of the questionnaire or course. Further, clicking on the Manager user's name in the list of non-respondents generates a message confirming that the user is not enrolled in the course, rather than displaying the user profile. The Manager role is one our site rarely uses, so the problem for us is minor, but assuming the issue is not peculiar to our installation, it could be a bigger problem for others, if not a security issue (for example if one or more functions are mistakenly assessing user capabilities in assembling the non-respondents list for a questionnaire). It may also happen with other roles, as Manager is the only one I have tested. I hesitate to file a bug report, as this could be unique to our installation or just a boneheaded misunderstanding on my part. We've used Questionnaire with much satisfaction for years - many thanks to the developers who have provide it for us!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manager role forces a user to be a potential respondent on questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, Thanks for your interest in the Questionnaire plugin. If you do not want your Manager role to have anything to do with the Questionnaire instances in courses on your Moodle site, simply edit the Manager role and remove all permissions for Questionnaire. Site administration ► Users / ► Permissions ►Define roles Manager / Edit role / Filter: Questionnaire : uncheck ALL permissions. Joseph EDIT.- See also CONTRIB-5311 .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deploying Questionnaire School-wide
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ryan, Unfortunately what you want is not possible. The only way is for you, as admin, to create a public questionnaire in a special course with no teachers and no students, then ask your teachers to "copy" that public questionnaire to a private one in their course (or do it yourself), so the students can answer it in each course and you can view the consolidated results in your "special course". Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Compare answers from multiple questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: @Heddy, I am replying to your question further to the discussion you started in the Quiz forum here . The Questionnaire plugin/add-on would be suitable for your purposes. In your favourite spreadsheet, import the responses file and manipulate the data to make the calculations. Here are some screenshots showing parts of the process.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question management
ResponsesInList.Text: Is it possible to undelete a question? Sorry to drag out an old question with a new answer (that's not related to Questionnaires but rather to Quizzes), but this question shows up high on the list in Google when I searched for Moodle Question Undelete. I have the problem using Moodle 2.7 (I explain after the answer). The deleted questions for me showed up as "old questions" in the quiz editing GUI (if you have checked " Also show old questions " in the GUI. You can get these questions back with a little creativity. Edit (gear icon) one of these "old questions", and inside the Editor, click the "Make copy" button. The new copy of the question won't be flagged as an "old question", so you have re-created the deleted question. It's not quite an un-delete (the "old question" remains), but at least you can move forward. Now for the context that got me here. I had for some unknown reason duplicated questions in many categories (perhaps by copying a course and/or importing questions from other courses, since we're not able to share the question banks easily). See my other various posts about that... While trying to delete the duplicates, I was informed by Moodle that it wasn't possible because the questions were in use in quizzes (they all had "*" next to them). However, later I saw that they actually were deleted (even though they show up now as "old questions"). The problem is that the quizzes that used these "old questions" are now broken, because they had random questions that drew from the category. My students got an error that there are not enough questions in the category, and the quiz fails.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire vs Feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cris and thanks for your interest in the "survey-type" modules in Moodle. 1.- The Feedback vs Questionnaire comparison discussion has been going on for quite some time, see e.g. this discussion (started back 8 years ago): Questionnaire and Feedback Modules - Opinion . Obviously  both modules have evolved radically since then and include new features. 2.- You write that "Telling us to "install it and figure it out yourself" is frustrating to me" and I quite understand the feeling. I was actually thinking of people having a (local) Moodle test site of their own, where they are completely free to install add-ons without having to ask an admin. Another possibility to test out Questionnaire is to go to my online test site. See the instructions here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=245086 3.- " I suggest starting a page on the wiki that compares/contrasts the two. " I vaguely remember doing something like that years ago. It is a lot of work, takes a lot of time and I am not ready to invest in this at the moment. I prefer to spend my time writing an exhaustive documentation for the module I maintain (an exhausting task in itself). The feedback/questionnaire comparison page you point to is outdated, by the way. 4.- "Moodle's Questionnaire seems to have the feature of specifying "N/A" as an answer, but looking at http://docs.moodle.org/27/en/Questionnaire_module#Types_of_reports I'm not able to see if I can get the same Analysis (with bar graphs of responses, averages) that I get in a Feedback." You're loooking at the wrong page, please read this page: Viewing_Questionnaire_responses . 5.-  "Can Questionnaires be "anonymous" like Feedback? It's important for students to give frank feedback without fear of retribution". Yes and no. Yes it's possible to set a Questionnaire to be "anonymous". But it's not possible to have non-logged-in guests to answer questionnaires. 6.- Can I export a Questionnaire's questions so it can be shared in other courses (with other professors using Moodle) like I can with Feedback? When an admin or teacher creates a questionnaire instance, they can create "Public" or "Template" questionnaires which can be used in other courses on your Moodle site. Again, the documentation explains this feature here: Setting_up_a_questionnaire#Questionnaire_Type . In conclusion, do take the time to read the whole Questionnaire documentation (it will take you only one hundredth of the time it took me to write it ), do try  Questionnaire on my online test site. And if you have any more questions, you are welcome to ask them in this discussion. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire vs Feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joseph!  We greatly appreciate the Questionnaire and the work you have put into developing it.  One of our favorite uses for it is to create a self-scoring weekly journal.  In many of our courses, our students are required to keep a weekly journal...where they reflect on the course content, or are to monitor some aspect of their own behavior or health, or are to investigate something, or need to document their service learning activities .  For these items, the instructors are not so concerned with grading what the students write or discover....but want to ensure that the students are doing the reflective process every week.  The questionnaire allows the students to get points automatically in the grade book for completing/participating...without the instructor needing to hand-enter each score.  The instructor can quickly review the "journal" and if a student is not properly doing the work...take points away from just those students---making  this is a great time saver for the instructor. If in some future version it was possible for the instructor to give feedback to the students responses in the questionnaire...that is something some instructors would like to see.   Thanks for a great tool! -regards, Troy Challenger

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: mod_questionnaire upgrade broken
ResponsesInList.Text: This tends to happen to me a lot on development servers. The quickest hack to get Yvon upgraded is to go into the database, find the row in the config_plugins table where plugin='mod_questionnaire' and name='version' and change the number from 2013122201 to 2013122200. What this means is that the 2.5.9 upgrade script has already run, but the 2.6.x upgrade will now run because the oldversion number is lower than the new one. A permanent fix might be to use 2013122201.01 or other higher number in the 2.6.x branch instead of 2013122201.  But this will mean that for users with 2013122201 already applied on 2.6.x that the upgrade script will run again.  In most cases that doesn't cause a problem because of the if exists checks, but you might need to add a few checks if there is anything that can't be run twice.

ResponsesInList.Title: Save Resume & Update Questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm using the latest version of the questionnaire module. We are using it to collect student information, however, we need our students to be able to update their responses even after they have submitted their answers. At the moment, it appears students can do this, however, they are required to re-enter all their responses (approx 30), therefore, my question. Is it possible for students to view their responses in edit mode, when they are updating their questionnaire. If yes, what changes do I need to make to my questionnaire. Thanks, Loreta.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Save Resume & Update Questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Loreta. There are two settings that you can use in Questionnaire. #1 Response options / Type / Respond many This allows students to respond to the same Questionnaire as many times as they wish. But their previous responses are indeed not displayed when they answer again, they have to start afresh. #2 Response options / Save/Resume answers / Yes This allows students to begin answering a questionnaire, then save their answers and leave the questionnaire, to come back to it later, edit or complete their answers and either save again or submit. Please note that, in that option, teachers can not view the student's answers until the questionnaire has been submitted. What you want would be a 3rd option which could be described as follows: #3 Response options / Type / "Respond many and review" This would allow students to respond to the same Questionnaire as many times as they wish. Each time they respond to an already responded to questionnaire, their previous responses would be displayed for them to edit. Would option #2 be a solution for you? If not, would you like to see option #3 to be implemented? I cannot make any promises, as I have not yet looked into the feasibility nor the amount of development time which might be involved. ATB Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Branching to a different part of a course based on Questionnaire answers
ResponsesInList.Text: If you have Moodle 2.6 and the latest version of Questionnaire (2.6) then you can achieve this by using the "personality test" feature. Create your MCQ questions with a "value" of e.g. 0 (zero) for all responses leading to the text presentation and a value of 1 (one) for all responses leading to the video presentation. Make sure you have an odd number or questions (3, 5, 7, etc.). In Advanced Settings, Feedback options, select General Feedback. On the " Editing Questionnaire Feedback Messages " page, in the Feedback Score boundary 100% Feedback  box, put a link to your Video Presentation and in the 50% box put a link to your Text Presentation. After completing the questionnaire, your students will be presented with a feedback page with either the link to the Video or the link to the Text presentations, according to their "responses score". Please note that the "redirection" will not be automatic, the students will have to click on the relevant link. Please note that your initial idea of using the "conditional branching" feature will not work, because conditional branching only works within a questionnaire instance, not inside the course. Joseph
