ResponsesInList.Title: Return to the confirmation page...?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am using the "Confirmation page" in a Questionnaire (accessible under the "Advanced settings" tab > "Submission options" section in my version of the Questionnaire plugin) to deliver feedback to students. For instance, we have students respond to some materials and prompts in a Questionnaire, and after they click "Submit," they are presented with general feedback on the confirmation page. From there, we might send them back to the Main Course Page, or for a few of them, tell them to click "Continue" so that they can see all participant's responses in addition to their own (had to change some permission to make that happen, by the way). When the student leaves the confirmation page, however, they can no longer return to that Feedback. The only way I know of allowing that to happen would be to allow multiple responses to the Questionnaire, and then the student would just put gibberish into the boxes and Submit the gibberish. Is there another way to allow students to return to the confirmation page, and the information included there? My second comment is very small, and that I had a user who wasn't terribly Moodle savvy complain that the "Continue" link on that confirmation page made her think that she was "Continuing on to the next activity" -- each of these Questionnaires is labeled "Activity 1 - Title," "Activity 2 - Title," and so on. Would changing that word "Continue" to "Review your response" or something else be advisable? I'm not sure I have an opinion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Return to the confirmation page...?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matt and thanks for your message. 1.- The "confirmation page" is only meant to contain a kind of "thank you for completing this questionnaire" acknowledgement. Strictly speaking, you cannot call its contents "feedback", as for me real feedback is dependent on individual choices made by respondents. Such "real feedback" is provided, for instance, by the "personality test" feature introduced in the 2.6 version of Questionnaire. Different feedback messages are displayed according to the choices made by individual respondents. Actually, I have a bone of contention with the so-called "General Feedback" feature that is to be found e.g. in the Quiz activity. I maintain that feedback cannot be "general" and can only by "specific". But that is another story. 2.- " For instance, we have students respond to some materials and prompts in a Questionnaire... " I'd be curious to know what are those "materials and prompts"? 3.- " When the student leaves the confirmation page, however, they can no longer return to that Feedback. " Yes, that is by design. If you are using version 2.6, one way you could retain a "permanent" feedback would be to hijack the "personality test" feature. You could introduce at least one question (yes/no, MCQ or Rate)  that you would use for that "general feedback", and which would be "permanent", i.e. the students would be able to view it as many times as they wish, by going to the "Your responses ► Individual responses" page of the questionnaire. 4.- The string "Continue" is used in many other places in Moodle activities and does not mean anything particular. Actually, it gets its meaning from the context and from what gets displayed on the next page that is reached. Changing it to anything more specific might cause problems. For instance, changing it to "Review your response" would be misleading if a Questionnaire's permissions were set to deny the student role from reviewing their own responses! I hope this answers your question(s), if not, do ask for more. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Guest permissions in Questionnaire 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Isabelle (and Mary). In Moodle 2.0, security (paranoia?) has been re-inforced. By default, is is now no longer possible for non logged-in users (aka guests ) to do any action which writes data to the moodle database . The same rule applies to forum, feedback, etc. This is controlled in the modules db/access.php file (and applies to all modules, including forum and questionnaire). Anyway, as I think I've already said in this forum, it does not make much sense to allow guests (non-logged in users) to answer a questionnaire. If only because if it so happened that 2 (or more) guests were answering the same questionnaire at the same time, their responses would be "mingled" and the result would be meaningless. If you absolutely need an anonymous questionnaire for guests, then I recommend setting up a survey outside of your moodle site , using for example the excellent open source survey provided by LimeSurvey . Joseph EDIT.- Things being as they are, it would certainly be more logical if the "submit" capability were simply removed from the capabilities settings for Guest in those modules which do not allow submitting. That would avoid the confusion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student created questionnaires/surveys
ResponsesInList.Text: @John, Yes, this is a roles/permissions problem, and not specific to the Questionnaire activity, of course. It is quite possible to give students the capability to Add (i.e. create) questionnaire instances (and questions) in a course. However, in order for students to do that, you must also give them the "Manage activities" capability, to give them access to the Turn editing on button. But then, this means that students with that "Manage activities" capability will be able to manage (i.e. change settings, delete, etc.) any other activity already created in the course. As far as I know, there is no way to restrict permissions to one and only one type of activity (or resource) in a moodle course. Of course, if you trust your students and have a special course where they can "play" with a (restricted) teacher role, then go ahead. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Anonymous questionnaire (2.6) and List of responses etc.
ResponsesInList.Text: Further to my answer in this discussion here , I am contemplating some changes to the "anonymous" questionnaire behaviour (in version 2.6 and maybe porting back to 2.5). 1.- Up to version 2.4, the "List of (individual) responses"  was available to the teacher, through a navbar displaying only numbers. If the questionnaire was set to "anonymous", then each individual response was displayed with the heading "Respondent: - Anonymous". 2.- In version 2.5, that same "List of (individual) responses"  was available to the teacher, through a navbar displaying the names of the respondents. In an anonymous questionnnaire, in order to preserve anonymity, the "List of responses" link was simply removed from the tabs (and from the Questionnaire Administration bock). Now, considering the discussion mentioned above, I think that was perhaps not the best decision, and I am thinking of making the list of individual responses available again to the teacher, by displaying a list of links called "Response 1", "Response 2", etc. There may be situations when a teacher wants to view all "anonymized" individual responses to a questionnaire, I think. That is the system currently used by the Feedback plugin. 3.- Now, we need to examine the "Show non-respondents" feature. Since that feature became available (in 2.5), it is available to the teacher, for full-name as well as anonymous questionnaires. My view is that - even for an anonymous questionnaire - a teacher may want to check non-respondents in order to send them an email reminder. However, the availability of that feature may pose a problem with anonymity, as a teacher may deduce from the list of non-respondents the list of those who have responded, and even the identity in the case of one student only having responded. The Feedback plugin has taken the position to obviate this potential problem by removing the "show non-respondents" feature from anonymous feedbacks. Should I do the same with questionnaire? I'm waiting for your reactions, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to go to previous page with Skip Logic enabled when required questions on page unanswered
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bob. I suppose you are talking about Questionnaire 2.5. 1.- What has not changed with the new "skip logic" feature is that it is not possible for a respondent to navigate back (or forward) from a page which contains an un-answered required question. 2.- What is new with the "skip logic" feature is that I have created an exception to that former rule, as follows. If a page contains one (or more) un-answered required question(s) AND that page is the child of a parent (located on a previous page), it is possible to navigate back to that previous "parent page" without answering any required questions first. The rationale for this "exception" is that, upon arriving on a child page, and viewing the questions asked on that page, a respondent may realize that they made a "wrong" choice on the previous parent page and wish to go back and change their choice. In that situation, it would not be sensible to require of the respondent that they answered questions that they might not encounter again, should they change their choice on the parent question page. 3.- On the contrary, coming back to the rule explained in #1, when a respondent is viewing a page with a required question that is not a child of a previous question, they it makes sense to force them to answer the required question before navigating back to the previous page, since, whatever they do then, they will always come back to that page containing the required question. 4.- However, for the sake of simplification, a better option might be to ALWAYS allow a respondent to navigate back to previous pages without forcing them to answer required questions. I will study this and, if there are no adverse opinions expressed nor any unwanted behaviours of the programme, I will implement that option. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Combining Questionnaire and Quiz for Branching
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Anita, " User can take quiz and after one of the question he will be directed to Questionnaire and back to Quiz depending on question responses. " That is quite impossible. What you must understand first of all is that the Moodle Quiz activity is a Test -like activity, whereas Questionnaire is a survey -like activity. Tests are used to test an individual respondent's knowledge , and to give them a score of aptitude. Surveys are used to gather the opinions of a panel of respondents , and do not lead to a score of aptitude. Thus these two types of activities have their own, totally different uses. Your only option , if you want to test a respondent's knowledge or aptitude and use a branching feature, is the Moodle Lesson activity. However, as you may already have noticed, the Lesson activity does not offer the variety of questions that are available to the Quiz activity. Hope that helps, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Groups and the show non-respondents report
ResponsesInList.Text: One of Joseph's new features in 2.5 questionnaire is the show non-respondents report which allows you to see a list of the students who haven't submitted survey answers and to send them a message. Something we've just noticed is the way it works with groups... If there are no groups then any-one who can see that report can see the entire list of students on the course and message them. If there are visible groups then any-one who can see that report can see the entire set of groups and each group's list of students on the course and message them. If there are separate groups then any-one who can see that report can see the groups of which they are a member and each group's list of students on the course and message them. It seems a little scary to me that any-one, like with the non-editing teacher role, would be able to see the full list of students on the course and message them.  Perhaps you should only be able to message people you're in a group with?  And maybe you shouldn't be able to see other groups member lists - but I'm not sure how that works elsewhere in Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Weekly Monthly, what's weekly?
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way to get around this behavior? Let's assume the following example: In Moodle the week starts Monday. The start date of the Questinonair is a Tuesday, a student answeres on Wednesday, and the questionnair can be answered weekly (Questionnair 2.4). If I understood the previous entries correctly, the student is able to answer next Wednesday one minute after s/he did last week, not Monday one minute after midnight and not Tuesday one minute after the start date, isn't it? We run the questionnair every week to asses the weekly progress, and we would like that the Q. can be answered once between Mo-Su every week. It get's complicated to tell the students to always answer it exactly on Sunday. The only way around is to allow any number of answers and hope the students only answer once, or does weekly mean once between Mo-Su respectively between the start date + 7 days? Thanks, Kurt

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Weekly Monthly, what's weekly?
ResponsesInList.Text: "Once a week" means once every 7 days . For example, if a student answers a questionnaire on Wednesday, August 4th at 9am, they cannot answer it again before Wednesday, August 11th at 9am. However, nothing forces them to answer the questionnaire again after that 7-day interval. This has nothing to do with what you call a "Moodle week". In the (to be released) version 2.5 of Questionnaire there is a useful feature of "show non-respondents" which allows teachers (or admins) to send an email reminder to students who have not yet responded to a questionnaire. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bug when adding new option to select or radio questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, This is not a bug , but the only way Questionnaire can deal with your answers editing. I would certainly strongly discourage editing questions once users have started to answer. Anyway, the response analysis goes by choice positions , i.e. if a user selected "Blue" (position 3 ) in the original version of your questionnaire, and you edit to replace choice "Blue" with "Yellow" in the same position 3, then of course that user's response does not change (it's still position 3 ) but it now displays the new "color" you have painted over Blue, i.e. Yellow. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire for Moodle 2.4 is available
ResponsesInList.Text: Questionnaire for Moodle 2.4 is available from the Moodle plugins Directory here . It contains a number of bug fixes and improvements over the previous version for Moodle 2.3. Please note that from now on, in accordance with the current Moodle "languages policy", all translations have been moved from the questionnaire/lang folder to AMOS . If the questionnaire strings have been translated in your own language, simply updating your installed Language packs in Site administration ► Language ► Language packs will install/update those translations. At the moment, the Questionnaire language strings have been translated - more or less completely - into those languages: German (de), Spanish (es), French (fr), Italian (it), Dutch (nl), Polish (pl), Portuguese (pt), Portuguese Brazil (pt_br) and Serbian (sr_lt). If you can complete the translations, please ask your Moodle language maintainer how to proceed. Also if you want to submit missing languages. Questionnaire for Moodle 2.5 will bring lots of new features, which currently need to be tested. They will shortly be made available on our github and hopefully in the official plugins directory later this year. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: questionnaire-template bug
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the detailed info. There is a very easy fix for that bug, use textlib function. In Moodle 2.4.2, file questionnaire.class.php line 970, replace `$survey->name = substr($survey->name, 0, (64-10));` with `$survey->name = textlib::substr($survey->name, 0, (64-10));` I have opened issue CONTRIB-4398 in the tracker. Thanks for reporting this bug. Please try out my fix and confirm that it works for you. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Odp: Re: Questionnaire and Fushion Charts Free
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gang, No, I wasn't subscribed to this forum. I don't have time for a complete guide, so here are some minimal instructions to get you started with all the things you need. You can also contact me for support services. Attached is the zip of the fusion charts I am using. Put this folder under your moodle/lib folder. (Oops zip is too large for this forum, you can download the zip here ) To use the charts, you will need to create the files to display the data. I created a folder in moodle root called results. In that folder, I have: 1. a file to display the results--this is created like any typical moodle view or index type page and is what I linked to from my menu. This file requires a HEAD to call the fusion charts js like this: <HEAD> <link rel="stylesheet" href="chart. css " type="text/css" /> <script type="text/ javascript " src="<?php echo $CFG-> wwwroot ;?>/lib/charts/charts/FusionCharts.js"></script> </HEAD> this page also has to include the code to render the chart like this: $strDataURL = "data.php"; echo renderChart("$CFG->wwwroot/lib/charts/charts/FCF_Column3D.swf", $strDataURL, "", "1", 700, 300, false, false); You will see I also have a css file in the folder with some colors, etc. for the display page in case you want to add images, etc. 2. a lib file, again just like a typical moodle lib file, this file has functions to gather the data from the questionnaire db tables. Since this is written for a specific questionnaire in a course, I start by getting the questionnaire by name like this: $ors1 = get_record('questionnaire', array('name' => 'Well-Being Assessment')); , then do a typical sql return for the data. You can gather the data in several ways, depending on what you want. In the above example, I gathered the data from one questionnaire, split into the different ranking questions, ( the questionnaire_response_rank table). 3. a file to render the chart (the file called data.php referenced above). This file needs these includes: include($CFG-> dirroot .'/lib/charts/includes/FusionCharts_Gen.php'); require_once('lib.php'); require_once("../config.php"); Then I created variables to call the lib functions I have to get the data, e.g. like this: $total1 = results_get_eh(); -- this is a function that gets one of the ranking scales I have in my questionnaire (e.g. one of the bars in the chart). Then, I used xml to display the chart like this: $strXML = ""; $strXML .= "<graph caption='' xAxisName='Life Areas' yAxisName='Average Score' decimalPrecision='2' yaxisminvalue='0' yaxismaxvalue='5' formatNumberScale='0'>"; $strXML .= "<set name='Spiritual' value='" . $total2 . "' color='9A1631' />"; $strXML .= "<set name='Emotional' value='" . $total1 . "' color='F6BD0F' />"; $strXML .= "<set name='Social' value='" . $total4 . "' color='003366' />"; $strXML .= "<set name='Intellectual' value='" . $total5 . "' color='E22520' />"; $strXML .= "<set name='Physical' value='" . $total6 . "' color='8BBA00' />"; $strXML .= "<set name='Occupational' value='" . $total3 . "' color='6D6EAF' />"; $strXML .= "<trendlines>"; $strXML .= "<line startvalue='0' endValue='0.8' displayValue='Weak ' color='89B812' alpha='30' isTrendZone='1'/>"; $strXML .= "<line startvalue='0.8' endValue='2.4' displayValue='Vulnerable ' color='89B812' alpha='40' isTrendZone='1'/>"; $strXML .= "<line startvalue='2.4' endValue='3.8' displayValue='Competent ' color='89B812' alpha='60' isTrendZone='1'/>"; $strXML .= "<line startvalue='3.8' endValue='5.0' displayValue='Strong ' color='89B812' alpha='80' isTrendZone='1'/>"; $strXML .= "</trendlines>"; $strXML .= "</graph>"; header('Content-type: text/xml'); echo $strXML; There are many different ways you can display the chart, you can refer to the fusion charts documentation for more info. Have fun. I have used the charts in other fun ways, e.g. I have a block with a form in it with some choices, in the footer of the block is a link to display the results in a chart that shows a trendline with the dates.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: upgrade from 2.3-> 2.4
ResponsesInList.Text: Glen "... so we removed the 2.3 questionnaire module code and ran the moodle upgrade without it - so the questionnaire module tables remained in the database... " Sounds like you did not follow the recommended procedure to remove the Questionnaire plugin from your Moodle site. You should never simply "remove" a plugin's folder from your moodle files. The normal procedure is as follows: 1.- Go to Site administration ► Plugins ► Activity modules ► Manage activities 2.- Locate the plugin you want to remove (in this case, Questionnaire) and click the Delete link. This will remove all traces of the plugin from your moodle database. 3.- After confirmation that you want to delete, you will see this message: Activities questionnaire Success 4.- Only then you can delete the Questionnaire directory from your Moodle site's files! OK, this what you should do now: 1.- Using phpMyAdmin (or similar tool) go to your Moodle site database and remove all questionnaire tables . 2.- Go to the mdl_modules table, locate and delete the questionnaire row. 3.- Re-install a fresh version of Questionnaire 2.4. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrade from 2.2 to 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Justin, Here at the OU we usually upgrade the plug-ins and core code simultaneously at least on our live system. There's often a period of time on our development and test systems when the core code has moved up a version and the plug-ins have not been updated to match.  This is the sort of situation your campus is in with the questionnaire module, if I understand you correctly.  It isn't dreadful for the stability of the whole system but there are probably a few bugs in your questionnaires that might make them unusable. ResponsesInList.Title: New 'Targets' question-type for Questionnaire module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, but especially Joseph & Mike, Today I've completed extensive work and testing of a new 'Targets' question-type for the Questionnaire module which is specially intended of Personal progress reviews, although it may have much wider uses. Many schools and colleges operate progress reviews in some form but as far as I can tell there is no module in Moodle that facilitates the workflow implications of this, without resorting to copy & paste, if the review is conducted for and by the student under the guidance of a tutor. Specifically this implies that target statements (answers) submitted in one response become targets to be assessed (questions) in the next. This cyclical flow of target setting - target addressing is exactly the point of suppying the Target question-type. Today I have opened a new tracker issue at CONTRIB-4260 which contains a patch file for making these changes to the Questionnaire module. The patch file contains language edits in the file lang/en/questionnaire.php which would need translation for the patch to work in any other environment including en_us. I am also attaching an edited version of the documentation I've produced for this as a pdf, so that its possible for all to understand what is involved and what the Target question delivers. But as this is a large file it is available at CONTRIB-4260 rather than here. This question-type is switchable in a new Questionnaire Settings panel, and along with it is the option of permitting one other question, the Checkbox, to roll responses forward in a manner that would be intuitive to students. Only the Target type will roll forward answers into questions, but the Checkbox can be set (per question) to let answers roll from one response to another. The key image from the pdf is largely self-explanatory, except to emphasize that targets that are not met are automatcially rolled forward into the next round and added into the New targets without the need for copy & paste. I would greatly appreciate whatever comments you care to make about this development. Let me close by saying that I am ever-grateful for the work done on the Questionnaire module by its writers and maintainers; I appreciate too the support Ravensbourne, London has given to this new development. Regards, John

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: White screen in questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: For future ref, this is the issue we had: It was an issue with Moodle and PHP Caching on the server . It seemed that in particular that one page of the Questionnaire module (view.php) when cached for a particular period of time was then not displaying the full page but only part of it. So for example, when we looked at the page early morning UK time, refreshed cache, then this worked ok when testing from anywhere. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem downloading data.
ResponsesInList.Text: @Ian, From your later posts it looks like you are having a timeout on your server. Unfortunately on shared servers you cannot change the timeout limits set by our host . That is the limit of cheaper, shared servers. On the other hand, the fact that you cannot download that particular "42 radio buttons" questionnaire responses whilst you can download responses to other questionnaires with 40 questions on your site is strange. There is certainly no limit to the number of questions you can have in a questionnaire but the more questions there are - and the more respondents - does strain your server's database queries. I am only guessing here, but it might be that one of your questions contains (somewhere in its text or in the "possible answers") some coded character or a sequence which your server does not like. In order to experiment with that questionnaire and its responses, you could EXPORT it (backup course with only the questionnaire and students) and IMPORT it (restore) either to a special "test course" on your moodle site or on a local moodle site, and see if you are still getting the problem, and then experiment with deleting some responses or/and some questions, until the timeout error disappears. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to limit Report of Public Questionnaire to only current course?
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, I found how to do that. I edited the following file: mod/questionnaire/locallib.php After line 1991 I added the bolded 2 new lines (just before $total = count($responses); ): global $SESSION, $DB; $responses=$DB->get_records_ sql ("SELECT moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.id, moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.survey_id, moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.submitted, moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.username FROM moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response JOIN moodle.mdl_questionnaire_attempts ON moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.id=moodle.mdl_questionnaire_attempts.rid WHERE moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.complete = 'y' AND moodle.mdl_questionnaire_attempts.qid=".$SESSION->questionnaire->id." ORDER BY moodle.mdl_questionnaire_response.id"); On line 2238(old)/2241(new) I added the bolded script so the line looks like: FROM {questionnaire_response} R JOIN {questionnaire_attempts} Z ON R.id=Z.rid On line 2240(old)/2243(new) I added: R.complete='y' AND Z.qid='{$SESSION->questionnaire->id}' So, now the summary reports of Public Questionnaires show only participants of the course where the Questionnaire is located and not all the participants of the Public Survery. I also made students to see summary results of the Questionnaires... but that is another story.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating multiple questionnaires using template
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lauren, Your problem arises from a minor bug that happens when a new questionnaire is made by copying an existing questionnaire (of any type: private, public or template). The original questionnaire does not, as you say, "duplicate itself", but unfortunately the copy you made from the original does not automatically take its new Title from its Name; rather it keeps its original title, hence the confusion. Here is how to proceed to avoid the confusion. Create questionnaire T01 Advanced settings, set Questionnaire Type as Template create your questions Create questionnaire Q01 Content options / Copy existing: T01 Advanced settings, Content options: Title: change from T01 to Q01 (i.e. match Questionnaire Title with Questionnaire Name. edit questions etc. Create questionnaire Q02 Now in Content options / Copy existing you see : T01 (your original template questionnaire) Q01 (the questionnaire you copied from T01) Hope this is clear. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Skip logic feature available for testing
ResponsesInList.Text: To all Questionnaire users. The skip logic feature has been asked as a desirable feature for the Questionnaire plugin, e.g. here . I have spent a couple of days of my Xmas holidays to implement a proposal which is available for testing and comment, on my Moodle test site . Login as teacher1 , password Teacher1! , go to the Questionnaire Module Demo course where you can take the questionnaire entitled Testing the Skip Logic setting . For a more complete understanding of how the feature works, you can create your own questionnaire from scratch (or make a copy of the Testing the Skip Logic setting questionnaire instance) and add your own questions. Please read carefully the online help provided for the Yes/No, Dropdown Box and Radio buttons question types, under the Skip Logic help button. Please report here any remarks, questions, which may help improve this feature, before I commit it, after approval of my co-maintainer, Mike Churchward. Joseph An extract from the online Help file follows Respondents can be routed through a questionnaire using 2 types of branching logic: 1. Skipping specific questions A skip pattern will jump a respondent over a group of questions that isn't relevant to them. Use a Yes/No question for this. Example 1 Page 1 Question 1 Do you own a car? Yes/No. Answer Yes -> go to page 2 Answer No -> go to page 3 (i.e. skip over irrelevant question(s) in page 2 Page 2 Question 2: What is the color of your car? Question 3: What is the make of your car? Question 4: How long have you owned your car? Page 3 Question 5: Where do you work? etc. Procedure to be followed to obtain the above "skip logic" flow Create Q1 as a Yes/No question, and set Skip Logic to "Yes" and set Response Required to Yes , of course! Insert a Page Break --- Create Q2 as a radio button or text or dropdown question type Create Q3 Create Q4 (you can create as many questions as you like on that page) Insert a Page Break--- Now continue creating questions normally, until you want to use Skip Logic again. 2. Conditional branching : A branch pattern will route a respondent to the appropriate section of the questionnaire: each respondent follows one of the branches. Use a Radio Button or Dropdown Box question for this. Example 2 Page 1 Question 1: Where do you teach? Primary school / Secondary education sector / University . Answer: Primary school -> go to page 2 Answer: Secondary education sector -> go to page 3 Answer: University -> go to page 4 Page 2 Question 2: How long have you been a Primary school teacher? Question 3: What age groups to you teach? [go to page 5] Page 3 Question 4: How long have you been a Secondary school teacher? Question 5: What it your main subject [go to page 5] Page 4 Question 6: How long have you been a University professor? Question 7: What is your domain of research? [go to page 5] Page 5 Question 8: Tell us what you think of Moodle in your everyday teaching routine... etc. etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Bug preventing numeric values from being saved...
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi In moodle/mod/questionnaire/questiontypes/questiontypes.class.php there is a bug that results in numeric responses not being saved in the database .  The bug is on line 238: 
```text
            $val = preg_replace("[/^0-9.\-]*(-?[0-9]*\.?[0-9]*).*/", '\1', $val);
```
 which should be: 
```text
            $val = preg_replace("/[^0-9.\-]*(-?[0-9]*\.?[0-9]*).*/", '\1', $val);
```
 That is, the first two characters of the regex have been transposed.  I don't think this has been fixed yet, but, if it has, apologies for the noise. Thanks. Later... Greg Oster

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question numbers not appearing when taking the questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Claudette, I expect you are using the Chrome browser. If not, please specify your browser (and its version). I have just conducted some tests on my moodle local test site, and it appears that this lack of question numbers bug only appears on Chrome. It seems linked to bug report CONTRIB-3193 : Legend tag does not wrap question text in questionnaire module. ResponsesInList.Title: Average Rank Precision
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I am facing a small problem. As I have shown in the screen shot I am getting the average score of each item (i.e 2.2 , 2.3 etc). Can anyone guide me on how I could increase the number of decimal places in the average score..(Ex. 2.2xx). Thank You

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Average Rank Precision
ResponsesInList.Text: Which version of Moodle and Questionnaire are you using?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Average Rank Precision
ResponsesInList.Text: I am using Moodle V -1.9.14.1 and Questionnaire - Version 2005021101 I got these from the readme.txt file. Thank You

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Average Rank Precision
ResponsesInList.Text: In file <yourmoodle>mod/questionnaire/questiontypes/questiontypes.class.php, inside function mkresavg(), locate the following two sprintf() functions: line 1994: `$table->data[] = array(format_text($content, FORMAT_HTML), $out, sprintf('%.1f', $avg));` line 2001: `$avg = sprintf('%.1f', $avg);` and change the %.1 to any value you want for the number of decimals you need, e.g. `sprintf('%.2f', $avg)` will give you 2 decimals, etc. Joseph PS.- See attached screenshot showing you where to find the version of your installed modules.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Average Rank Precision
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks a lot. This is what I was looking for. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How anonymous is anonymous
ResponsesInList.Text: My experience is that using logs or the database , you can figure out who submitted each questionnaire but it takes work and the logs go on and on.  Submissions are listed in the order they are submitted, so the first questionnaire in your results is the first person to submit. My question would be this:  If you tell them the questionnaire is anonymous and then go behind their backs and figure out who said what, you've broken trust.  Do you really want that? If you want demographic information and have institution/department filled in for your students in their profiles, when you download the results to a text file, it leaves the name off but includes group assignments (if you use them) some of their information...for example, I work in corrections, so I have parole officers, corrections officers, clerical staff, counselors, etc...each of them are assigned to a specific unit.  I can see which unit of which facility answered without knowing which person.  That gives me some general demographics without (facility A thought topic A was helpful/useful but facility B really didn't...or the officers in all facilities appreciated content B but the counselors thought it was too basic, which good for needs assessment type stuff). If you want to know who responded and how, don't make it anonymous.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Users can view guests' questionnaire submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, "Normally", Questionnaires are expected to be completed by students enrolled in a Moodle course. If a questionnaire is completed by a guest, then the attempt is saved as "guest attempt' and of course any further "guest" will be able to see that attempt. Please note also, that if 2 (or more) people are logged in at the very same time as guests on your moodle site and complete a questionnaire open to guests at the same time, then their responses will be mixed up. The same holds true for Quizzes. Moodle activities in general are not suited for guests/anonymous visitors, but for students regularly enrolled into "courses". That is especially true of activities which need to save data entered by students to the moodle database . Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire Modlule in Moodle 2 - Change Theme
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Carlos, There are several reasons. And maybe my Questionnaire co-maintainer Mike will add a few more. Some parts of the Questionnaire's themes seemed to conflict with the general Moodle theme's CSS rules. In Moodle 2, the themes have been completely re-written, and it was too complicated for the Questionnaire's own themes to keep up with all those changes. Although blocks and plugins may have their own CSS stylesheets, I don't think any 3rd-party plugins have full-blown themes of their own, at least not in Moodle 2. Please note that Questionnaire for Moodle 2 does have its own styles.css stylesheet, which you can customize on your moodle site as you like - if you have admin rights, of course. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: questionnaire export problem with long answer text
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the last file, Rob. I can spot the problem and will file a bug report with a fix any time soon. However, for longish choice texts, I would really advise using the "hidden" option, for exporting - in responses - shorter label s instead of the longer text values. This is explained (but needs improvement) in the Questionnaire documentation wiki. Here is what I would suggest for your question #8: Q.- What are you most likely to do when you see someone being bullied? Possible answers (choices): report=Report it to a teacher or staff member ask to stop=Ask the bully or bullies to stop Join in Nothing step in for friend=Step in if it’s a friend, don’t get involved if I don’t know the person(s) being bullied The full text of choices will still be displayed to the students taking the questionnaire, but the exported responses file will display the shortened form, much easier to read in your spreadsheet anyway. Q01->report    Q01->ask to stop    Q01->Join in    Q01->Nothing    Q01->step in for friend Oh, and you can actually edit your questions and introduce the shortened choice texts even after students have answered the questionnaire. It does not change anything to their answers. Hope that helps, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error writing to database
ResponsesInList.Text:
We also had this problem; it seems to be an issue with the 'value' field in questionnaire_quest_choice: the XML schema specifies that this field can be null, but our database (which has been upgraded over time) had this field set to NOT NULL.  When creating new entries in this table the 'value' is not specified in questions.php (approx. line 390 in our copy of this file), so this was causing a write failure. Joseph, I guess this is something that needs changing in db/upgrade.php?  I don't know how many people it will affect, though. Austin, the way I fixed this was to run the following command within MySQL: 
```text
alter table mdl_questionnaire_quest_choice modify value text null;
```
 If you are not running MySQL or your database prefix is not 'mdl' then you'll need to alter this, but allowing null values should fix it. Hope this is helpful. Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ERROR: SMTP Error: Data not accepted.
ResponsesInList.Text: I had the same problem, and your tip helped me resolve it, but it was a little more complicated. First I changed the "noreply" to a valid address. Still no mail sent. Then after some more digging, I found that my php.ini file did not specify a default sender address. I edited the php.ini file and added a default sendmail_from = info@ligminchalearning.com Now when I run the cron the mail goes out. I dug around in some PHP forums and probably found out why this effects some modules, like the forums, and not others. A module in Moodle can define that it pulls sender information from the system settings, or not. If it doesn't specify to use the Moodle system settings, it defaults to what the default settings are in the php.ini file. But if there is nothing specified in the php.ini file (my case on a hosted installation setup by simple scripts) then the mail from address is the domain name, which is rejected by the sendmail process. So the problem is caused by some sloppy coding in some modules, duh... So if others are struggling with this problem, set the noreply value to a valid address, AND make sure your php.ini file has an entry for sendmail_from = <insert real email address on your site> This line is used by both Windows and Linux PHP installations. John Jackson

From the error messages you quote it is obvious that you installed the questionnaire module in the wrong place to start with. Those messages tell you that moodle is now looking for moodle/mod/css/version.php; moodle/mod/css/images.php; moodle/mod//images/questiontypes.php files which of course do not exist there and should never have been there. You probably unzipped the questionnaire files to the wrong place in the first place. What can you do now? Logged in as admin, go to Modules/Manage Activities . If the Questionnaire module still shows up there, click on the Delete link. Check the contents of your moodle/mod/ folder for any unwanted files there. If this does not work, you may have to look into your Moodle database , using phpMyAdmin . In the mdl_modules table, if Questionnaire is still there, delete it. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copy a questionnaire between courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there. When you save it, save it as a template, and then it will be available in the other courses and you can slightly modify it.

Nor can I find an export or import tab.  I am grateful for any assistance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copy a questionnaire between courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sally. Yes I am still here The instructions referring to templates and import were for if you use items within the same Moodle. To do what you want you will have to (first ensure the second Moodle has the questionnaire module - it is not standard) and then in your course admin settings click "backup" Only tick the questionnaire to back up and then click next to create a zipped copy of this course (which will just have the questionnaire in it) Then you download it to your computer. Go to the Moodle where you want it and to the course where you want it and click "restore" You will be prompted to upload the zipped folder you downloaded from the other site - follow the instructions to upload and unzip/restore into your second Moodle. As for the "template" option, that is in the "advanced settings" option once you save and display the questionnaire.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated Email to Student
ResponsesInList.Text: @ Ian You could place that enrolment key in the Confirmation page that is displayed to the student upon completing the questionnaire. Editing Questionnaire Settings > Advanced settings > Submission options > Confirmation page > Body text You should of course make it clear to the student that a) they'll have to copy that registration key and remember it in order to go to the next section and b) that they will have no other means to retrieve that key. Please note that you may have to tinker with the duration of the display of that Confirmation page. If you need help, please ask. Another possibility is to re-direct to a "special" page on the web (inside of or outside of your Moodle course/site) containing all the necessary instructions & key. In that case, use Editing Questionnaire Settings > Advanced settings > Submission options > Confirmation URL . At the moment what you wish - send an automatic email message upon questionnaire completion is not available. Sorry, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: why does questionnaire show up in gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't think a scale will work as you want it. The questionnaire simply records the numeric value stored in the grade setting for itself when a user submits it. There no partial grading. For example, if you assign 100 to the submission grade setting, then anyone who submits a questionnaire will receive 100. If you assign 10, they will receive 10. If you assign a scale, it will store the negative id number of the scale (for example, the "separated and connected ways of knowing" is identified as -1). Then, if the user submits the questionnaire, they will receive a grade of -1. I suppose this could be modified to store the index number of the last scale item, but I'm not sure this would have value. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: why does questionnaire show up in gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear all, I find a dirty solution to stop posting the questionnaire result on gradebook. First, you have to hack on the code in the "lib.php" file to disable the "questionnaire_update_grades" function as below: function questionnaire_update_grades($questionnaire=null, $userid=0, $nullifnone=true) { return NULL; } You can simply rename the original function as "function questionnaire_update_grades_original": function questionnaire_update_grades_original($questionnaire=null, $userid=0, $nullifnone=true) { global $CFG; if (!function_exists('grade_update')) { //workaround for buggy PHP versions require_once($CFG->libdir.'/gradelib.php'); } ... Second, if you have already created some records on the gradebook, then you have to remove them by issuing SQL commands: DELETE FROM mdl_grade_items where id = xxx; DELETE FROM mdl_grade_grades where itemid = xxx; where xxx is the id you can get from the SQL from your course: SELECT * FROM mdl_grade_items WHERE itemmodule = "questionnaire" ORDER BY courseid; Please remember to do a backup before proceeding. It works for my case. Good luck. Regards, Murphy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: why does questionnaire show up in gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christian - Plugins is a term used in Moodle for any Moodle add-on that can be easily dropped into Moodle. They are managed as self-contained packages, and follow a strictly defined structure and API so that Moodle can manage them easily. All modules, blocks, enrolment plug-ins, authentication plug-ins, filters, etc., are plug-ins. This includes the ones that come standard with Moodle and are maintained by Moodle. Questionnaire is a module, and as such is a module plug-in. It is third party because it is not maintained directly by the Moodle core developers. Hope this helps explain things. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using Questionnaire as a self-assessment tool
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kerry, I would add a new database to my course and then create all of the appropriate fields that I want to use for the self assessment. You could use a yes/no format or you could use some kind of likert scale format to have them assess on a scale that could show improvement over time. I believe that there are two ways to look at subsequent assessments. One way is to just have each participant edit their original entry with a thought of printing the first entry so you can measure progress. The second way is to just have the participants do the assessment again (my preference). Now you have a record with a date of each assessment. When you create the template for the list view of the results, you can configure it in such a way that the participant will see all of their attempts in a table sorted by date, which will easily show progress and growth. You also have the option of turning on comments so the instructor could comment on progress etc... This kind of self assessment using the Database module works really well. You can find an example of this referenced in this post, http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=118496&parent=760485 . The sample database and data are still live. Now copy the link address (right click, "copy link") of that questionnaire. From the homepage, go to "Modules" - > "Blocks" -> "Sticky Blocks".  In this sticky block, put some text, like "Please complete the end of the year survey" and link it to the survey using the link you just copied.  Now every course will have a direct link to the survey. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk add questionaires
ResponsesInList.Text: That is a good idea on linking to the questionnaire in the sticky block. But since all the courses need to take the questionnaire, instead of creating a metacourse and having to add all the courses to it: Create a blank course. In the course settings, set the course to be available to students AND to allow guest access. This way all students can enter the course without having to be enrolled in the blank course. Create questionnaire in blank course. As mentioned above, in the questionnaire, make the first question a "Course" field where the student will enter their course number/ID or whatever identifier you use. As mentioned above, in the site admin block > Modules > Blocks > Sticky Blocks > Select Course Page and add an HTML block. In the HTML block, put some like "Please complete the end of the year survey" and you can hyperlink that text. This sticky block will then appear in every course in your Moodle instance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: UTF-8
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry for the delay. You will have to convert the data in the tables as well as changing the collation of the tables. There is information here to do that: http://en.gentoo-wiki.com/wiki/Convert_latin1_to_UTF-8_in_MySQL . You will only need to do the conversion if you were storing old non-UTF8 data in the tables. If you have been only storing UTF8 data in non UTF8 tables, then chaning the collation of them will be all you need to do. Note - make backups of your data before attempting any of this! You may want to check the settings for the default collations for your database. Most add-ons don't specify a collation, so it depends on this setting when the tables are created. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to copy a Questionnaire that is on the Front Page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Frankie - if you go back into the questionnaire and click the Advanced tab yo can either save it as a template - and then when you go to another course you can select that template instead of making a new questionnaire, and then edit the questions - or else you can save it as public which means you can select it in another course but you cannot edit the questions and any responses go back to the original questionnaire location.(It doesn' mean public as in the general public can answer it. It is possible to have a questionnaire on the front page for non-logged in users, ie the "public", but to do that you have to override permissions to allow guests to view and complete the questionnaire - which is what you'd have to do if you wanted outsiders to your Moodle to see your questionnaire, like you posted in the Lounge !)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire and Moodle 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: See Roadmap . Basically, there are issues with the design and code of both feedback and questionnaire. Then there is the core survey module that is very rarely used. The plan is to replace all three of these with one new module in Moodle 2.1 (with, I think, automatic upgrade from all three.) feedback was added to Moodle core, before the design problems were identified. Since it is now going to be replaced with something else, it was disabled in 2.0, but left in the codebase. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire and Moodle 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Stephen - Just to be clear, there were various changes to the coding style and various APIs with Moodle 2.0 that requires all CONTRIB modules to be updated to work in 2.0. I have created CONTRIB-1988 to monitor the major ones that folks seem to use most. Hopefully Joseph and others will be able to get these readied reasonably quickly. In terms of upgrading your site to 2.0, without the code in /mod/questionnaire the upgrade should work fine and simply ignore your existing questionnaire data. If you are actively using questionnaire, then you likely will want to hold off upgrading to 2.0 until the updated questionnaire is ready. The hope is that by Moodle 2.1 there will be the new activity module that combines feedback and questionnaire with plans to import existing data from both of those into the new activity module although I have no idea when that may actually take place. The goal is to provide the best of both questionnaire and feedback modules. Do not hesitate to let me know if there are any questions and please feel free to watch, vote for, and/or comment on CONTRIB-2004 which is for the updated 2.0 version of the questionnaire activity module. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire Weekly Response - answers not appending week to week
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 1.9.8 Our use case: We want to survey our students at the end of each training week for their endurance times on physical exercises.  We believe the Questionnaire (used as a survey without grades and numerical answers for input of endurance times) is the best answer for this.  We use weekly topics format and we want to present a Questionnaire survey to the student at the end of every week's topic for students to enter endurance times. Our problem: When we create the Questionnaire survey for week one, we make it private (we only use one course), define two numerical questions, no grading, response type weekly, student can view all responses.  This works great.  The problem comes when we add a second Questionnaire for week two:  we type in the exact same title and description and choose the copy existing option for the first week Questionnaire.  It looks the same week to week but when we test it in the second week we only see week two answers and not week one answers. If we choose weekly response does Moodle really enforce students to wait 7 calendar days before accepting the results?  We don't think so, because in our testing (on the same day), we can input and see results for week 2 but week 1 is missing.  It seems like Moodle sees these Week 1 -Week 2 Questionnaires as different activities and not appending data. Can anyone chip in here with advice to get submitted results to append using Questionnaires? Is there a better way to accomplish progress (endurance times or grade progressions) tracking in Moodle? Thanks in advance, Eric

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire Weekly Response - answers not appending week to week
ResponsesInList.Text: 1.- The problem comes when we add a second Questionnaire for week two:  we type in the exact same title and description and choose the copy existing option for the first week Questionnaire.  It looks the same week to week but when we test it in the second week we only see week two answers and not week one answers. Of course. The second questionnaire you create (in week 2 topic) is a new questionnaire, totally unrelated to the first questionnaire you created in week 1. If you want responses to be "appended", you must create one questionnaire only , and set it to be answered weekly. Maybe place it in the Topic 0 section. 2.- If we choose weekly response does Moodle really enforce students to wait 7 calendar days before accepting the results? Yes, it does. If you try to answer such a questionnaire  on the same week, a warning is issued. You have already filled out this questionnaire for us this week. Thank you. Please have all your settings right and give it a try, it should work as expected. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire Weekly Response - answers not appending week to week

What are best practices for 'coaxing' students who progress through a course in a linear [top down] fashion to backtrack in the course back up to the 0 section to update their results?  Do most admins create a link resource?  Sorry if this seems like a remedial question, I am just trying to use the software per design spec and original use case and not reinvent anything. Eric

However this is done, we will provide a way to migrate your existing surveys into the final. Post you responses in this discussion. mike

Perhaps the least favorite part of feedback for me is the very front end for students. Answering a feedback should mean being taken to that feedback immediately, without another screen in between. Multiple paged feedbacks would also be nice to have. I also would like a way to go from the overview of feedback results back to the individual feedbacks. For example, if I have a textbox answer question, and I am reviewing all the answers to that feedback on one page, sometimes I see one particular answer a student gave that I want to know which student gave it. The emails that feedback sends to me when a student completes a feedback aren't too helpful because all they tell me is the student completed it. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire and Feedback Modules - Opinions
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, here is the story. A long time ago (almost three years!!!) we had to decide on one of these, and after some discussion ( this one !) the consensus at that time was clesrly for Feedback to be standard (note that carrying both modules in core is simply not an option). Feedback had enough features and an interface people liked plus cleaner, more Moodley code that programmers liked (to ensure people built more in future). Questionnaire was a bit of a Frankenstein module at the time with an awkward interface borne of it being built around PhpESP. So finally Feedback got into core over a year ago (where it is now) awaiting the next release. It's working fine there, just needing a few tweaks to polish it up (in my opinion). Everyone knew this was now a core module, and there is a 1.9 version that can be used now, with no fear of losing data in an upgrade to 2.0 later. Meanwhile, development continued heavily on Questionnaire. (This makes me a little sad because I would love to have seen that effort going into the one we'd chosen here instead). Questionnaire is now a lot more Moodley and usable. However, I just had a quick skim and still see some problems, such as non-strict XHTML (hard-coded styles, tables for layout), all the questiontypes being crammed into one file instead of being pluggable, no inline documentation etc. So it's not perfect, and needs quite a bit work to review it properly and polish it up for 2.0. If we switched to Questionnaire now it would - upset a lot of people who had counted on Feedback being standard - be quite a lot of extra work, with more cost and more delays to 2.0 I would do it if there was an OVERWHELMING vote to do this, but otherwise it just doesn't seem to be fair. I would much rather see a clear analysis/specification of the bugs and missing features from Feedback so we can direct some effort into improving that module.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire and Feedback Modules - Opinions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Martin - Out of respect to the people who put a lot of effort into what questionnaire has become, I would like to correct a few of your points. To begin with, I respect the decision that was made to include Feedback into core. A decision had to be made, and at the time, the noise that was coming from the community seemed to tip the scale toward Feedback. The reality of questionnaire is that the entire module had been rewritten to make the interface what the people wanted before Feedback was announced as a core module. It was released into contrib almost the same week as the announcement. Communication was just not what it should have been to give Moodle the information they needed to know that. Now to specifics: non-strict XHTML (hard-coded styles, tables for layout) I do not believe this is the case. Joseph dedicated a lot of time over the last years to resolve these. There are no hard-coded styles that I'm aware of (there are some unused constants that have been removed just recently). There are some tables in some of the question formats, as there are in Feedback. all the questiontypes being crammed into one file instead of being pluggable Somewhat true. Making them pluggable was being held off while it was determined if the question library could somehow be used instead. Feedback does have somewhat pluggable questions, but does not use the question library either. no inline documentation Not true at all. There is a ton of inline documentation. One of Joseph's biggest efforts was in this area. And it has translations into many language packs. and needs quite a bit work to review it properly and polish it up for 2.0 Not sure about this either. A version already exists in 2.0 and is being constantly updated with the changes to 2.0. Questionnaire has a very large install base, and will continue to be maintained and improved. At some point down the road, when Feedback satisfies all Questionnaire users, it might be possible to create a migration path from one to the other, allowing the two projects to fuse. Mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire and Feedback Modules - Opinions
ResponsesInList.Text: (taken from MDL-14493 ): IMO , the best path for Moodle core is a module called "Survey", that is whatever the best features of Questionnaire and Feedback are in one stable module. The current 'Survey" module would then simply be a standard pre-configured version of this delivered with Moodle. And, this path would require an automatic transition from the module being used to the new one (that is questionnaire => survey / feedback => survey / survey => survey).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire and Feedback Modules - Opinions
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Mike's last two posts. It has long been obvious to me that there should only be one such module in Moodle, correctly called "Survey". The current "Survey" module is not very useful, but as Mike suggests, could always be shipped with Moodle as an "example". The names "Questionnaire" and "Feedback" are misleading (especially the latter). And the other existing module, "Choice" has very limited features, but could live on in Moodle. On principle I also agree that the new "Survey" module should include all (or most) of the currently available features of Questionnaire and Feedback. Ideally it would also include one feature currently not available in either module, namely Conditional Branching (as per LimeSurvey and other such well-known survey software). Daniele has provided a little wish-list of features (in contrib MDL-14493 ) which would need to be prioritized. Those interested may also look at my comprehensive (at the time, summer 2008) side-by-side comparison of the Questionnaire and Feedback features here . However... I do not see the practicality of such a venture at the moment. As it stands now, Feedback is not very different from what it was a year ago. If the plan is to continue to abide with the decision taken about a year ago to have Feedback in Moodle core (from 2.0), there is a lot of work to be done on Feedback (not just a couple of days' work...). This would mean Moodle HQ devoting some programmer time to help Andreas with the job, but it's not for me to say. Whatever further decision is taken, in order to promote the use of the new "Survey" module, and whatever distance separates this new module from the existing Feedback and Questionnaire modules, efforts should be made to ensure data transfer from those modules to the new one, by providing some export/import tools (as described by Mike). Joseph PS.- Should this discussion continue in this thread? or maybe we should start a new thread? How to get people posting to the Feedback forum informed of the discussion? Or should all discussion take place in the Tracker?

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there, I forgot to turn on grading for a Questionnaire until over 30 students had already responded. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Glenys, When you create a questionnaire instance, the default grading is turned on (Submission grade = 100). I'm surprised that you say you "forgot to turn it on". Rather, you must have turned it OFF. Anyway, here we go for your regrading. There is no "regrading" feature in questionnaire so you'll have to to it by and, in the Gradebook. Fortunately, for just 30 students that should not take too long. Situation I have created a questionnaire instance e.g. [Questionnaire 003] with No grading. Three students have responded ( they have been graded 0.00 ). Then I changed [Questionnaire 003] to be graded 10. Since I turned [Questionnaire 003] grading to 10, two students have responded and have therefore been graded 10 . Action Go to your gradebook: Grades ► View ► Grader report Click the Turn editing on button in the top right corner. If you do not see the Edit grade boxes, you may have to change your options in Grades ► My preferences ► Grader report: General Advanced element Quick Grading Yes While you are there, you might wish tochange the Students per page to a larger number, to have all of your students on the same page... Locate the column of [Questionnaire 003] Click on the Sort in descending order . The grades are displayed, starting with 10.00, followed by 0.00, followed by empty grades (for students who have not yet responded to the questionnaire). All you have to do is to replace all the 0.00 with 10.00. Do not forget to click the Update button right at the bottom of the form. et voila!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tracking course name/number
ResponsesInList.Text: The way to do this is as follows: Set up a public questionnaire in a "special" course which is not accessible by the students. In each course where you want the students to answer that questionnaire, create a questionnaire instance based on that public questionnaire. All the responses will go to the public questionnaire residing in the "special" course and will only be visible to the person(s) who have access to that "special course". For each response there, the origin of the courses will be displayed. This is a rather cumbersome process, and several hacks have been suggested in the past but none of them is satisfactory. However, I can guarantee that it does work as expected and is the only practical solution at the moment. Joseph ----------------------------------------- From the online help: There are three types of questionnaires: Private - belongs to the course it is defined in only. This is the standard Moodle module concept. You create a questionnaire and its questionnaire content for the course it is defined in. Editing teachers of that course can change the questionnaire and all teachers can review the results. Template - can be copied and edited. This type of questionnaire cannot be used directly, but its content can be copied into a new questionnaire and edited. Public - can be shared among courses. If a questionnaire has already been created (in another course on the same Moodle site) with the "public" setting, then you may use that "public" questionnaire in your own course(s). The number of settings available to such questionnaires is limited and you cannot edit its questions nor view the responses. Example .- If a public questionnaire has been created in course A, it can be "used" in courses B, C, ... All the responses from courses A, B, C, ... are collected in the public questionnaire created in course A (the original course where it was created) and are viewable there by the person (admin or teacher) who originally created it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic Linking
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Beto, 1.- The automatic glossary linking feature does not pertain to the Questionnaire module itself. It is a site-wide setting which you enable or disable in admin settings. If the name of your questionnaire generates an autolink, this is because you have turned Administration / Modules / Filters / Manage filters / Filter all strings ON . 2.- If you want to prevent the autolink feature when you are typing (or pasting) text in moodle's HTML editor (everywhere on your moodle site), not just in the Questionnaire module), select the text and click the "Prevent automatic linking" button on the second line of the HTML toolbar. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire - adding teacher comments
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jean, Unfortunately the questionnaire was not designed with this feature in mind as it is a data collection tool and not a collaboration tool. But there are a number of ways that you can do this kind of data collection and still be able to provide comments. If you don't need an actual form for students to fill out then a glossary is a great way to do it setting up the glossary so that entries have to be approved before anyone else can view them (this assuming you want the students and yourself to be the only ones able to see the responses.) If you want them to fill out some kind of form then you want to use the database activity. You can build the form in any way that you like with any kind of field and then you decide which way to display the data. It is a bit more complex than the Glossary activity but does give you some additional flexibility. It provides a comments box if you like and the data can be exported to a spreadsheet file. If you want to clarify in more detail on what you actually want to accomplish I am sure we can even give you a bit more detailed information. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: Anonymous questionnaires AREN'T anonymous
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Vedran, Thanks for mentioning this bug. I have fixed in in Questionnaire for Moodle 1.8 and 1.9. and committed it via CVS to contrib . When deleting a response in an anonymous questionnaire, the message is now (as it should be): 
```text
Are you sure you want to delete the response by - Anonymous - ?
```
 Please be aware however that if a teacher (or admin) has access to a moodle site database it is always possible to do a sql query to find out the username of any response. If total anonymity is important to you, then you should probably use other tools than Moodle. Joseph PS.- In the moodle forums community we tend to prefer it when people enter a brief description of themselves, besides an avatar or photo. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire shows only a blank page
ResponsesInList.Text: Mitja > Fatal error : Cannot redeclare questionnaire_upgrade() (previously declared in /home/moodle/mod/questionnaire/db/ mysql .php:3) in /home/moodle/mod/questionnaire.old/db/my sql .php on line 76 Well, there should not be a /home/moodle/mod/questionnaire.old/ folder in your moodle installation! When you visit the admin page, your moodle thinks that you have installed a new module in the /mod/ folder, and it tries to install it, but of course it fails... Here is what you could try, to start from a clean start (remember to do a backup first if you have important data you want to save). Delete moodle/mod/questionnaire.old/ folder Go to Administration ► Modules ► Activities ► Manage activities and Delete the Questionnaire module. Immediately after that, completely delete /moodle/mod/questionnaire/ folder. Re-install the Questionnaire module in /moodle/mod/questionnaire/ folder. That should you start you from a clean installation. Hope that works, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: You have to be a Questionnaire Owner???
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Claire, this is what the online help says (from Quiz/Advanced Options/Content options / Questionnaire Type): There are three types of questionnaires: Private - belongs to the course it is defined in only. This is the standard Moodle module concept. You create a questionnaire and its questionnaire content for the course it is defined in. Editing teachers of that course can change the questionnaire and all teachers can review the results. Template - can be copied and edited. This type of questionnaire cannot be used directly, but its content can be copied into a new questionnaire and edited. Public - can be shared among courses. If a questionnaire has already been created (in another course on the same Moodle site) with the "public" setting, then you may use that "public" questionnaire in your own course(s). The number of settings available to such questionnaires is limited and you cannot edit its questions nor view the responses. Example .- If a public questionnaire has been created in course A, it can be "used" in courses B, C, ... All the responses from courses A, B, C, ... are collected in the public questionnaire created in course A (the original course where it was created) and are viewable there by the person (admin or teacher) who originally created it . So, if you created a Public questionnaire, you have to remember which course you created it in and go that course to view the responses. You cannot view the responses from any other course, even if you are enroled as teacher there or have admin rights. QED Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire - no login required
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jean, Moodle looks at anybody that isn't logged in as a guest. By setting your type to respond daily then the guest user can only complete the survey once per day. If you have many guests that want to complete the survey on the same day then they will get an error about not being able to complete the survey because it has already been completed. Unfortunately you can't guarantee a user will not be able to take the survey again unless they are an authenticated user. For multiple users to take the survey it will need to be set to respond many. If you want a stand alone tool with more functionality then you can take a look at Lime Survey (free and open source or PHPESP also open source and the base for the Questionnaire module)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Respondent Eligibility Question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jenna, This is easily done by going into the edit mode of the questionnaire. You will find a tab at the top of the page called "Override permissions" Click on this tab and then on the resulting screen click on the "Student" link in the "Role" column. On this next screen find the setting that says "Complete and submit a questionnaire" and select the radio button in the prevent or prohibit column. If you don't want them to view the questionnaire set the "View a questionnaire" option to prevent or prohibit as well. Click the "Save changes" button at the bottom of the page and you should be good to go. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Respondent Eligibility Question
ResponsesInList.Text: Randy, The procedure you describe is correct. Actually, the only setting that is really needed to prevent students from completing & submitting a questionnaire is to set View a questionnaire to the prevent OR prohibit state. If a student cannot view a questionnaire, they will obviously not be able to complete it. Unfortunately, this solution is not perfect, since the questionaire instance is still visible for the students. So they can see the Link to the questionnaire, they click on it only to be told "Sorry, but you do not currently have permissions to do that (View a questionnaire)". It would be more logical for the link to that questionnaire instance to simply not be displayed at all for students. Unfortunately - again - if you simply decide to "hide" the link to the questionnaire, then it will be invisible for students but... teachers will not be able to complete it, and will get this error message: "Sorry, this activity is currently hidden". Nothing is perfect! Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Respondent Eligibility Question
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay, here is a better solution to the problem that actually hides the Questionnaire for those that aren't allowed to take the survey. The following describes this process: Groupings must be enabled at the site level. To use groupings, the feature must be enabled on the site by checking the enablegroupings box in Administration > Miscellaneous > Experimental . A groupings tab will appear on the Groups page. Put all of your teachers into one group and all of your students into another group by clicking on the Groups icon in the course administration block. After adding teachers and students to a group click on the Groupings tab at the top of the Groups page. Click on the "Create grouping " button at the bottom of the Groupings window. Give your grouping a name and save it. Now on the groupings page you should see your new group in the list. At the end of the list in the "Edit" column, click on the icon that looks like three little people. Now add the teacher's group to the list on the left. Just select the teacher's group on the right by clicking on it and click on the "add" button. Now go back to your Questionnaire and put it into edit mode. Scroll to the bottom of the page and make sure the "Show advanced" button has been clicked. Set Group mode to Separate In the Grouping option select the grouping that you just created. Tick the box that says "Available for group members only". Save your changes Now when a teacher logs into the course they will see the Questionnaire and students won't even see it! The glory of groupings! Let me know if this works. It works fine on my system.
