ResponsesInList.Title: Re: public questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Edward, From the Questionnaire online help: Public - can be shared among courses. If a questionnaire has already been created (in another course on the same Moodle site) with the "public" setting, then you may use that "public" questionnaire in your own course(s). The number of settings available to such questionnaires is limited and you cannot edit its questions nor view the responses. Example .- If a public questionnaire has been created in course A, it can be "used" in courses B, C, ... All the responses from courses A, B, C, ... are collected in the public questionnaire created in course A (the original course where it was created) and are viewable there by the person (admin or teacher) who originally created it. If you are logged (as admin or teacher) in in course A, in the public questionnaire created there you can see the responses. If you are logged in in courses B or C, in the questionnaires created there using the public questionnaire created in course A you cannot see the responses . I hope that answers your query, if not, please develop your question. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: public questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joseph I understand this, my problem is that I have a number of courses that have the public questionnaire in them. I wondered if there was a way to identify which course contained the public questionnaire that all the results are recorded in. I've inherited the Moodle so wasnt involved in setting-up the questionnaire. The easiest way I know, is to create a hidden course containing the public questionnaire. Then add the questionnaire to the other courses, all results will then be recorded in the questionnaire in the hidden course. Hope this make sense.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: public questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: If you can access your database , you can easily tell from the tables. The 'questionnaire' table lists the survey it refers to in the 'sid' field. The 'questionnaire_survey' table contains that 'sid' value in its 'id' field. Each 'questionnaire_survey' record has an 'owner' field that is the course id of the course that owns that survey. The 'questionnaire.sid' field is a many to one relationship. That is, one survey id (sid) can be present in many questionnaire records.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: public questionnaires
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is an implementation of Mike's suggestion: SELECT q.id as 'questionnaire id', s.name AS 'survey name', q.course as 'course id', c.fullname AS 'course name' FROM mdl_questionnaire q, mdl_questionnaire_survey s, mdl_course c WHERE s.realm LIKE 'public' and q.sid = s.id and q.course = c.id ORDER BY s.name,q.idSince a public questionnaire must be created before being used, the ORDER by s.name,q.id will place the reference to the course where that public questionnaire was created at the top of the list of the courses where it is being used (marked in yellow on the phpMyAdmin screenshot below). Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't see grouped data from "View Responses" in child course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Thomas, Thank you for your appreciation of the Questionnaire module. I did not create it, only took part in its refactoring in various stages, and I am co-maintaining it with the invaluable help of Mike Churchward. 1.- That said, let me clarify things, and explain the expected behavior of the so-called "public" questionnaires. In Course A, create questionnaire QA and make it "public" and set it to "Groups separate" In Course B, create questionaire QB based on public questionnaire QA In Course C, create questionaire QC based on public questionnaire QA Courses B and C have students grouped into groups. Students answer the questionnaires in courses B and C. Then, the teacher can view the responses from courses B and C "consolidated" in questionnaire QA in course A. Because the "consolidated results" in QA in course A may come from a number of courses which may have groups (or not), and those groups may have identical names, it would be quite complicated to display the results other than "in bulk". Should we have a feature to display results from individual courses? from individual courses AND groups within those courses OR across the courses? What do you think? 2.- You write "3) If I go to the first course, I can see all of the questionnaire results regardless of whether they were submitted in the first or second course " Does this mean that, in that scenario, you have students in Course A who actually can respond to public questionnaire QA? That should not be. A "public" questionnaire should be placed in a special course with no students in it, and should not be taken. It should only be used as a repository to collect data from the other courses where it has been "copied" for that purpose. 3.- You write "I was expecting that I would get the "View responses" tab at the top of the instance in the second course, as well, but in fact, there are no tabs at all at the top of the questionnaire in the 2nd course. I don't think it's a permission issue since I'm the site admin." This is the intended behavior of questionnaire instances based on a public questionnaire. No one is allowed to view the responses in the courses where they have been created. Responses are only available to the original public questionnaire, in the course where it was created. This is clearly mentioned in the online Help file (Advanced Settings tab / Content options / Questionnaire Type). Joseph EDITED

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using Questions from Quiz's question bank

The long answer is that - for me - the kind of questions that you would ask in a quiz are totally different in their nature from the questions you ask in a survey-type activity such as Questionnaire (or Feedback). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: reports inconsistency
ResponsesInList.Text: Yaniv, Thanks for mentioning this problem. Here is the situation regarding Coursename ► Reports ► Activity report and Questionnaire at the moment (1.9). 1- All the modules which report something to that Activity report in fact report the number of Views, not number of responses, etc. In the case of some resources or activities , the number of Views is relevant. In the case of activities such as Quiz, Lesson , Questionnaire (and others) that information is not very useful. The number of times that a Questionnaire has simply been viewed (rather than submitted) is not great information! 2- Anyway, it seems that the way that Questionnaire logs Views and Submits has changed some time ago. At the moment it only logs Submits, not Views. You are probably not using the latest version for 1.9. 3- What do we do now? I see 2 possibilities. a) Questionnaire should log all Views, which will then appear in the Activity Report in the Views column. This will be coherent with the way the other modules log user activity. But this is apparently not what you want. b) Whenever a questionnaire is submitted, Questionnaire should log this as View (as well as Submit). Consequently, the Activity Report will show in the Questionnaire View column the number of submissions. This is what you want, but it is not coherent with the other modules' behavior. Before doing anything I would like the opinion of other Questionnaire users (and Mike's view of course). Joseph PS.- For anyone who wants to test out option #b, simply add the following line in file questionnaire/locallib.php, function view(), around line 192 /// Print the main part of the page add_to_log($this->course->id, "questionnaire", "view", "view.php?id={$this->cm->id}", "{$this->name}", $this->cm->id, $USER->id);

ResponsesInList.Text: I don't have this module so I don't know what exactly the export xls contains. But suppose the data you export is columns A-K (Fig 3). In the xls template you leave these columns empty. Then you add to cell L2 the formula =J2-1 and to cell M2 the formula =K2-1 and copy these two cells down to 999 or whatever number that suits your needs (if you prefer the copying may be done in the xls instance rather than the template). Set the background of these cells to grey so as to mark them as calculated. Now you open a new instance of the template, then you copy from the downloaded questionnaire data columns A-K and paste them into columns A-K in the xls report. Columns L and M will display the shifted values. All that remains is to do the statistics on columns M and L rather than J and K (of course you can also implement the statistics in the xls template so that as soon as you paste the data you get the statistics). Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Nobody can login without first closing and restarting the browser
ResponsesInList.Text: The good news is that questionnaires seems off the hook. I installed a second instance of Moodle (the techies at Siteground are really helpful) and a more likely candidate for the cause for the problem is related an accumulation of errors caused by on-campus browser settings / server restrictions. The bad news is that while the past week felt like a lot of intensive research, consultations with IT, and lots of grasping at straws and using sledgehammers to crack walnuts, the problem is still unresolved! I think I need to redefine the problem and post again in a different forum ... either in installations or general problems. ********************* FYI here's some of the distilled wisdom all taken from a variety of Moodle forums. Implemented or checked out... Test if sessions is not be configured properly on the server by calling the script http://yourserver/moodle/lib/session-test.php . If your server is on shared hosting check that you have not reached your disk space quota. This will prevent new sessions being created and nobody will be able to log in. Your own computer (not your Moodle server) may have a firewall that is stripping referrer information from the browser. Here are some instructions for fixing Norton firewall products. Try deleting cookies on your computer and/or try another browser or another client computer In Site Administration > Server > Session handling, try setting a value for 'Cookie prefix'. You can also do this by setting $CFG->sessioncookie='something'; in config.php. This is especially true if you are using multiple Moodles on the same browser. You are using the correct username and password, yes? The presence of a return or other character after the last ?> in your config.php. This seems to cause all manner of problems (1, 2 ) including the one you are experiencing. ...deleting browser cache and cookies Not applicable / too scary / can't understand it / not yet attempted.... The server admin can also fix this for everyone by editing the Moodle configuration page and changing the variable " secureforms " to "No" by accessing database via phpMyAdmin . In the table "mdl_config" is a row with the name "dbsessions", by default its "value" will be set to 0, change that to 1 and you will enable dbsessions. To find that row quickly run the following query: Carefully check the permissions in your 'moodledata' area. The web server needs to be able to write to the 'sessions' subdirectory. Try deleting the sessions folder in your moodledata directory (anybody currently logged in will be thrown out) Client / client site side firewall such as Zone Alarm installed on your computers. To check that there is no client side cookie problem please see http://www.iatn.net/help/cookies/index.asp?Xonce=1 Can you log in in Firefox / I.E. / other browser? Is your server date and time okay? If your sub- domain name is longer than 10 characters (e.g. a_long_subdomain.somewhere.com ), IE will have difficulties in setting cookie http://hk2.php.net/manual/hk/function.setcookie.php If your cookie privacy settings in IE or firefox are the problem then sometimes you must reboot the browser to get new privacy settings to take effect. There was also a July 2006 Moodle bug such that clearing cookies resulted in the " Unfortunately, cookies are currently not enabled in your browser". http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=49316 Try using the login block (but if you are the admin and you can't login you will not be able to use the login block) instead of the login page. Is there a sever side session problem? There could be a lot of reasons?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question about the database structure

For a questionnaire to exist somewhere in Moodle it must have an activity added somewhere to a course. It will use a survey. More than one questionnaire can use the same survey. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Update Questionnaire won't allow me to edit questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alasdair, You do not say which version of Moodle you are using. I expect you are using Moodle 1.9+. Here an extract from the Questionnaire online Help which should help you understand your problem. Joseph Questionnaire Type There are three types of questionnaires: Private - belongs to the course it is defined in only. This is the standard Moodle module concept. You create a questionnaire and its questionnaire content for the course it is defined in. Editing teachers of that course can change the questionnaire and all teachers can review the results. Template - can be copied and edited. This type of questionnaire cannot be used directly, but its content can be copied into a new questionnaire and edited. Public - can be shared among courses. If a questionnaire has already been created (in another course on the same Moodle site) with the "public" setting, then you may use that "public" questionnaire in your own course(s). The number of settings available to such questionnaires is limited and you cannot edit its questions nor view the responses. Example .- If a public questionnaire has been created in course A, it can be "used" in courses B, C, ... All the responses from courses A, B, C, ... are collected in the public questionnaire created in course A (the original course where it was created) and are viewable there by the person (admin or teacher) who originally created it.

ResponsesInList.Text: We're running several questionnaires to track and gather various data. However, some of the answers to the questions we are asking need to be modified routinely. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is it possible to change answers in an active Questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thomas Anyone who already responded and had picked "Tom" for an answer, would now show up as having answered "Steve". Presumably because Tom was the third choice, and Steve now is the third choice. Your diagnostic is correct here. I should say it is not recommended to alter your questions once respondents have started to answer a questionnaire. In fact it does not make sense to me. Are that questionnaire settings "answer many times"? Anyway, the only solution I see to your example is to simply add any new "choices" at the end of your list of choices. Who was your instructor? version 1 - Jack - Steve - Tom Who was your instructor? version 2 - Jack - Steve - Tom - Laura

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is it possible to change answers in an active Questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Joseph, Thank you for your rapid reply. I was afraid that was the case. Let me explain a little about how I'm using the questionnaire. I use the questionnaire as a media equipment request form, and as a training evaluation survey. Both of these are set to "answer many times", since the same respondent may need to use each one multiple times. The media equipment request is mostly text-based, but does have check-boxes for the specific media equipment needed, as well as a check-box question for any services that need to be provided. We need to keep all the previous responses so that we can have records of what equipment is being used (and your summary feature is great for that!) In this case, since they're short lists, I think your solution of putting the new choices at the end of the list will probably work out great, and appreciate your suggestion. As for the training evaluation... this one has many more drop-down fields, radial buttons and check-boxes. Again, we need to keep all the records for reporting. Fields that could regularly change in this questionnaire include the name of the training course, the room the training is held in, and the instructor name. Unfortunately, some of these lists are quite long (especially the drop-down for training courses)... and were previously alphabetized. Adding the choices at the end may cause some confusion and are not as ideal a solution. I'm guessing that part of the problem is that we're basically using your questionnaire not only as a tool to collect data... but we're also trying to use it to store data... and of course, it's not intended to be a database . I'm wondering if my best option might be to export the previous responses to a text file before I make any modifications. Then, I can group and store all responses in an external spreadsheet or database. Sadly, I would lose the ease of your summary page data... but could certainly come up with my own reports. Thanks again for your help... and if you have any more suggestions, please let me know!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is it possible to change answers in an active Questionnaire?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Thomas, Thanks for the clarification. You are certainly using the Questionnaire module for "non orthodox" uses! Are you sure the database module would not be more suitable? Anyway, to answer your last question about exporting the data, you can very well export the responses to radio buttons and check boxes as text rather than numbers. Please see the detailed online Help available next to the Question name field when you create or edit questions. Here is an extract: Edit question - Question Name You can optionally enter a Question Name for each question. The Question Name is only used when you export responses to CSV/Excel format. If you never export to CSV, then you needn't worry about Question names at all. If you plan to regularly export your questionnaire data to CSV, then you have a choice of two options for question naming. Option 1: significant names In the Question Name box, enter meaningful , short and different question names for all of the questions within one questionnaire. In the CSV export file, all those question names will be prefixed with the question's actual number (= position) in the quiz. etc. And, when you Download in text format, in the Options for text download (CSV) , select Include choice codes OR Include choice text according to your needs. That should do what you want. ATB Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire: Removing old and test respondents
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Phil, Not sure I understand what you mean by " old and/or test respondents ", but anyway there are two ways to remove "responses" from a questionnaire. Method # 1 - one by one If you don't have too many responses, you can delete them one by one. As teacher or admin, in your questionnaire, click on the link All responses: View n ; next screen click on the View by response button ; next screen: select responses one by one and click on the Delete This Response button; answer the message "Are you sure you want to delete the response by xxx?" by clicking on the Yes button, answer the "Deleted response 24 by xxx" message by clicking on the Continue button. Can be very tedious! Method # 2 - bulk remove all responses from myquestionnaire01 Create a new Questionnaire, and name it e.g. myquestionnaire02 in: Questionnaire Content: Define New Content: Create new: Help - OR - Copy existing: Select Name Select the name of the Questionnaire that you want to empty all responses from (e.g. myquestionnaire01) . Save your questionnaire. Now you have a questionnaire called myquestionnaire02 which has exactly the same content (the same questions) as your old myquestionnaire01 but with no responses in it. If you want, you can delete the old myquestionnaire01 and rename Delete myquestionnaire02 to Delete myquestionnaire01 . Hope that helps, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is this as complicated as it seems?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I've had a look at ProQol R-IV . What you wish has been asked a few times before; this feature is not currently available to the Moodle Questionnaire module. This feature is a kind of mix between the current features of a Quiz and those of a questionnaire (or survey). It does not quite fit the Quiz format because the required "scoring" does not carry connotations of correct/incorrect and it does not fit the Questionnaire format because ... it does not exist. If you want a respondent to take the questionnaire and have some text displayed onscreen according to their "score" on the various questions, this is clearly not possible at the moment. However, when all the respondents have answered, the "teacher" or admin can export the responses (to Excel or a statistical package) and from there do all the necessary calculations and advise each respondent of theirs "result" e.g. by e-mail. Introducing this feature in the moodle Questionnaire would mean a huge re-factoring. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Wrong 'Response Required' message
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Recently we provided a special "No answer" default choice for the radio buttons questions (see CONTRIB-846 ). The problem you mention is similar to the situation which made us provide for that fix. If a non-required Rate question has been partially ticked by respondent (as shown in your screen shot), then it is impossible for the respondent to untick their choice. One solution would be to systematically provide a non-required Rate question with the N/A column pre-filled (see my screenshot). What do other Questionnaire users think? Joseph PS.- In the meantime you can always select the N/A option to add a N/A column in your Rate question. That way, if respondents click one choice and want to change their mind, they can always click ALL OF THE N/A choices before saving their questionnaire responses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Wrong 'Response Required' message
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't understand why a non-required Rate question must be completed once you  answer one or more of the sub-questions. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Wrong 'Response Required' message
ResponsesInList.Text: The program checks that all choices in a rate question have been checked irrespective of whether that question is required or not. Normally, when a respondent begins to answer such a question, they are expected to complete it. In a required question, it is normal behavior for the error message to be displayed if the question has not been completely answered. In a non-required option, I see 2 possible options: 1) if that question does not have a N/A column, then if some but not all of the choices have been checked, save the response for that question as empty 2) the second option is the one I suggested in my previous mail, i.e. force such questions to have a N/A column, with all N/A choices pre-selected by default. I see no other option.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Wrong 'Response Required' message
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the second option is better. What value will be set for N/A ?  Will it be considered empty ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Wrong 'Response Required' message
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, N/A = empty.

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire: making exported data more compatible with statistical packages
ResponsesInList.Text: To Questionnaire users who export data for statistical study. I have spent a lot of time recently to make the Questionnaire's Download in text format facility able to export data in a format more compatible with standard statistical packages (such as SPSS ). I have put all those changes on my moodle test site . Before putting all those changes to contrib, I would like interested moodlers to test it and to report in this thread. Hopefully I have answered all of Marja's wishes . I have tested the export to the statistical package I own ( Sphinx ), which is similar but less powerful than SPSS and the exported file imports OK into that package. How to test on my test site. Log in as teacher1, password teacher1 (or teacher2, password teacher2). Go to the Questionnaire module Demo course. Click on A Sample Survey about your favorite CMS , click on the All responses - view 42 button. At the bottom of the screen, click the Download in text format button. Either open in Notepad or save to disk. If you have opened in Notepad, select everything, copy and paste into Excel. If saved to disk, import into Excel or your favorite statistical package as usual. Do the same manipulation with a very similar questionnaire in that course, CMS survey . Now look at the columns headings in the first row and compare them. The difference is that in A Sample Survey about your favorite CMS the question name field has been left blank when creating the questions, whereas it has been filled in in the CMS survey questionnaire. I do hope the way the data is exported (as numbers rather than text, except for all-text responses of course) is what is expected of data which will be imported into a statistical package (or simply into a spreadsheet). Of course the names of modalities will have to be restored by hand in the stats package itself, as needed. Please test and report (in this thread). Of course you can also create your own questionnaires to test out the export. I have introduced a small change to the possible answers fields in the questions, to export shorter modality names when such labels are really long. Example, in A Sample Survey about your favorite CMS , question #1 "What do you think of those statements?", Virtual learning=Virtual learning is more effective than classical learning. Traditional learning=Traditional learning will disappear in favour of VLEs. The (shorter) part to the left of the = sign will be used for column heading in the export file, but the full modality label (to the right) will be displayed in the questionnaire for the respondent to see. Joseph PS.- I am still pondering how to answer Yaniv's query . It is not easy, because with the "rate on a scale" question type there arises a confusion between rank and score. I need more thought about it.

I have looked carefully at various survey software and questionnaire templates and I have never seen any where a multichoice, multiselect question had more than one Other box . Since in actual Questionnaire version the possibility to have more than one Other box a) makes data processing and output more complicated and b) is not justified, I plan to restrict the Other box in multiselect (check boxes) question type to 1 instance only (same as in the Multichoice radio button question type). This looks reasonable. What do people think? Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: making exported data more compatible with statistical packages
ResponsesInList.Text: One solution would be for the export data routine to create one column for Other choice with binary data (1=selected; 0=not selected) and another column for Other choice with actual respondent's (text) response. What do you think? That was my piont - binary data (data from checkbox) column for quantitative and text data (data from text field) column for qualitative analyses. This Other choice should have two columns. My vote for only one Other choice for multi-choice (Radio) question, but for multi-select (Checkboxes) I'm in doubt especially for those used in preliminary testings when we are examining the adequacy of our choices before we will make the final selection of them.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: making exported data more compatible with statistical packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marija (and other Questionnaire users interested in exporting data to stats packages)! Further to our exchange in this thread, I have implemented an extra (binary) column for the Other choice in multiselect question type. Please test it on my test site (see instructions in my first post in this thread) and report. In order to implement this I have had to restrict the Other choice option in multi-select questions to one only. This is coherent with most other survey software that I know of. I do understand that in some (rare) cases it might be useful to have more than one Other possibility, but after all, if respondents must use this box, they can always enter their response at more length (and the teacher can analyze this later on). Example: What are your favorite drinks? (Check boxes) lemonade water wine Other : milk, orange juice, Coke, hot chocolate, whisky Note.- I am currently working on implementing some of Daniele Cordella's suggested improvements, especially those aiming at providing a (much needed) more user-friendly interface for entering and editing questions. Among those improvements I would like to make the !other option a clicked box or something like that, to replace the cumbersome entry of !other= as one of the "possible answers" to Radio buttons & Check boxes. That will be a few more days/weeks of work, I expect... Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove All responses view ## button
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, now I understand the problem (only occurring in 1.8). For guests to be allowed to take a questionnaire, it has to be set to Anonymous ( and to Respond many times ). In version 1.8, Questionnaire assumes that students (identified or Guests) are always allowed to see their own responses. The only possible setting about viewing responses is the View all responses (i.e. the statistics view). Unfortunately (from your point of view), this means that for anonymous responses, when a Guest displays " all your responses ", he displays the responses by the previous people who logged in as Guests as if they were his own , because "Guest is Guest". This complicated situation of Guests taking questionnaires has been discussed before in this forum. Actually, because Questinnaire has no way to distinguish one Guest from another Guest, using Questionnaire to collect data from Guests cannot work satisfactorily, simply because there is no way to prevent the same person to take the Questionnaire again and again, as "Guest". So the final results of your Questionnaire will always be questionnable. If your only problem is that of not displaying all responses to Guest users, then upgrading to Moodle 1.9 (and the 1.9 version of Questionnaire) will be the answer. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Maher, Is this question a "real" question in your course evaluation? If so, it's rather strange because it mixes up a number of items which should be evaluated separately . Another problem is that you are using the Rate question type for obtaining binary answers; for binary answers you should use the Yes/No question type. Actually, the problem is not with the Questionnaire module's questions but it is that you (or your faculty members) do not ask the right type of questions. Here are some examples of more meaningful questions. A rating scale question requires a person to rate something along an evenly spaced continuum. Rating scales are often used to measure the direction and intensity of attitudes. Some examples: For me, the PowerPoint lectures were : useless |not very useful|OK|useful|very useful I think that the material for Exam I was completely covered in lectures: strongly disagree|disagree|no opinion|agree|completely agree or I think that the coverage of the material for Exam 1 in lectures was: insufficient|not quite sufficient|fairly complete|complete Binary questions Using the Yes/No question type Do you agree that the material for Exam 1 was completely covered in lectures? Yes / No. Using the radio buttons question type: The material for Exam 1 was completely covered in lectures. Agree / Disagree. I hope this makes things clearer. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire data format regarding
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Suresh, The reason for the different behavior you see between 1.8 and 1.9 versions of the Questionnaire module is that I have spent a lot of time - in answer to Marija's request - to make the data exported by Questionnaire as straightforwardly useable as possible in a stats package. Statistical packages will want to use numbers to produce tables, statistics and graphs, not words. So my answer is that if you need the original wording of choices rather than the choice numbers, you can do it very easily in Excel or the stats package. For example, if you import the exported data file of results from Moodle -Questionnaire into Excel you might get this table: Response Submitted on: Institution Department Course Group ID Full name Username Q01_favorite color 332 29/10/2008 12:15 Course Fullname 101 3 Bella Ben benbella 2 333 29/10/2008 12:16 Course Fullname 101 4 Dupont Jean dupont 3 Using Excel's Search & Replace on the Q01_favorite color column you can easily change 1 to blue, 2 to red and 3 to yellow and get: Response Submitted on: Institution Department Course Group ID Full name Username Q01_favorite color 332 29/10/2008 12:15 Course Fullname 101 3 Bella Ben benbella red 333 29/10/2008 12:16 Course Fullname 101 4 Dupont Jean dupont yellow

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Odd ordering of responses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Everyone, I believe I have found a fix for this issue. In the get_response_single_results() method of the questionnaire_question class in /mod/questionnaire/questiontypes/questiontypes.class.php I have added an order by id. -- BEFORE -- // JR added qc.id to preserve original choices ordering $sql = 'SELECT qc.id, qc.content, COUNT(rt.response_id) AS num '. 'FROM '.$CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_quest_choice qc, '. $CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_'.$this->response_table.' rt '. 'WHERE qc.question_id='.$this->id.' AND qc.content NOT LIKE \'!other%\' AND '. 'rt.question_id=qc.question_id AND rt.choice_id=qc.id'.$ridstr.' '. 'GROUP BY qc.id,qc.content'; $rows = get_records_sql($sql); // handle 'other...' $sql = 'SELECT rt.response, qc.content , COUNT( rt.response_id ) AS num '. 'FROM '.$CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_response_other rt, '. $CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_quest_choice qc '. 'WHERE rt.question_id='.$this->id.' AND rt.choice_id=qc.id'.$ridstr.' '. ' GROUP BY rt.response,qc.content'; ------------ -- AFTER -- // JR added qc.id to preserve original choices ordering $sql = 'SELECT qc.id, qc.content, COUNT(rt.response_id) AS num '. 'FROM '.$CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_quest_choice qc, '. $CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_'.$this->response_table.' rt '. 'WHERE qc.question_id='.$this->id.' AND qc.content NOT LIKE \'!other%\' AND '. 'rt.question_id=qc.question_id AND rt.choice_id=qc.id'.$ridstr.' '. 'GROUP BY qc.id,qc.content ORDER BY qc.id'; $rows = get_records_sql($sql); // handle 'other...' $sql = 'SELECT rt.response, qc.content , COUNT( rt.response_id ) AS num '. 'FROM '.$CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_response_other rt, '. $CFG->prefix.'questionnaire_quest_choice qc '. 'WHERE rt.question_id='.$this->id.' AND rt.choice_id=qc.id'.$ridstr.' '. ' GROUP BY rt.response,qc.content,qc.id ORDER BY qc.id'; ----------- The only thing I'm not sure about is if this fix will need to be done in other areas for different question types. I don't know the questionnaire module well at all! If you want to compare the fix to the old one go to the following URL 's OLD: http://openlearn.open.ac.uk/mod/questionnaire/report.php?instance=1367&sid=1364&action=vall NEW: http://openlearnacct.open.ac.uk/mod/questionnaire/report.php?instance=1367&sid=1364&action=vall Also I don't have commit access to the contrib CVS area, do you want this committing back? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HTML coding in Label
ResponsesInList.Text:
Marija, Before displaying a "label" (sectiontext), its text is formatted as safe HTML . This is where the "radio button coding" is stripped out. You will find it in file questionnaire/questiontypes/questiontypes.class.php, in function sectiontext_survey_display($data) at line 1292. You might replace 
```text
format_text($this->content, FORMAT_HTML)
```
 with 
```text
$this->content
```
 and the radio-buttons, etc. that you want to display will be displayed. However, I don't think it's a good idea, for safety reasons. So I will certainly not change this in the regular distribution of the Questionnaire module. I would suggest another solution. Why don't you simply do a screenshot of the part of the questionnaire you want to "demonstrate" as an introduction and paste that screenshot into the text of your label? Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: People was asking me for a simple new feature

What you want to achieve (for your colleague) is not possible at the moment. Please remember that the goal of the rating question type is to rate responses along a scale, hence the use of numbers , not words! If your colleague wants to export the response data as text, then I suppose the aim is to process that data either ina a spreadsheet (e.g. Excel) or a statistical package. Those programs will want to use numbers to produce tables, statistics and graphs, not words. If your colleague needs to establish a table of equivalences between labels and numbers, she can do it easily in Excel or the stats package. I have spent a lot of time - in answer to Marija's request - to make the data exported by Questionnaire as straightforwardly useable as possible in a stats package and am certainly not going to change it now (unless you have strong arguments to convince me that it is needed). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Complex course surveys
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lori - The "public" type of questionnaire is designed to be created in one course and "used" in other courses. The concept here is to create the "public" questionnaires in a course designed specifically to house those questionnaires and manage the responses. That way, you can limit the people who can evaluate the responses by limiting access to that course. For the certificate, the current one available in "contrib" can be set up so that it can't be accessed until specified activities have been completed. This includes questionnaire. You can also now assign a grade to a questionnaire that is given on completion. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Complex course surveys
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mike Thanks for the reply. I figured the certificate would work that way. If I might trouble you for a few more details. Unfortunately we are the end of the semester and I don't have time yet to play around with this actually using Moodle. So it is a problem stuck in my head that I want to figure out. If you set up a "public" questionnaire, how would students access the evaluations? Through their actual course or through the course created for questionnaires? Here's a scenario...whatever details you can provide through this process would be great: NUR 101 is a course in which all 60 students need to evaluate the course. They also have smaller clinical groups (8 students in each) who will need to do separate evaluations of their specific instructor and site. So I am trying to figure out if I need to set up separate questionnaires and link to these individual questionnaires through their NUR 101 (e.g., Clinical Site and Instructor A eval, Clinical Site and Instructor B eval). Does that make sense? Also, if the certificate is set to be available once the questionnaire is complete, on what page is the certificate set up: the course set up for evals or their actual course page? I know this is a lot of questions, but we have the option of purchasing somewhat costly software to do this or use Moodle. I would prefer to use Moodle for a number of reasons, but I don't want to leave the software out of the budget if Moodle will not work with this. Thanks again for any of your thoughts...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Complex course surveys
ResponsesInList.Text: Essentially you set up a public questionnaire in a course that you will use to access that questionnaire's results, and manage those questionnaires. Nobody will actually fill out that questionnaire in that course. Then in any course you want to collect data for that questionnaire, you add a new questionnaire that "uses" that public questionnaire instead of creating a new one with new questions. All response submitted to a questionnaire that "uses" a public questionnaire submits that data to the public one in the course it was created in. If the users are allowed to see their own responses, they will still be able to see them in the course they completed the questionnaire in. But, to see all the results, you need to go to the originating course, and have access to it. If you want different questions asked, you will need to set up different questionnaires.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire Module - New Version - Testers Wanted
ResponsesInList.Text: Daniele, This is how I imagine most modules and plugins maintainers work. 1- When a bug is fixed or an improvement is made to a module or plugin, and has been tested locally, the maintainer with the CVS committing rights commits the changed file(s) to the moodle core or the moodle contrib CVS repository at http://cvs.moodle.org/ . The best way for moodle users who need to use the most recent version of any moodle core files or contrib files is to use CVS. If you have installed your moodle with CVS, then you can update at any time, without asking yourself the question "is there something new?". If there is something new, then it will be updated, if not, then nothing will happen, it's as simple as that . If you really want to know which files have been changed quite recently, then go to the relevant CVS repository and "sort by date" (see attached example for the Questionnaire plugin). In the CVS repository you can also see exactly which lines have been removed, added or changed, compared to the previous version. 2- Every night (I'm not sure whose "night" it is around the globe, but it seems to be during our European night), all the modules and plugins in the database are automatically updated to the most recent files in CVS core or contrib. Again, if you want to have the latest version of any module or plugin, simply download it, unzip and copy it to the relevant folder on your moodle installation, where any newer file will replace older ones. To sum up: a) using CVS, you can download and install any changed or new file immediately after a module maintainer has committed it b) using the modules and plugins database, you can get the latest changes some time in the morning for any changes committed the day before I agree that it would be nice if there was an automatic device which would scan the CVS repositories for each module & plugin in the database and would display a timestamp of the most recent change in any file in each module, next to the link to download, something like: Discussion Download latest version -> 11:59 14/06/2008 Download for Moodle 1.9 -> 11:59 14/06/2008 Download for Moodle 1.8 -> 11:59 01/06/2007 Download for Moodle 1.7 -> 11:59 01/01/2007 Download for Moodle 1.6 -> 11:59 01/01/2006

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire Refactoring
ResponsesInList.Text: I have just committed a completely overhauled version of the questionnaire so that its interface will be like all other Moodle modules (for better or worse). This has been committed to HEAD for the contrib/questionnaire module. The code in HEAD should be considered BETA at this point, and not used on production sites. Continue to download versions for your specific version of Moodle for stable code. Changes include: Use of Moodle's formslib for all questionnaire editing functions. Update to 1.9's standard course module settings. Addition of capabilities and roles support (this will replace the "respondent eligibility" and view "responses settings" eventually). Separation of standard course module settings, from questionnaire display settings and question editing. Use of tabs to access these separate interfaces (access to tabs is controlled by capabilities). Fusion of the question editing and question re-ordering screens. Addition of group controls. This will affect response viewing only at this point. Ability to assign a grade to a completed questionnaire. Not all of these changes are complete in the version in CVS at this point, but the module is working. If you wish to test this version on a non-production site, please go ahead and download the version from HEAD. If you do install this new version, make sure you logout and log back in after completing the upgrade; otherwise you won't have the new capabilities assigned to your account. mike

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mike, Do you have a time line or rough idea when the questionnaire will be back ported for Moodle 1.9 The latest version works fine in Moodle 1.9 In the upgrade.php file, l change the if ($oldversion < 2008031904) code to something like $studentroles = get_roles_with_capability('moodle/legacy:student', CAP_ALLOW); $teacherroles = get_roles_with_capability('moodle/legacy:teacher', CAP_ALLOW); $editingteacherroles = get_roles_with_capability('moodle/legacy:editingteacher', CAP_ALLOW); $capview = 'mod/questionnaire:view'; $capsubmit = 'mod/questionnaire:submit'; while ($questionnaire = rs_fetch_next_record($rs)) { $ context = get_context_instance(CONTEXT_MODULE, $questionnaire->cmid); /// Convert questionnaires with resp_eligible = 'all' so that students & teachers have view and submit if ($questionnaire->resp_eligible == 'all') { foreach ( $editingteacherroles as $editteach) { assign_capability($capsubmit, CAP_ALLOW, $editteach->id, $context->id, true); } foreach ($teacherroles as $teach) { assign_capability($capsubmit, CAP_ALLOW, $teach->id, $context->id, true); } /// Convert questionnaires with resp_eligible = 'students' so that just students have view and submit } else if ($questionnaire->resp_eligible == 'students') { /// This is the default; no changes necessary. /// Convert questionnaires with resp_eligible = 'teachers' so just teachers have view and submit } else if ($questionnaire->resp_eligible == 'teachers') { foreach ( $editingteacherroles as $editteach) { assign_capability($capsubmit, CAP_ALLOW, $editteach->id, $context->id, true); } foreach ($teacherroles as $teach) { assign_capability($capsubmit, CAP_ALLOW, $teach->id, $context->id, true); } foreach ($studentroles as $stud) { assign_capability($capview, CAP_PREVENT, $stud->id, $context->id, true); assign_capability($capsubmit, CAP_PREVENT, $stud->id, $context->id, true); } } } rs_close($rs); Will it be possible to add this or something like this to the latest version?

ResponsesInList.Title: Text export - questions naming
ResponsesInList.Text: Mawuli Kuivi - Tuesday, 29 April 2008, 09:48 PM ------------------------------------------------------------ Instead of using the name of the questions, will be nice to have to 'question' description. Hence instead say question_1, l would have "What is you name" in quotes. See the online help where the matter of (optional) questions names is explained in detail: Edit question - Question Name You can optionally enter a Question Name for each question. The Question Name is only used when you export responses to CSV/Excel format. If you never export to CVS , then you needn't worry about Question names at all. If you plan to regularly export your questionnaire data to CVS, then you have a choice of two options for question naming. Option 1: significant names In the Question Name box, enter meaningful , short and different question names for all of the questions within one questionnaire. In the CSV export file, all those question names will be prefixed with the question's actual number (= position) in the quiz. Examples: question number (position) in the questionnaire question name entered by teacher field header in csv export 5 favorite colors Q05_favorite colors 6 why_use_Moodle Q06_why_use_moodle 7 user-friendliness (rate question with 3 possible answers: Moodle, WebCT and Blackboard) Q07_user-friendliness->Moodle Q07_user-friendliness->WebCT Q07_user-friendliness->Blackboard Option 2: leave the Question Name boxes blank For each un-named question, CSV export will automatically generate a question name. This is required for table header fields in the CSV and subsequent Excel tables or any statistics package you might be using. The question name generated will be based on the question number in the actual Quiz (excluding Section Text pseudo-questions, of course) e.g. Q01, Q02, ... Q99. For questions with multiple answers, such as rate-type or Likert type questions, a sub-question number will be generated (Q02_1, Q02_2, Q02_3, etc.). This type of "short-name" naming scheme is advisable for exporting your data to a statistics software. Of course, it's up to you to have your own system for remembering which abbreviated question name corresponds to which question in your questionnaire! question number (position) in the questionnaire question name entered by teacher field header in csv export 5 Q05 6 Q06 7 Q07_1 Q07_2 Q07_3 It is quite possible (but maybe not advisable) to mix the two systems, and have within one questionnaire both named and un-named questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Download in text format and other formats
ResponsesInList.Text: The basic idea of providing an export as text (or CSV) format function if to enable users to export raw data which they can then import into any software of their choice. The common basic format which will allow this importation is text or CSV (comma separated values). In the export format currently used by the Questionnaire module, fields are separated by a tabulation and each record is a new line. There is really no standard CSV format, but the Questionnaire export format works fine with MS Excel, Open Office Calc and the statistics packages on which it has been tested. The reason why the exported file has a *.txt extension rather than a *.csv extension is that I have found that when opening a *. cvs file in MS Excel, some "decisions" are automatically made by the software, which can lead to incorrect importing, expecially in the case of non-English languages or non-English versions of MS Excel. There was no such problem in OO Calc. Therefore the correct procedure to import an exported data file from Questionnaire is as follows: In MS Excel Click the Open File button (or select Open from the File menu). You will probably not see the file listed. Click on the "Files of type" bar and select Text Files. You should now see your .txt file listed. In the Text Import Wizard Step 1 of 3, "Delimited" means that data points in your file are separated by specific characters, so that is the right choice. If you are using a Macintosh computer, change File Origin to "Macintosh." If your Questionnaire exported file contains a large number of UTF-8 characters, the File Origin box should show UTF-8 (automatically). However, it there are only a few of those, then you may have to select UTF-8 manually from the dropdown list. Normally, the next steps (2 and 3) of the Text Import Wizard should be automatically set to the correct values, but you may have to change things manually. More info about Excel CSV import here . All about the CSV format here . This may sound complicated but I think that the export/import data operations are usually done by more advanced users who appreciate the flexibility of being able to do what they want with the raw data rather than having automatic options imposed upon them. Some other modules in Moodle have chosen a different option, but there are often problems with the "Export to Excel" option they offer. So in Questinnaire, we keep it simple and "raw". Joseph PS.- In your original mail, Mawuli, you asked 3 separate questions, which is not a good idea in forum discussions . So I have split your post into 3 separate discussions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Templates in Moodle Questionnaire Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alastair, May I suggest an alternative option for your survey? Logged is as admin, on your college moodle site, in block Main Menu, Turn Editing on, Add an activity, Questionnaire. Create your " Initial Student Survey " questionnaire. Choose Respondent type anonymous or fullname, select Respondent Eligibility Students... Questionnaire type: Public . Edit your questions and Save. Hide it so no-one will see it but Admin. Then ask your staff to add that questionnaire to each of their courses. Turn Editing on, Add an activity, Questionnaire. Create " Initial Student Survey " questionnaire. Choose Respondent type anonymous or fullname, select Respondent Eligibility Students... In the Define new content section, select Use public and select Initial Student Survey. Save. When students have answered the questionnaire, log in as Admin, on the moodle site front page , go to the Initial Student Survey questionnaire, click All responses view n button. On the View all responses page you can view the statistics information for all the questions. If you now want to get a breakdown per course, click the Download in text format button and save as a csv text file which you can import into e.g. Excel or another statistical package. There you can view, order and sort the responses according to courses, etc. Please note that with the proposed method, teachers will not be able to view their own students' responses. Admin will have to make that info. available to them (if desired) by filtering the appropriate info. from the spreadsheet and post it to them. However, this method is fairly simple to implement and does not need a special tool to be developed. What do you think? Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire: proposed changes to view all responses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I have been spending "a few" days making a fairly large number of changes to the Questionnaire module so that it will validate against XHTML 1.0 Strict validator. That was very boring work but instructive... As I was doing this, and testing and re-testing the module, I decided to change the way that students can see their own and other respondents' responses. Present situation Questionnaires can be set so that 1) only teachers can view a) their own and b) their students' responses. Questionnaires can also be set so that students can view their own responses. However, there is no setting to allow students to see all the other students' responses (i.e. the statistics page). Proposed changes You can specify who can see the responses of all respondents to submitted questionnaires (general statistics tables). Students can view ALL responses -> Never = by default, only teachers of the owning course can see all questionnaire submitted responses. After answering the questionnaire This allows students to see all responses after answering a questionnaire (the questionnaire must be set to respond once only) If a questionnaire is set to respond more than once, then students cannot see all responses unless you use the next option (when closed). After answering the questionnaire is closed . Please note that students can always see their own responses. I see no reason why this should not be so. Before committing those changes to CVS I'd be interested to hear opinions from the Questionnaire users. You are welcome to try out these proposed changes on my test site as usual. Log in as teacher1 password teacher1. Create your own questionnaires or use an existing one. Make some changes, log in as student and check what happens. Because the questionnaire module is still not "roles-aware", do not try to Switch role to student; go to Participants list, click on a student's name and log in as. Looking forward to your comments, Joseph PS.- I will commit all the WC3 XTHML strict validation modifications and the view responses modifications at the same time, later this month.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 1.9 and Postgresql Install errors
ResponsesInList.Text: Jonathan - I am assuming that you are doing a fresh install. If (and only if) that is the case you may want to use phppgadmin or some other tool (even the pg command prompt) to drop the tables; however, if you are upgrading and already have data in those tables obviously you do not want to drop them. I dropped them because I wanted to get a fresh install to work. After dropping the tables I used a text edit to change line 45 of the /mod/questionnaire/db/install. xml file to read: <FIELD NAME="changed" TYPE="datetime" NOTNULL="false" SEQUENCE="false" ENUM="false" PREVIOUS="thank_body"/> Essentially I just removed the DEFAULT="0" part of that line since that was what was causing the problem. I also created an issue - CONTRIB-343 to alert the maintainer of this issue. Thanks for bringing this to our attention and let me know if you have any other problems.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: always asking a bit more
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Daniele, The problem you describe arises from the fact that the Questionnaire module is missing a "conditional branching" facility. If we had that facility, which exists in many other survey software, it would be possible to do the following: Question #1. Has the user ever been tested with the HIV test? yes no If answer to Question #1 is yes , then display questions #2 and #3 If answer to Question #2 is no , then skip to question #4 Question #2. Date of the test? Question # 3. Which was the outcome of the test? positive negative Question #4. blabla Your solution is ingenious, but it cannot work because of the way the radio-button (single choice) question type functions in Questionnaire (and in all similar survey software). This type of question presents the respondent with a list of closed choices from which he must select one (and only one ). Optionally, this type of question can offer an "other" choice (and only one ). By offering more than one choice to your radio button question you destroy the normal functioning of the question. What is really needed is a "branching" facility such as described at the beginning of this post. I have not idea how easy/difficult it would be to implement. All the best, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Feedback vs Questionnaire - pros and cons
ResponsesInList.Text: We are in the process of moving our online program from WebCT to Moodle. We have a standard 24-question evaluation with both multiple choice and fill in blanks that we need all students to complete at the end of every course. (This is an institutional requirement.) Any opinions on whether the Questionnaire or the Feedback module best meets this need? Are there any pros and cons for one over the other for this type of use? Or any suggestions on other options? Thanks in advance for the input! Susan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Feedback vs Questionnaire - pros and cons
ResponsesInList.Text: Susan - I prefer feedback and would say that in general it is easier/more intuitive to setup a feedback (i.e. "more Moodle like"). Questionnaire impressed me as well as being a powerful tool and it was first on the scene so I installed both on my production server . When it came time to choose which to use for doing course evaluations I opted to go with feedback. Another factor to consider is that feedback is being considered for inclusion in Moodle core so long term it MAY mean less maintenance. That being said, both a good tools for the job. You may want to download and experiment with both but if I had to choose I think I would go with feedback. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Feedback vs Questionnaire - pros and cons
ResponsesInList.Text: Susan, Not sure what a "fill in blanks" question might look like. I suppose it would simply be an "open text" question type? If you want to try out your 24-question survey in the Questionnaire module without having to install it on your moodle server you are welcome to try it out on my moodle test site . Log in as teacher1, password teacher1 (or teacher2, password teacher2) and go to the Questionnaire module demo course. Create a questionnaire, enter your 24 questions. Then log out and log in again as student1, password student1 (or student2 password student2) and enter responses. Or you can send me privately your 24-question survey and I can enter the questions for you. Joseph PS.- I totally agree with Antony's reply. Basically, Questionnaire is more powerful (and less user-friendly) than Feedback. It all depends what you want to do with it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Delete old questionaire surveys
ResponsesInList.Text: Mark - There are three types of questionnaires: private, public and template. Private questionnaires can only be accessed in the course they are created in. Public questionnaires can be used in any course, but the results can only be accessed in the course they were created in. Template questionnaires cannot be used directly, but can be used to create new questionnaires in any courses. They can only be managed directly in the course they were created in. In all cases, questionnaires are created as an activity in a course somewhere. Template questionnaires can be seen in any course when you are creating another, as they can be used to create new questionnaires. But, they exist somewhere in a course. To delete them, you need to go to the course they belong to and delete them as any normal activity. Does this help? mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Delete old questionaire surveys
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks, Mike, for providing a detailed explanation. What is really important for Mark to understand is to locate the course where the template(s) he wants to delete were created in the first place . I am providing an illustrated example of 1 & 2 creating a template questionnaire and 3 deleting it from the course where it was created. Finally, when a "template" questionnaire has been deleted from the course where it was created, it is no longer available as a template for the creation of new questionnaires anywhere alse on the moodle site. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire: groups and permissions - HELP!
ResponsesInList.Text: This is the scenario: Moodle 1.7. One course with forced separate groups. Groups consist of a number of students and one teacher. Course contains several questionnaires. Requirement is that teacher can view responses from own student group only. An editing teacher can view all responses from all groups (no good) and a non-editing teacher can't view any (no good). I've tried tweaking the overrides but of course there are no specific overrides for the questionnaire module as it is non-standard. I've looked at the documentation and forums for roles and capabilities and groups but I'm not a programmer so I'm getting royally lost! Has anyone tried to set up a similar situation? Would attaining this scenario require a lot of alterations/amendments to the Moodle code or could it be just a few lines here and there? Any help would be greatly appreciated as I have to have an answer by Monday.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: groups and permissions - HELP!
ResponsesInList.Text: At the moment the Questionnaire module is not role-aware. If there is a real demand for it, I might try to do something about it. Of course the biggest incentive to do this would be with a view of inclusion of Questionnaire in a forthcoming version of Moodle. If you want this inclusion, you can vote for CONTRIB-56 . Joseph PS.- Do contact me if you are in a hurry.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: groups and permissions - HELP!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joseph Thanks for your reply. I suspect there may be a demand for this as 'quality control' is quite a big thing and the whole guidance side of education I think quite rightly has a place in a VLE. I have used the questionnaire module extensively for student and staff surveys cross college and so it was a natural step to transform the student questionnaires which make up part of their individual learning plans to an online environment. Since these questionnaires are used cross college, the ability to have one course in which all students and their respective class tutors are enrolled in groups is preferable to replicating the same materials within every course, for statistical analysis I am sure also. It was only when I tried to set up the groups that I ran into problems. I posed my issue too to the Scottish Moodle Users Group (SMUG) and found that others had tried to do the same thing as me. One suggested solution was to give a non-editing teacher the rights to login as another user and so view their groups' questionnaire responses but again this was not group specific and teacher from group A was able to login as a student from group B. So I have given up on using the questionnaire module for this situation and will have to make them assignments, as this gives the required confidentiality within groups. I am not happy to do this as it is harder to train staff and students to use the assignment module than the questionnaire module, but as I need a solution for Tuesday 21st August, I am left with little choice I fear. Thanks Karen

ResponsesInList.Title: Questionnaire "Improvements"
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I've been working with the questionnaire module for some time now and over the recent months I've made a few changes to acommodate different requests. The last few days I've redone those changes and tried to make everything fairly concise and clear and commented, etc - just about done now. I thought I'd outline what I've added or changed and then see if there is interest in rolling my changes into the module. I added a "random" attribute to each question so that you can set the position for a specific question or make it random which will scatter the questions labelled "random" amongst the available slots. I added post-questionnaire functionality. When the questionnaire is created you choose available functions from a list of public and private functions that can be called by the questionnaire on submit and each question can call one or more of these functions using either specified values for the function arguments or taking the value from another question's input. This allows things like having a questionnaire where the person taking it can enter in some names, email addresses and other info and have emails sent to the people that were entered. One survey I did involved a person entering a few names and emails and having new questionnaires created from the results of the first questionnaire and then register the names as students and create a new course and enter the students into the course and send them invitations to do the newly created survey which would in turn create new surveys with .... in other words, sort of a chain questionnaire. I ended up getting it to work but it was quite a jumble of code by the time I had it done so now I've taken the basics out and rewritten it to provide the most basic framework I could (at least without trying too hard). These additions are pretty well complete although not particularly polished. I thought I'd just post this before I finish it off in case there are any ideas,comments, requests, etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire "Improvements"
ResponsesInList.Text: Would a copy of the module do? I have it to a point where it can be used as a fresh install but not to where it updates an existing questionnaire module. I'm hoping to get it more or less to that point by the end of the weekend but it does work now. As I mentioned I'm taking the bones of the added code from a bunch of modified questionnaire modules that I made for various projects in the last 6 months and that code was written with no regard to being used for any purpose other than the one at the time of writing so I'm in the process of cleaning up various pieces and putting them into this present one. What this means is 1) it does work and can be demonstrated 2) there is more to come 3) I haven't spent a lot of time getting it to be asthetically pleasing 4) I'm not saying that there probably aren't bugs 5) I'm sure I've overlooked a lot of functionality, and 6) I know of specific things that need to be improved before it is really ready to go. I'll just go through a few things that I know are wrong since not knowing them may cause some confusion during experimentation. I'm having a bit of trouble envisioning what the permissions should be for the various functions - I made a quick stab at dealing with it by making a system where permission could be given to a category, a course, a questionnaire or some combination but I'm not entirely satisfied with it so I've been developing for and only really paying attention to the "public" ones. I also haven't spent much time on error checking like making sure there is no existing function of the same name, etc. You'll notice in the questionnaire module home folder there is now another folder called "custom_methods" which has 1 file and 2 folders in it. One of the folders is "Create_New_Functions" which is associated with a pre-made questionnaire that is created when the module is first installed and is available for use right away. When you create a new function you are asked at the moment to specify a folder name and this is where that folder will be created (at the moment). The plan is to create public functions (or methods) within the other premade folder "public" but I haven't absolutely sorted it out yet. Within the "Create New Functions" folder you'll see one file "create_new_method.php". The equivalent file will be created in the folder specified and the questionnaire that is already made asks for a function name and the name specified will be the name of the file within the new folder. This file is a "stub" - it has some comments in it and one loop that prints out the names and values of the arguments passed to it so that it can be tested upon creation and so that whoever ends up writing the actual code for these function can see what they have available to work with. The created file has this in it - // available arguments are // args['url'] and is of type string // args['reason'] and is of type string function ban_a_site($form_info,$survey_info,$args){ foreach($args as $key=>$value){ echo "The value of $key is $value"; } In the function creator questionnaire ( the one that is installed when the module is and that is associated with the "Create_New_Functions" folder in the "custom_methods" folder) it asks for the folder name, function name and the arguments which are entered in a comma separated list of variable:type pairs ie "url:string,reason:string".  There is also a field to enter the owner in - right now I just enter "public" (all lower case). Two other fields which will be there are "short description" and "long description" but in the interests of not having to worry about them I have not put them in yet. The space and functionality that they provide has been already done though. When this questionnaire is submitted the folder and stub file are created and the function is now available to other questionnaires. The functions that are created are applied at the time of question creation or later editing. There is a new line in the questionnaire creation process that you enter a comma separated list of the functions that should be available to the questionnaire. There is a list of functions and each function has three links beside it to the argument list and descriptions of what the functions do. The info comes up in javascript alerts at the moment. When creating a question there is space for a list of all permitted functions assigned to the questionnaire and beside each function name are inputs for each of the arguments as well as an "enable" checkbox. Each question can be assigned one or more functions by filling in the argument fields and checking the enable checkbox. This is primarily the area where one might notice some poor layout but there is a defined area between functions so the association of the arguments to a specific function is fairly obvious, even if not on the same line all the time. I haven't included a few things that will be included so the layout will surely change soon. In each of the argument fields you can enter one of two types of input for now although there will be a few other choices before long, as in a few days from now. Those two types are a string within quotation marks ie "duplicate content" or a THIS.REASON_FOR_BAN type. The first is how you would include any literal strings you wanted. The second way which starts with THIS. and has no quotes surrounding it refers to the questionnaire itself and the particular input that you want to use for the actual argument that will be passed to the function. You can use any question on the questionnaire whether it comes before or after the question to which the function is assigned. There is no particular advantage at this point to which question a function is associated with. However, there is another type of input which has yet to make it from my projects into this "reference" version which is to use FUNCTION.QUESTION_NAME as the input. In this case the argument for this function will be the result of the function referenced by the FUNCTION.QUESTION_NAME. This is a little convoluted as there can be more than one function associated with any particular question. I do have a method for dealing with this and it can enable some interesting results but it hasn't been made generic yet. There is also some other functionality coming that has a number of stock routines that can be associated with an input to the questionnaire like ROUTINE.QUESTION_NAME.TO_LOWERCASE for example. I also included in one project a VALIDATE.QUESTION_NAME.FLOAT which validates input according to instruction. The result of this is that at some point which question gets which function associated to it doesn't much matter but as the other features get introduced it would. So right now strings are have quotes and otherwise THIS,FUNCTION,ROUTINE,VALIDATE prefixes to question names will eventually do something. All must be uppercase - both the 'THIS.' part and the question name part. The module seems to convert all question names to uppercase anyway so I just continued the tradition. The existing "Create_New_Function" questionnaire can be used as an example of this variable naming. So, the procedure is to add a "Create_New_Function" questionnaire to a course by copying the existing one and then create your function using that. I usually demonstrate by creating a function to send some mail - I call the folder "Send_Mail", the function name is "send_some_mail", the arguments input is "to:string,subject:string,message:string" and the owner is "public". This creates a "Send_Mail" folder in the "questionnaire/custom_method" folder with a file inside called "send_some_mail". Then create a new questionnaire called "Test Function" entering "send_some_mail" in the allowed functions at creation time, do not give it an url to go to when submitted, give it four questions with text fields called TO,FROM,SUBJECT and MESSAGE and fill out and enable the function "send_some_mail" with the appropriate THIS.TO, THIS.FROM, THIS.SUBJECT and THIS.MESSAGE inputs (no quotes). When someone takes the questionnaire the function "send_some_mail" in the file "questionnaire/custom_methods/Send_Mail/send_some_mail.php" will be called and the four arguments will be present for that function to use. Obviously the functions themselves have to be written but the rest seems to work. Assuming that all goes well when you submit the "Test Function" questionnaire and it returns to the confirmation page you should see a list of variable value pairs - proof the the arguments were passed properly to the function. A few bothersome details exist, like how the returned text ends up coming after the "Return" button but because of the way I had to do things it works that way. I assume I or someone will figure out the proper way at some point. Following my explanation is probably harder than just doing it - I have taught a few people to do it so far and the concept that I find that they don't get right away is that you use a questionaire (the existing one) to create functions and then you create questionnaires that use them and then you write the actual function so that each part is a separate step. I'll post the url where my version of the questionnaire module can be downloaded. I've tried to change the existing questionnaire code as little as possible and the parts I've changed are commented (slightly), there is a file that lists the files (mostly) and where (line # more or less) that I've changed and the datatables I've added and the fields I've added to existing tables.
