ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire "Improvements"
ResponsesInList.Text: If you mean can I show an example then no, it was done for someone else and is used by them internally ie not available to the public. I can sort of explain it. I wrote a lengthy explanation of how to use this modified questionnaire which should sort of give the idea of what might be done. In one case, a initial person would be assigned to take a questionnaire and there might be four fields for two email addresses and two names, another field for a message, another for the sender's name, ten yes/no questions and another ten  fields for ten future questions. That initial person, "Adam" would fill in the names of his friends "Bob" and "Carol" and their email addresses, his personal message, his name, answer the ten questions by selecting yes or no, and then enter ten questions of his own. When submitted the following would happen. Bob and Carol would be registered as members and entered into a course created for them with a questionnaire created in that course that has the same basic form but with the new questions that Adam had entered and with the spaces to enter their own questions. Bob and Carol would receive an email notifying them that Adam had made a questionnaire that he'd like them to take and could they please go to the link and take the questionnaire. Bob might give Debbie and Ed for his two contacts and Carol gives Fred and Gertrude and so on. That is the basic premise, although there ended up being much more due to the people who I did this for getting functions done to manipulate the results of the questionnaires. This includes having an instant graph or chart drawn as well as an automated assessment. All of this basically happens independently of me so that what they did was create a longer questionnaire, say 80 questions and have 10 of them the new questions created by each user and to manipulate the order of the questions based on the results to date. For example the goal might be to get as many "yes" answers as possible so you experiment with giving people tests with the most commonly asked "yes" questions at the start to see if people will just eventually say "yes" to all of them and by wording the questions correctly (the new questions) each participant tries to get a higher "yes" score from their contacts.  It went deeper than that but the data and courses etc started adding up and fortunately the experiment ended without exposing the limitations of my lousy hacks. I made a few functions for them like when Adam gives Bob and Carol the instructions to take the test it might turn out that Bob hasn't done the background studying necessary to take the test and after a few days he needs reminding and then he needs reminding until it gets done so I made a remind function which the makers of the exam would attach to the questionnaire and it would cause the monitoring of the questionnaire_attempts table and send them an email every so often. Since Bob and Carol weren't members but needed to be they had to be registered so I made a "register_new_user" function which the makers of the exam attached to the questionnaire so that when Adam submits the questionnaire Bob and Carol get registered. Since you can attach multiple function to any question and use the inputs from any question as the arguments for the functions you can get quite complex things to happen once you have six or seven generic functions you can assign to any particular question/questionnaire. One thing that I've done on another project was to use a method of using the results of one function as input to an argument of a different function so that you might have four arguments that get passed to one function with each argument being a reference to a different function. I tried to get the "chain questionnaire" project to be able to use the above "functions passed as arguments" technique but by this time the whole thing was getting a little "unwieldy" to say the least and no-one could keep any sort of handle on what was really going on. There were some interesting results but nobody really wanted to spend the time it might take to track the process to see if the results were really valid ie they appeared random but whether that was because the functions were acting in random manner or whether the process was in fact reacting to the function paths and inspiring a randomness in people's answers will never really be known. What I'm hoping to do with this effort that I'm doing now is to eliminate some of the areas where expedience made my coding less well thought out than it might have been had I known what was going to be asked for in terms of "features". I'm hoping to get the architecture of the process done reasonably soundly and then improve the pieces. Ideally the basic path is or will be sound and minimally dependent on the questionnaire module itself so that a library of functions that work with the questionnaire might be possible and maybe we will have lots of "plug-ins" for the questionnaire.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire "Improvements"
ResponsesInList.Text: 6 months later .... I have a version of a questionnaire module I've done - a link to the module is at the end of the post - I left a few things out since I was trying to keep the changes I had to make to the original questionnaire as basic as possible and the functionality as non-specific as possible. I did it for a client who has a very specific purpose and in the interests of time I put some "hardcoded" data into my original modified version but I've removed them in this version. This to explain why there are some "coming soon" areas. I started to try and make it do the upgrades to existing questionnaire modules but haven't finished that yet - this version is for new intalls only. There is quite a bit more functionality than I described in earlier posts - sort of. I've included some things which obviously don't help at the moment but I haven't included the evaluation part of what I did as it was very application specific. I'm in the process now but thought I'd put the questionnaire out there to get feedback if anyone is interested in it before rewriting my code to encompass the general instance. My client is hoping that the new stuff can be incorporated into the standard module so as to take advantage of improvements in the future without having to constantly pay to have the module redone. There is no documentation as of yet - I am working on it and will put something together in the near future but a lot of the stuff is pretty straight-forward I think and anyway, most of the new functionality needs to have corresponding functionality implemented in the results (marking/scoring) part of the questionnaire. I intend to "finish" this project (for now) in the next week or so - if anyone sees any problems or an opportunity to add some additional functionality then now would be the time to suggest it, while I'm familiar with the code. I will also be putting up some screenshots as I go through my "final testing" which hopefully will save writing documentation. When you create a question for a questionnaire there are a few new fields that can be entered. One is "Random" which does just that - puts a question in a random spot but if you set it to "No" then it will retain that spot so if you have questions 1 and 3 set to "No" and questions 2, 4 and 5 set to "Yes" then 2 and 4 and 5 will randomly switch places but 1 and 3 will stay in their positions. As of yet I haven't implemented any way to record which order the questions were presented to students but I did for my client and will likely try to do it again - I wasn't happy with the manner in which I accomplished it so I haven't included that part. There is another new field called "points" and it exists to assign a point value to a question. At the moment it has a dropdown choice from 0 - 20 (for no good reason except I haven't changed it from the client's need). Another field is "Section Name" which lets one assign a question to a section for marking purposes. In a questionnaire designed for example to evaluate behavior in a number of areas one might want to score the sections separately but could be used for other things. It became necessary when keeping track of the questions' order when random questions are present, etc as well as when used in conjuction with the different functions that can be called from the questionnaire. Another field is "Default Text" and is there to put some default text into a text input. This field can be set to take a variable in a case yet to be described. There are another 5 new fields that are "N/A" which represent functionality existing in my client's version that I haven't been able to include at this time because it was not general enough. I left them there to remind me to do them and also in case anyone suggests new functionality. When choices are present there are a number of fields beside each potential choice - four of them at this point are just "Coming Soon" (again, for unimplemented stuff) but the new one is "Percentage of Points" and this allows a question to be set at (for example) 12 points total value and if there are (for example) 5 choices of "perfect, good, adequate, poor and bad" you could assign "perfect" to 100 and so a response of "perfect" would be worth 12 points (the total potential value of the question) and "poor" might be "30" which would be 3.6 points, etc. One of the other fields used to be for a method of allowing the answer to one question to be taken into consideration when assigning a score to another but I haven't included that at this point. There is also a dropdown box in which you can specify the order of the choices - "normal", "random" and "reverse". I did have a fourth option of randomly normal or reverse but left it out. Again, I haven't included any way of keeping track of the order in which the choices were presented to the survey taker. All of the above fields (with the exception of "Random" have no effect at all on the questionnaire and are used only for scoring purposes. As regards the original posting's described feature of being able to create post-processing custom functions to be called upon questionnaire submittal - it goes a bit further now in that when you create a function to be called by questionnaire there are actually three functions created. One does pre-questionnaire display, another is called for each individual question and lastly the original post-questionnaire submittal processing. The pre-display is just because I could, I've used it for a few things but not for anything useful yet. The individual question function was originally to change words in the questions, or to include time-sensitive pictures or info with the question but has proven more usefull to fill out dynamic defaults in the text fields for the answers. This allows one questionnaire to go to a subsequent questionnaire and have some of the fields pre-filled out for the survey taker. At the moment I am still converting it to suit the general case but that is why it is there. The other part that I haven't included yet, but will, is a new type of field "Hidden". Again, you can have it be a variable filled in by the individual question processor. At any rate, the demo is at http://rcmp.org/moodle_questionnaire/index.html if anyone wants to look at it or comment. I don't have any examples of it working that are publicly accessable - oh, and for now only the mysql database stuff is done.

Things are different with enrolled students (or teachers, etc.) who have a USER id on your Moodle site so that it is possible for them to answer anonymously and for the Questionnaire module to mark them has "having answered once". Please be awere that with these settings anyone logged in as Guest (or anyone logged in as enrolled student/teacher) can answer the questionnaire as many times as they want, which statistically renders the responses you get pretty useless. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: download responses to CSV
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Daniele, Please remember a general rule on discussion forums is to always post only one question per message . I will answer here your question about downloading user responses to CSV ( not CVS ). When you are in report mode, at the bottom of the View All Responses screen you can see the Download in text format button which saves all user responses to a text file which is a CSV file. Here is the text of the Help file that you can see if you click on the Help icon next to the button. I have spent a lot of time (re-)writing the help files for the Questionnaire plugin, trying to make them as explicit as possible, but help files are only useful if users actually read them. Download in text format If you need to study the data of the questionnaire responses outside of Moodle in a software such as Excel , Open Office Calc or a statistical software package, you can export the data in text format. The text format available here is of the so-called CSV (comma separated values) type. However, for more universal use, the tab (tabulation) separator is used, rather than the comma or semi-colon. When you click on the Download in text format button, a window opens, asking you whether you'd like to save the data file or open it. Select save . The data file is named after the name of the current quiz, however you can save it under a different name. The proposed data file extension is *.txt, but you can rename it. Note that you must rename it with a *.csv extension for import into Open Office Calc . Then go to your external software, and open the file into it. The following operations depend on the software you are using and on a number of other parameters. If you are using a non-ascii language interface in Moodle or you are using the English language but some of your questionnaire questions (or responses) have non-ascii characters in them, then Excel (or Open Office Calc ) might be able to automatically detect that your file is UTF-8 encoded, and decode it accordingly. Please note that if most of your data file is using standard ascii characters and only a very small number of non-ascii characters are present, the automatic detection will not work, and you will have to select the UTF-8 encoding in the list provided by your software by hand. At the top of the "table" imported into e.g. Excel , the first line contains the names of all the question fields. This is followed by one line per response. The first 7 fields are as follows (in the English version): Response Submitted on: Course Group ID Full name Username The submitted_date field contains the date (and time, i.e. hour minutes seconds) when the response was submitted by respondent. For example: 15/09/2007 15:57. Normally you should be able to use Excel cell formatting to display such dates at will, in your own language formatting conventions, including the seconds, and if you wish full day or months names, while retaining the sorting facility.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Answers already selected on a new Response
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Antonio, I have solved this problem and committed to Moodle 1.7 to 2.0 (HEAD) versions in CVS . I have added this explanation in the Help files: Save & Resume (Help File) Setting this option allows users to save their answers to a questionnaire before submitting them. Users can leave the questionnaire unfinished and resume from the save point at a later date. Note .- If a questionnaire is set to Save/Resume answers , then guests will not be allowed to view it . Since there is no way for Moodle to tell one guest from another, it would not make sense for one guest to start responding to a questionnaire and another guest to finish it! Questionnaire Response type (Help File) You can display your users' full names with each response by setting this to "fullname". You can hide your users' identities from the responses by setting this to "anonymous". Note .- If your Moodle course allows guests, they will only be allowed to respond to a questionnaire whose responses have been set to anonymous . Joseph PS.- For translators. Please update your translations to the latest language files available in English and e-mail them to me. Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: Proposal for an enhanced version 2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Marija, After a few days (and many hours) of hacking away at my machine I have come with a new numbering and naming system for the Questionnaire questions. Here is a copy of the (new) online help. Enter the text of your question (i.e. What is your favorite color? ) in the Question Text box. You can optionally enter a Question Name for this question. The Question Name is only used when you export responses to CSV/Excel format or if your questionnaire is set up to send email responses to the teacher . If you never export to CVS or use the email reponses setting, then you needn't worry about the Question names at all. If you plan to regularly export your questionnaire data to CVS, then you have a choice of two options for question naming. Option 1: significant names In the Question Name box, enter meaningful , short and different question names for all of the questions within one questionnaire. In the CSV export file, all those question names will be prefixed with the question's actual number (= position) in the quiz. Examples question number in the questionnaire question name entered by teacher field header in csv export 5 favorite colors Q05_favorite colors 6 why_use_Moodle Q06_why_use_moodle 7 user-friendliness (rate question with 3 possible answers: Moodle, WebCT and Blackboard Q07_user-friendliness->Moodle Q07_user-friendliness->WebCT Q07_user-friendliness->Blackboard Option 2: leave the Question Name boxes blank For each un-named question, CSV export will automatically generate a question name. This is required for table header fields in the CSV and subsequent Excel tables or any statistics package you might be using. The question name generated will be based on the question number in the actual Quiz (excluding Section Text pseudo-questions, of course) e.g. Q01, Q02, ... Q99. For questions with multiple answers, such as rate-type or Likert type questions, a sub-question number will be generated (Q02_1, Q02_2, Q02_3, etc.). This type of "short-name" naming scheme is advisable for exporting your data to a statistics software. Of course, it's up to you to have your own system for remembering which abbreviated question name corresponds to which question in your questionnaire! question number in the questionnaire question name entered by teacher field header in csv export 5 Q05 6 Q06 7 Q07_1 Q07_2 Q07_3 It is quite possible (but not advisable) to mix the two systems, and have within one questionnaire both named and un-named questions. I am committing these changes, plus many other minor improvements & bug corrections tonight. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: Proposal for an enhanced version 2
ResponsesInList.Text: Marija > 2. There were again some problems with the Date question. I have troubles entering date of birth in the required format (and any other, for that matter). A friend of mine was, while testing, entered 6/6/1666 as a date, but it was automatically converted into 31/12/1969. The date format is using the php mktime function . This is very useful for automatic date checking and (re-)formatting. For example, the following conversions will occur: date entered date displayed 16/9/07 16/09/2007 32/1/08 31/01/2008 29/2/2007 ( not a leap year!) 1/03/2007 6/6/1666 31/12/1969 or 1/1/1970 However, this type of date is supposed to apply to "current" dates, and thus only applies in the range of years from 1902 to 2037. In the context of questionnaires/surveys, etc. the date-type field is supposed to be used mainly for entering current dates, such as date-of-birth, date of applying for a job, date for an appointement, etc. Another reason for this "restricted" range of dates is the ability of e.g. MS Office to format the date field at will (when the questionnaire data is exported to CSV and Excel) for dates in this range, but not for dates outside the range. If a date outside the 1902-2037 range is absolutely needed as a response, I suggest using the plain text box format. However, to make things more clear to respondent, I have modified the date question type behavior to issue an ERROR statement instead of reformating to 1/1/1970 when the date entered is not in the expected 1902-2037 range. This will take effect when I update to CVS in the coming days. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: Proposal for an enhanced version 2
ResponsesInList.Text: Antonio > What is happening is that any date before 31/12/1969, ex. 10/10/1950, is saved like 31/12/1969. This does not happen to me. The problem is not due to the language version you are using. If you are using PHP 5.1 or 5.2 (and Windows), only dates outside of the 1902-2037 range will issue an error message. PHP 4.3 seems a bit outdated now, and it has that limit, as explained in the following, copied from the PHP Manual . The valid range of a timestamp is typically from Fri, 13 Dec 1901 20:45:54 GMT to Tue, 19 Jan 2038 03:14:07 GMT. (These are the dates that correspond to the minimum and maximum values for a 32-bit signed integer). However, before PHP 5.1.0 this range was limited from 01-01-1970 to 19-01-2038 on some systems (e.g. Windows ). On Moodle sites where it is not possible to upgrade to PHP 5.1 (minimum) the only workaround I can think of is to create the question date as a simple text box question, to avoid re-formatting... Other than that, since I do not have an earlier version of PHP on my machine I cannot test the wrong re-formatting problem. Sorry. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: Download CSV does not work properly with Portuguese Language and Regional Settings
ResponsesInList.Text: Antonio, I have exactly the same problem with French version of Excel. The problem arises from the fact that only an English version of Excel will correctly read a *. cvs file, because of 2 problems: a) the separator used (comma "," for some languages or semi-colon ";" for other languages) and the character set being used. Try this, it works ok for me in French version of Excel: 1- When you do the CSV export of your questionnaire responses, change the *.csv extension to a *.txt extension before saving the file to disk. For example, save it as responses.txt 2- Open Excel. 3- In Excel, Open File / Filetypes: Text files: *.prn, *.txt,*. csv / open your responses.txt file 4.On the next Excel screen, Excel might or might not automatically detect that your data is "delimited", if not, then check the Delimited radio button 5. On the same screen, File Origin: in the list of character encodings, select 65001: Unicode (UTF-8). 6. Next screen: Separators: check the "comma" check-box Next... And you get your correct data! ResponsesInList.Title: Re: save and resume
ResponsesInList.Text: After more thorough investigating the code of the Questionnaire module I have come to the conclusion that it is not possible to enable both the anonymous respondent option and the Save/Resume option at the same time . For the Save/Resume option to work, the module has to store the ID of the actual respondent in the database , in order to retrieve it later, when that respondent wants to continue and submit his answers. Storing the respondent's ID is logically incompatible with the 'anonymous' option, because it would mean that the responses would not be really anonymous if it were possible to retrieve the respondent''s ID from his saved attempts. What I suggest it that there should be a mechanism to prevent setting both options at the same time or, in the meantime, at least a warning in the online help explaining things. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using a date selector for the Date type field
ResponsesInList.Text:
To adjust the date format for all of your questionnaires you can hack file mod/questionnaire/locallib.php line 25, change: 
```text
define('QUESTIONNAIREDATEFORMAT', '%d/%m/%Y');
```
 to 
```text
define('QUESTIONNAIREDATEFORMAT', '%m/%d/%Y');
```
 To check that it works, create a question of Date type in your questionnaire, go to "take the questionnaire" and next to the input field you will see, instead of the default example: (e.g. 21/4/2002) -> (e.g. 4/21/2002) . In my (forthcoming) proposal for a new version of Questionnaire, I have made this date formatting dependent on language files, so you will have e.g. 23/4/2007 in the English lang file, 23-4-2007 in the French file, 4/23/2007 in the US_English file, etc. Please note that at the moment there is not a very robust format checking for the Date question type in Questionnaire. If a respondent enters a response which does not correspond to the expected format, it will simply be ignored, the respondent will not receive a "wrong format" error message. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: Problem in editing questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Io, 1- There are two "families" of question types in Questionnaire: "family 1": questions which do not require answers: text box essay Yes/No date numeric question text (a description text, not a real question) "family 2": questions which require answers radio buttons check boxes rate (scale 1..5) You can change the type of an already created question within one family but not to the type from another family. Examples you can change an Essay question's type to Yes/No or Text Box, etc.: you can change a Radio Buttons question's type to Check Boxes or Rate. You cannot do what you want to do : change a Radio Buttons question to Essay. You have to delete those questions with the wrong type and create new questions with the correct type instead. In the new version (v.2) of the Questionnaire which I propose here , if you try to do this an error message is displayed telling you that it's impossible. 2. " Something else, that looks strange, happens every time i choose to edit the questionnaire, the option "save/resume answers" turns in to "No" even if i change it every time to "Yes" and save the changes " This was a bug which I have corrected in v.2. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help me！
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, This problem is not specific to the Questionnaire module but to any Moodle module which exports data (including dates) in the CVS (comma separated values) format (for Excel, etc.). Here is how to proceed. In the Questionnaire module, when you click on Download CSV button, a popup window appears in your browser, asking you whether you want to open the aiciba.csv file in MSO Excel (default) or save to disk. Do not choose Open with Excel but Save to disk . Save to disk but change the CSV extension to TXT , i.e. save as aiciba.txt Open MS Excel. From the File|Open menu in Excel, File Type, select the list: *.prn *.txt *.csv and open your aiciba.txt file. Normally, Excel detects the encoding of your file. It detects that aiciba.txt is encoded as 65001 Unicode 5UTF-8). (If this is wrong, select the correct encoding from the File encoding dropdown list). In the Excel import options, select Delimited , Next , Comma (you can see the result on your Excel screen). Now you can see all the imported data from your aiciba file... but the SUBMITTED column has dates in Unix timestamp format: SUBMITTED: 1178343421, 1178343478 Just to the right of the SUBMITTED column, insert a new column, name it DATE. In the first cell to the right of the first SUBMITTED date, write this formula: B2 / 86400 + 25569 Unix timestamp date 1178343421 is changed to Excel format: 39207.23404 Now go to Excel menu Format|Cell|Number|Date and select your favorite Date/Time formatting. Copy the formula in all the cells in the DATE column. See result on attached screen shot. NOTE.- If you want the time (hour, minutes and seconds) to be displayed as well as the date, it's possible, but you may have to adjust the conversion formula above by adding or substraction the number of hours difference with GMT time. For more details, see Unix Timestamp Converter . All the best, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Text: I think I've traced it to a function called `response_select_name` which seems to assume that the question name is unique as it adds data to a array using that as a key. This clobbers all but the last entry which is consistent with the output I'm seeing.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: CSV output broken when question names repeated?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, As I am currently working at tracking bugs & proposing some enhancements to the Questionnaire module, I will look into this problem ASAP and report here. In the meantime if your priority is to rescue your results, I suggest simply renaming the questions which at the moment have exactly the same "field name". For example if you have 3 questions all named MYQUESTION in the Question Name field, go to Questionnaire edit mode (Update this Questionnaire) and rename them MYQUESTION1, MYQUESTION2 and MYQUESTION3 and save your questionnaire. You will be able to export your results to CSV/Excel correctly. I have just tested this and it works for me. Joseph EDIT.- Yes, the `response_select_name` function seems to be the culprit. ``

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: CSV output broken when question names repeated?
ResponsesInList.Text: In the Questionnaire plugin, when new questions are entered and the Question Name field is left empty, it is automatically filled with a name which is extracted from the Question Text. Example: Question text = Do you like Moodle? -> automatically generated Question Name = LIKE_MOODLE. There is a routine which a) removes common "grammar words" from the Question Text (only valid for English) b) changes to UPPERCASE and c) adds underscores as word separators. Now, if a teacher creates two questions of different types but with the same question text (or very similar question text which results, after the automatic filtering, into the same Question Name), both questions will have the same Question Name. This Question Name is stored in the database, but does not appear at all in the Questionnaire itself. So there is no problem when using the Questionnaire. The Question Name is only used for CSV export, where, as mentioned by David, it causes a problem. I am suggesting this code hack, which will automatically detect duplicate Question Names and add an asterisk (or asterisks) so that the CSV export now works OK. In file mod/questionnaire/locallib.php , around line 890, add the lines in blue to the code. // constraint: fieldname must be not empty // generate it from the content if empty See results in attached screen dump. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire Module - 4th Release
ResponsesInList.Text: Setting up a questionnaire requires two distinct steps. The first one is to create a survey using phpESP; the second is to add that questionnaire activity to a Moodle course. To create a survey, go to the phpESP management interface as an administrator. This is found at http://[your_site]/[your_moodle]/mod/questionnaire/phpESP. The directory you specified cannot be accessed directly. Once there you can create a new survey. Before you can access this survey in Moodle, you will need to activate it (use the 'Change Status' option at the management interface). Once you have a survey or surveys created, you can add them as questionnaires to a Moodle course. From the Activity drop-down, choose Questionnaire, and fill in the details. The survey you created will be available from the drop-down there (but only if you activated it). As far as importing users, you don't need to import users to a survey. Moodle users of a course will be able to use questionnaires in that course. If you want to import users to Moodle, read the help file on your Moodle site about this (you can find it here as well). mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re-thinking Feedback Anonymity
ResponsesInList.Text: Andreas - I hope you are doing well. I have started looking the feedback code and want to make some minor hacks that impact anonymity. I would like to 1) log all completions and 2) change the timemodified for the completed feedback to midnight of the current day. The first one is easily enough accomplished by simply moving the add_to_log in complete.php up before the if statement around line 224 as follows: $savereturn = 'saved'; add_to_log($course->id, "feedback", "submit", "view.php?id=$cm->id", "$feedback->name"); if($userid > 0) { However, the second step is causing me a little more trouble. I thought that if changed line 824 of the lib.php file where $timemodified is defined that that would take care of things; however, it does not seem to be that easy. At this point, I'm not so much concerned about the proper timemodified being stored in the feedback tables. Even if for anonymous and non-anonymous feedbacks the timemodified is always midnight of the current day that would be fine with me as it would obscure the identity of the respondents sufficiently to prevent a direct match. Although as I think about it I will also need to shuffle the order of the responses to prevent a teacher from simply comparing the log order to the responses. Have you had a chance to give any further thought to how we might log anonymous feedback and still be able to consider the responses anonymous?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-thinking Feedback Anonymity
ResponsesInList.Text: Andreas - I've slept on this anonymous thing and here is one thought that I had and I thought I would run it by you to see what you think. I started shuffling the completed responses but realized that a teacher would never be able to step through the individual responses. I thought that if we created a field in the feedback completed table called random_response that we could store an integer and use that as the response. Rather than viewing completed responses by the timemodified (i.e. date of submission) we could view anonymous responses as Response #1, Response #2, etc. The logic for viewing could be something like: if anonymous feedback then $feedback_completed = get all of the completed feedbacks sort $feedback_completed by random_response if there is a null random_response then shuffle $feedback_completed

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-thinking Feedback Anonymity
ResponsesInList.Text: I have finished making my initial hacks and initial tests to Andreas' work. The hacks are based off of feedback17.zip and I have been testing them in Moodle 1.8. These hacks changes a couple of things: All submissions are logged (anonymous and non-anonymous) Userid is stored in the feedback_completed table so that admins can track a response back to a particular user Because the userid is saved, analysis can be viewed by groups (for both anonymous and non-anonymous). To be done: Consider adding an option to allow for anonymous and non-anonymous submissions. If the feedback is anonymous then an extra pushbutton for submit non-anonymously could be selected. This would allow for when a student really wants the teacher to know who it is from. Similarly, if it is a non-anonymous survey, the student could choose to submit it anonymously; however, the student should understand that if only one anonymous feedback is submitted it will be deducible whose it is. This initial hack is attached to MDL-9140 (a request to include the feedback module into Moodle core) should anyone be interested in helping to test it. Alternatively I will try to keep a latest version available at http://www.jesuitcp.org/facultypages/aborrow/feedback_hack.zip . Use at your own risk (i.e. make a good backup before using). Please note the changes to the /mod/feedback/db/ mysql .php file which adds 2 fields to the feedback_completed and feedback_completedtmp tables. Feel free to email me with any feedback, suggestions, etc. you might have. Peace.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-thinking Feedback Anonymity
ResponsesInList.Text: I have started playing with some of the options I suggested above regarding anonymity and it occurred to me that another possible advantage/feature that could be added would be to allow anonymous responses. Just thinking out loud, I would envision that a feedback could be setup to be completely anonymous, completely non-anonymous, or to allow anonymous responses. By allowing anonymous responses, the student could choose whether they want to submit anonymously or submit with name. If they submit with their name then the name would be displayed but if it is an anonymous submission then the name does not appear. It seems to me that there may be cases where there is a real advantage to giving the student the option to have their name attached to something or not (this would require two different submit buttons).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-thinking Feedback Anonymity
ResponsesInList.Text: I think it needs to be all or nothing. If you make some students anonymous and some not, the teacher may figure out who the anonymous ones are by a process of elimination. If for example it were used for giving feedback on the course and all the positive responses came from non-anonymous students and the negative responses from the anonymous ones-the teacher would know who gave negative reviews.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-thinking Feedback Anonymity
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, I was assuming that most students would choose to remain anonymous but some students may choose to identify themselves. Your point is a good one and if the option is given to have both anonymous and non-anonymous responses, then those choosing to remain anonymous should be aware of the limited anonymity. Perhaps some careful wording of the language files could communicate this.

On that page is a request from the administrator (or teacher) asking the student to send an email using a mailto link. The student is asked to include his or her real name in the message. Would this be a reliable method? I am not good enough at programming to create the completed.php thing mentioned above. --Sarah

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ideas for making a questionnaire/feedback mandatory yet anonymous
ResponsesInList.Text: Sarah - We are currently not able to track who submits a feedback when in anonymous mode. There has been some discussion on this but currently it is not permitted. I personally think that the student submission should be logged; however, there was concern that the log timestamp could be used to match up to the response submittal time. I think that if it is anonymous we should probably create a log that a student submitted it and record the time of the submission; however, in the feedback tables the time would not be recorded. I would also like to see submissions be sorted by group. I think that logging would be the best way for a teacher to know if a student has completed a feedback and it would really only take a line or two of code but some steps should be taken to help ensure anonymity. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ideas for making a questionnaire/feedback mandatory yet anonymous
ResponsesInList.Text: For us, the ability to log whether a student has completed the evaluation is critically necessary. I can understand why the author of Feedback would want to maintain anonymity but I can imagine other situations like ours, in which feedback goes to people other than the instructor. In these cases, there should not be the problems that anonymity seeks to avoid: an instructor might try to retaliate against a student who offered negative feedback, or might favor a student who gave positive feedback. We (administrators, not teachers) need to learn some basic things from students. Some of those things are about issues that are unconnected to the teacher or curriculum. And we would provide results of feedback on the teacher and curriculum to the teacher in compiled, aggregate format only. I like the Questionnaire module because the student response, even anonymous, is logged. Also, Questionnaire can send the student who has just completed the Questionnaire to a specific URL, which could ask the student to send an email to an administrator (other than the teacher), letting the administrator know that the student has completed the Questionnaire. How difficult would it be for me to include these functions in Feedback?--Sarah

ResponsesInList.Title: "Tagged" content in Questionnaire Creates "tagged" field name, messes up export
ResponsesInList.Text: Dealt with this one quite a bit this past couple weeks -- turns out that if you html-encode the content of your question in the Questionnaire module and leave your field name blank, the encoding doesn't get stripped from the created field name so numerous questions can actually be created with the same field name, fouling up the exported data significantly. The most recent version located on moodle.org in plugins retains the same problem. I used strip_tags around line 894 of locallib: $str2 = $str1; (became "$str2 = strip_tags($str1);) where it goes to create a field name for a blank and it seems to have corrected my problem. Couldn't find it in the tracker.

ResponsesInList.Title: Bug in Questionnaire for PHP 5.2 (possibly fixed)
ResponsesInList.Text:
I apologize for not looking to see if this has been resolved already extensively, but I have found a bug in the Questionnaire module when using PHP 5.2. The bug can be found in line 293 of the file /mod/questionnaire/locallib.php. Here's the line in question: 
```text
 add_to_log($this->course->id, "questionnaire", "submit", "view.php?id=$this->cm->id", "$this->id", $this->cm->id, $USER->id);
```
 What happens is an error of type "Catchable Fatal Error" is thrown when 4th parameter is passed, because I guess PHP doesn't like double object attribute references in a string context . The fix for it is really simple: 
```text
 add_to_log($this->course->id, "questionnaire", "submit", "view.php?id=" . $this->cm->id, $this->id, $this->cm->id, $USER->id);
```
 Again, apologies if this has already been addressed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: duplicating feedback forms
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes - there is the option of saving a feedback as a template. Then the other teachers/professors simply use the template questions. I am even playing with the idea of automatically (using some manual SQL ing) add the Course Evaluation feedback to the course as a default activity. Until then, here are the instructions I provided our faculty: Instructions for putting template into your class sections : 1) Login to Moodle 2) Go to the course you want to use 3) Turn Editing On 4) Go to the week that you want to add the survey to 5) Add a activity—click on feedback activity a) enter a name for the survey b) enter a description c) if desired, select the open and close dates and times d) leave the feedback responses set to anonymous e) If you want the students to be able to see the results set Show Analysis to Students to Yes; otherwise, leave it set to No f) If you want to receive an email when a student submits a survey set Send Email Notifications to Yes; otherwise, leave it set to No g) If you want students to be able to submit multiple times set Multiple Submit to Yes; otherwise, leave it set to No h) In the Page After Submit box type the text you want displayed to the student after they submit the survey. I usually go with something like "Thank you for your feedback!" i) If you are using a metacourse, set the group mode to visible. Otherwise you can set it to no groups. j) If you want to hide the survey from the students, set Visible to students to Hide; otherwise, leave it set to Show k) Single click on the Save Changes pushbutton 6) You are now ready to add questions to your survey. Single click on the Edit Questions pushbutton. 7) In the Use a Template dropdown box, select the New Student Survey option and then single click on the Use this Template pushbutton. 8) Confirm that you want to use the template by clicking on the Use this Template pushbutton 9) Congratulations, your survey is now ready for the students to take. You may single click on the Continue pushbutton on the top of the page. After the students have completed the surveys you may view the results by coming back to the survey and clicking on the link that reads Analysis (Submitted Answers: #). Feel free to let your Moodle administrator know if you have any questions.

All had the same problem with respect to getting the 'This Course does not exist' error when creating new questionnaires or from templates. I upgraded to Moodle 1.6.3 which did not resolve the issue. I then removed the Questionnaire module then reinstalled it. That not only fixed the creation error but also revealed that the module was not correctly installed. The set up screens for a Questionnaire are now easier to read and are more explanatory. It appeared that this issue arose after upgrading to Moodle 1.6 so, perhaps, the ugrade affected something. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Im destinated never to get surveys/ feedback / questionnaires working
ResponsesInList.Text: That looks like a variation of the problem that you reported the other week.  It isn't a moodle problem as such - PHP is reporting that it is unable to write a PHP session file at /data/session/5/5/ This path may be in your web hosting space (outside of the web root) - the default name for it is moodledata - or (depending on how your hosting server is set up) the server's security setup may not allow moodle to override the standard php setting for session files, and may be storing sessions in a partition elsewhere on the server's disk.  Looking at your previous reports, where you had 80GB free but php was reporting that it was out of space when attempting to write sessions, I would hazard a guess that the latter is the case, and PHP is configured to only write session data in this area that you do not otherwise have access to.  In which case it is either out of space again, or your web server process does not have full access to that area, due to some misconfiguration by the people administering your server. The alternative, if PHP *is* storing sessions in your own hosting space, is again that the web server process (which PHP runs under)  does not have the correct permissions to that area. Do you have command line access (via SSH, for example) to your hosting server?  If so, please have a look for a directory called moodledata, outside of the directory where the moodle php and html files are stored.  In there should be a subdirectory called sessions, and inside that *should* be where moodle stores the session files.  The ID that your web server process runs under ("apache", or "nobody" probably, depending on how your server is configured) should have read and write access to the whole of the moodledata directory, including the sessions directory.  If it doesn't moodle will never be able to handle uploaded files or write sessions files, unpack SCOPRM modules, handle forum attachments and so on. If there are no session files in that directory, and the permissions look correct, then PHP on your server is configured to store the sessions elsewhere and moodle does not have control of it.  In that case it is a job for your server provider to sort out - a PHP-related settings problem. Oh, one last thing - in order for moodle to work correctly, you really need to make sure that PHP is not running in "Safe" mode, and that if it is using the openbasedir directive, that the whole of your hosting space is included in that directive.  Both of these options control and prohibit PHP from using files or running programs outside of the web root directory, and thus prevent moodle from doing its job properly.  These are settings that you will probably need your server provider to check - unless you are runnng your own VPS or dedicated server. regards Sean K

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Anonymous questionnaire  for more students
ResponsesInList.Text: Because if the student is anonymous, the survey has no way of knowing who they are when the come back to view their results. So it gives the result of the previous anon. user to the current one. Changing this would require the user information to be stored with the 'anonymous' result, in which case an anonymous survey would no longer be anonymous. IMO , the best solution is: don't enable survey saving for anonymous surveys.

In order to truly make it anonymous (beyond the first response) the order of the responses when viewing by response should be randomized (it this is not already being done). I have not checked out the code so I am uncertain if this has already been covered. Alternatively, for an anonymous response a log entry could not be made; however, I like the ability as a teacher to check who did and did not do the assignment by reviewing the logs and thus think that randomizing the order of the responses would be more beneficial.

ResponsesInList.Title: Restore is failing.
ResponsesInList.Text: When l tried restoring a course today and it said Could not restore modules! I did some testing by restoring the course many times with one module at a time. I found that the Questionnaire module was the one giving the error. I am running 1.5.4 Moodle and the Questionnaire was downloaded on June 13. Any help?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore is failing - Attn: Mike Churchward
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mike, I found the problem and the solution. When you backup the questionnaire from an old version and try to restore it into a new version, you get this error.  The is a field in the questionnaire table called qtype. This field used to be enum('unlimited','once') and it is now an interger. So when you try to restore, the insert_record function is trying to insert a string into an integer location, hence it fails. Please add this to the restorelib.php (questionnaire_restore_mods) if ( $questionnaire->qtype == 'unlimited' || $questionnaire->qtype == 'once' ) { $qtype = 0; This will ensure this value is only changed when qtype is one of the two strings. Also, in the questionnaire/db/{ mysql , postgres7}.php files, you need to remove all if ($record->qtype == 'unlimited') { $qtype = 0; } else if ($record->type == 'once') { $qtype = 1; } set_field('questionnaire_response', 'qtype', $qtype, 'id', $record->id from the first part when updating questionnaire_response since this table does not have any field called qtype in function questionnaire_upgrade_2006031700() Please let me know if you have any questions and when this is complete.

ResponsesInList.Title: !other option of Check Box and Radio Button question types
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Mike & others I have to start by saying how extremely useful we find the Questionnaire Module in assisting lecturers and administrators to do survey-based research. Thanks for sharing this wonderful resource. I’ve been developing a questionnaire, which mostly performs well as respondents are able to enter and submit their data without any problem. I even receive email copies of each submission. However, intermittently , the software refuses to accept submissions, which means that we cannot actually use the module at all. You can imagine users’ frustration at not being able to submit a questionnaire after they’ve been entering data for about 20 to 30 minutes. After such a failure to submit, respondents will simply not be prepared to enter the data again, or even to complete a paper-based version of the questionnaire that we have distributed. Due to the importance of this particular research in our institution, the team of researchers cannot risk loosing out on any submission. I’m obviously very keen to get this module stable and working reliably as I can see the usefulness of this module in the future of our institution. In an effort to get to the source of the problem, I’ve been testing my particular questionnaire extensively using different browsers. I hope that the following description of the way that I’ve set up the questionnaire and what I believe might be the cause of the problem, would assist in correcting the problem. (Right at the bottom, I’ve also added some background information of our Moodle installation) My questionnaire Although all of my potential respondents are lecturers at our institution, they are not necessarily registered on our Moodle site. I have therefore set up a public questionnaire in a course that allows guest access without a key. Since guest users are usually not able to edit or add to the contents of a course, I’ve added a questionnaire on the Moodle front page (where, guest users can usually change or edit data), obviously linked to the public questionnaire within the course where the data is captured. Other questionnaire settings are as follows: Open or close dates: none specified Type: respond many Respondent type: anonymous Respondent eligibility: all View responses: teachers and students Questionnaire type: Public Save/Resume answers: No I’ve consciously stayed away from anything that might make the questionnaire more complicated, for example, I did not activate Saving/Resume answers or used Section Text in the questionnaire. Neither did I activate a different template. For questionnaires that do not get accepted, I’ve noticed that the !other option of Check Box and Radio Button questions are checked automatically, obviously without any corresponding data, as the respondent has not necessarily checked it. After activiating the setting "Always display this message when a page contains errors" in Internet Explorer, I was able to capture the error messages when the page "does not display correctly". I have listed the details of error messages below. 1. Logged in as a guest on the front page, selecting the !other option for both radio button and check box questions, presents the following error message as soon as I try to enter text in the text box (and, in fact, also for every additional letter I try to enter into the text box): Line: 116 Char: 9 Error: 'elements[...].value' is null or not an object Code: 0 URL : http://moodle.ru.ac.za/mod/quetsionnaire/view.php?id=8076 2. Also logged in as a guest on the front page, even after successfully submitting a questionnaire (which also gets confirmed by the backup email) , I get the following error message: Line: 125 (sometimes 112) Char: 1 Error: 'HTMLArea' is undefined. Code: 0 URL: http://moodle.ru.ac.za/mod/questionnaire/view.php?id=8076 Is there perhaps something wrong in my setup (guests accessing the questionnaire from the front page) or is there it the !other option that is causing the problem. Does anyone perhaps know of a workaround, is this information useful in solving the problem, or am I barking up the wrong tree? Anyone who would like to have a closer look at my questionnaire is welcome to give it a try on http://moodle.ru.ac.za/mod/questionnaire/view.php?id=8076 (choose the "Login as a guest button" when presented with a login page <dry smile>). Any suggestions will be greatly appreciated. Thank you in advance for your help. Markus ------------------------------------------ Our Moodle environment: We are running the latest version of the Questionnaire module (2006031702) on the following environment: Moodle 1.5.3+ 2005060230 (Will be upgrading to 1.6 on Friday) PHP Version 4.4.2 on FreeBSD 6.1-PRERELEASE Apache Version 2.0.55 MySQL client API version 5.0.18.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are there any clear instructions?
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'm having the same problem as you with the creating of new items in
the questionnaire and assume it's a bug.  There's another post in
this forum about it.  My own understanding is pretty vague and I
was trying to re acquaint myself with things when I hit the aforesaid
bug. The distinction between private/public/template is in the results I think.  A questionnaire is a collection of results.  People can add results to a questionnaire
for a period of time.  Private ones collect reults from with a
single course.  Other course admins can't see the questionnaire to have
their teachers/students add results to it.  Public questionnaires are
moodle wide.  All teachers/students (unless restricted) can add
results to the questionnaire while it is open and as long as the course admin or
the site admin makes it available to them (in a course or on the front page ). Templates aren't  questionnaires and don't have results stored with them.  They are banks of items available moodle wide that can be used as the basis for future private or public questionnaires.  A little like the quiz item banks. Hope this helps

Is there an option for e-mailing questionnaire to students? What would be the best strategy? Your thoughts on this issue also? Thanks in advance! Katie

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: E-mail questionnaire to students
ResponsesInList.Text: You're right that the questionnaire module is better than the survey, primarily because the questionnaire module is vastly more customizable than the survey module. As far as email goes, we have had struggles with emails and the questionnaire module. But I think this is still "in the works", but being able to email students the results is not so straight forward at this point. If you want each participants answers sent out individually, then you can simply put the students' addresses in the email field. If you want the total results emailed, then I would suggest that you put a faculty persons email in the email field, and then wait until you get the results finished, export the results to an XML file, and then email the students the XML file. Otherwise, this is a good suggestion for future development. Matt C.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: E-mail questionnaire to students
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Katie - You could email a link to the questionnaire to the students, but they would still need to complete it in the course. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: bug in backup/restore?
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a production server of Linux and one test machine on Windows. This is what I do to have a mirror on the Windows machine. rsync /moodle and /moodledata directories and overwrite /moodle/config.php on Windows to reflect different paths mysqldump  > file.sql (on Linux, with some options to select the databases,...) mysql.exe < file.sql (on Windows) But I suspect that this method is not perfect and some of the links can be incorrect in the destination, but that could be solved by searching/replacing directly in the file.sql. Moreover, all steps should be done together on frozen servers so that there are no transaction between. In this way, I am also able to restore the questionnaire with data. Hope it helps, Miro

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questionnaire: bug in backup/restore?
ResponsesInList.Text: To dump the database, I use command line tools (mysqldump). However, that is entirely equivalent to GUI tools - only faster if you do it frequently and from a batch file. However, it should be synchronised with the content of /moodledata directory - you should consider to block web access between sqldump and backup of /moodledata so that nothing happens. That was what I called in my poor English "frozen server". About the possible links in the mirror server: for example this can happen if there are absolute links (written by users manually) on the source server pointing to some other part of the course. If these are stored in the database in text/blob entry, they will not be translated to a correct location on the mirror server - instead they will still point to the source server. Therefore, it might be necessary to search/replace the sqldump file for such occurences. I hope it helps. Miro

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: survey already completed
ResponsesInList.Text: If you are seeing a 'survey already completed' message, this means that the user has already submitted the survey and is not allowed to resubmit. If you are seeing a survey with data filled out already, you have the questionnaire settings set so that 'Resume' is 'Yes', and they have already filled out the surveay and 'Saved' it but not 'Submitted' it. Setting 'Resume' to 'Yes' means that the users can fill out a survey over multiple sessions, retaining their data. When complete, they must use the 'submit' button. mike

'.$record2->lastname; } else { $userfullname = ''; } Then I modified the email $body initiation line in the same function to read: $body = "From course $coursefullname. Respondent: $userfullname";

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tracking Student Completion of Anonymous Questionnaire Submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ricky - This is one of the feature already slated to be developed. Right now, 'anonymous' isn't completely anonymous. The 'questionnaire_attempts' table tracks all user attempts and stores the response id of the 'questionnaire_response' table always. 'Anonymous', prevents the userid from being entered in the 'questionnaire_response' field, and prevents the user information from being displayed with the results. But, you can always associate the entry in the 'attempts' table with the 'response' table and figure it out. The feature request will provide the ability to do both. Have the respondents hidden from the teachers, or have it completely anonymous - no associations at all. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CSV exports garbled characters in Japanese?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bob, I guess you mean comman seperated variables not current versioning system Do you mean the longstanding problem or a new one? I have no idea about the new problem but, as for the other, for Moodle users' reference. A longstanding problem of moodle is that it exports files in the encoding used for the system (either EUC-JP or Ja_uft8) but Microsoft programs particularly notepad and excel can only cope with JIS.  So this means that the excel file export is a no no, and that one has to use CVS files. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unclear about public questionaire behavior
ResponsesInList.Text: A 'public' questionnaire is used to gather survey data from many courses into one location. A 'private' questionnaire gathers each course's data into that course. When you create a 'public' questionnaire, you are making that questionnaire available to any course. When a course uses that questionnaire, the responses go back to the course that created the public questionnaire. If you copy a template or private questionnaire when creating a new one, you have created a brand new questionnaire with the same content as the one you copied. When you use a public questionnaire, no new questionnaire is created, but rather the new one points to the public one. Hope this helps. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New Version - Postgresql Compliance - Please Test!
ResponsesInList.Text: Harry - Looks like a lot of errors. I guess that auto convert script wasn't worth much. If you can do the conversion, that would be great. The MySQL file is in the same directory as the PostgreSQL file - its called 'mysql.sql'. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New Version - Postgresql Compliance - Please Test!
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay. Just committed another large update to CVS, fixing a lot of problems we had getting PostgreSQL to work with this module. With the help of Harry Burgin, who was kind enough to use his system as a guinea pig, I believe we have a working module. At least, it now seems to work on both my MySQL system and his PostgreSQL system. It should be available in a zip archive from the CVS area in another 24 hours or so. If you have this installed on a Postgres system currently, please remove the module from your system using your 'admin/config/module' function and re-install it. The data tables for the questionnaire need to be rebuilt under PostgreSQL. A number of issues were fixed over the last release, most importantly the Postgres7.sql file. The 'CHAR' values have been changed to 'VARCHAR' to correct for the extra padding Postgres adds with the fixed length 'CHAR' field. Also, some issues that were cropping up in either MySQL or PostgreSQL hopefully have been fixed. These appear to have been caused by the use of 'HTTP_' variables in phpESP, and scope issues. Please let me know if there are new problems. mike

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - You can always get the latest zip here: http://download.moodle.org/modules/ . You will either be using PostgreSQL or MySQL - this depends on your hosting environment. If you've never installed the module, you don't need to worry about re-installing it. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Rate data not saved in CSV export file
ResponsesInList.Text:
Does anyone know a workaround for this problem? I have a questionnaire in which I have used the 'Rate (scale 1 ..5)'
Type question. Some 250 students have answered the questionnaire and all
the results appear within the Moodle interface. However, when I export
the results as a CSV file the results for the items that used the 'Rate
(scale 1 ..5)' Type question are wrong. There are two versions of this problem: On my production site I am using Moodle 1.4.3, and Questionnaire Module
version 2005030101. In this case all of the item names appear in the
top row of the CSV file, but all of the results for the 'Rate
(scale 1 ..5)' Type are missing. On my experimental site I am using Moodle 1.5, and Questionnaire Module
version 2005062701. With this set up, only the result of the last 'Rate
(scale 1 ..5)' Type is reported. What is more, the reported results is
one less (minus 1) than the actual number chosen. Having
done a search for 'CSV export' within the Questionnaire forum, it seems
that I am not the only Moodler to have experienced this problem. For
example see Peter Noelle's posting , and Alex Walker's posting . I realise that for any future questionnaires I make, the solution
will be to use another item type (e.g. radio buttons), however is there
anyway that I can extract the results for the 'Rate
(scale 1 ..5)' Type items in the questionnaire that has already
been answerd by 250 students on my production site . I had the results
sent to my email, so it may be possible for me to convert these 250
emails into a CSV file, however, if anyone knows a simpler solution, I'd
much appeciate your advice. Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Text: I would like to give the same questionnaire for each course and lesson , and tabulate the results both by lesson and by course. I can do it manually by using a Template, but it is rather boring to repeat it for each week and each course. Is there any way to automate this? BTW , 'Public' would be ideal, if I could separate the results at least by course, if not by week/lesson.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bug in Questionnaire?

I usually test the decision of whether to allow an option to be configurable against the impact it would have on the activity's purpose. If having it there vs. not having it there would change the way the activity functions, and thus change the way it could be used in the course, then I add a configuration option for it. In this case, I could see no change to function for it being there vs. not being there. Anyone else have an opinion? mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using the same questionnaire in two courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Piersante - A Public questionnaire is one that can be used across multiple courses, with all the results staying together. The course that it is created in is the one that can look at the results. A Private questionnaire can only be used in the course it is defined in. If you want to use the same questionnaire privately, in many course, create it as a Template . A template questionnaire cannot be used directly, but can be copied to a private questionnaire when you create it. When you create a new, private questionnaire, you have the option of creating it from scratch, or copying another questionnaire. You can copy a Template questionnaire from any course, or a private questionnaire from the same course. Hope this helps. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Serious bug: Guest is allowed to fill in questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Q has a 'respond once' setting for anonymous, which IIRC gather checks an IP or a cookie (Mike?). But really of course you can't. But if you force login, then of courseit isn't anonymous. Mostly we rely on the fact that these are prettylong surveys we give and most folks are far too busy to try and stuffthe box-and they aren't on that controversial of subjects that anyone is likely to have a big axe to grind. This is certainly an issue with student evals, but since Moodle logs 'anon' responses of logged in students, it probably shouldn't be used for that in it's current form. We use it for a number of forms that aren't really surveys, but need emailing and CSV export. We have a complete set of custom reports based on various fields working with Q, at some point we'll try to release them (hardcoded table names now ). But the main thing is folks can take them from an url without having to login, which makes the mod very useful for quickly making public forms and surveys that don't require login (in our experience, if you require a login for a survey your response rate goes down the drain). So we'll have to hack that out if it gets put in (can you comment it with something easy to find if you 'fix' this Mike?). In general, I think anonymous surveys about controversial subjects are probably a very hard thing to do right. For instance we've built surveys for clients where the authentication was completely separate from the results, however the survey got a very low response rate and in informally checking with some of the subjects we found--quite reasonably--that they didn't believe that the results actually were separate, after all the system knew who they were before they took the survey. Cookie setting and IP checking certainly reduce the chances of ballot stuffing, but I think it's a pretty tough thing to get right overall.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Serious bug: Guest is allowed to fill in questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: This looks good-enough to be reliable in most circumstances--use long forms, IP-checking and avoid dangerous topics.  I agree response rates are the most important thing--and anonymous surveys will allow that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Serious bug: Guest is allowed to fill in questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, If my understanding of the way the Q works is correct, then the only way you can get information about who filled out an anonymous Q (even with moodle authenticaton) is by comparing timestamps in the moodle logs with timestamps on the CSV-export spreadsheet. And this is only circumstantial information - not hard information. There is no information in the CSV-export about ip-address, username, name, etc. if the survey is anonymous. So an anonymous survey is basically just that, even if users have to authenticate. Suggestion: One could still improve anonymity a bit by not logging questionnaire activity in the moodle logs for anonymous questionnaires. Lars.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Serious bug: Guest is allowed to fill in questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay, just to clarify some things. 'Anonymous' questionnaires are anonymous to phpESP only. The data that is retrieved using the reporting system won't indicate anything about the Moodle user who responded. The Moodle tables that track usage will still have data about which users responded. All questionnaire responses are recorded in the'questionnaire_attempts' table. These include user id. Multiple vs. single attempts are enforced using this table. Now, we could enforce even more anonymity by not tracking the userid with the responses, if this is important. As for guest responses, they are logged with the guest userid. For this reason, single completion questionnaires with guest responses wouldn't be very useful. Only the first guest login would be allowed. So, for now, I will implement it this way: anonymous questionnaires will allow guest access if they allow multiple submissions and are not restricted to either teachers or students (i.e. everyone can complete them). This change is now in CVS. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Serious bug: Guest is allowed to fill in questionnaire
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mike, All questionnaire responses are recorded in the'questionnaire_attempts'table. These include user id. Multiple vs. single attempts are enforcedusing this table. This info is off limits to anyone but the moodle admin, so the only way a moodle instructor can get info about usernames is by comparing timestamps in moodle logs and on the csv spreadsheet. Would it be possible to eliminates the logs for anonymous surveys? Now, we could enforce even more anonymity by not tracking the userid with the responses, if this is important. Good idea for anonymous surveys! Lars.

ResponsesInList.Text: OK, I did find something more... $FULLME is defined in moodle/lib/setup.php as: $FULLME = qualified_me(); ... qualified_me() is defined in moodle/lib/weblib.php as $url[' host '] where $url is an array obtained by: $url = parse_url($CFG-> wwwroot ); .... parse_url() is a PHP function that divides a URL in an array, where array['host'] contains the host. array['port'] contains the port etc So it is here that the port information gets lost! Now I don't know where the bug is: Is questionnaire that wasn't supposed to call $FULLME to get the address? Is setup.php that wasn't supposed to call qualified_me() to form $FULLME? ResponsesInList.Title: New Release - Management & Reporting Now in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text:
Its been a long time coming, but I have just released a new version of
the questionnaire module. This version begins the process of bringing
the phpESP management and reporting features into Moodle. This version allows owners of questionnaires to edit the content of that questionnaire at any time. There is no need to use 'test', 'edit' and 'activate' modes any longer. I have attached the README.TXT file here to describe the details. Here are the highlights: Adding
a questionnaire is now done from one interface. When you add the questionnaire to
the course, you will be offered the option of creating a brand new one,
copying an existing one or using a public one. Viewing the
results of the questionnaire can be done from the same screen as the
questionnaire view. If you have the rights to view them, there will be
a link at the
top right of the screen. There is now three types of questionnaires. 1.
Private - the most commonly used type. A private questionnaire belongs to the
course it was created in and cannot be accessed outside of that course.
Topic Leaders can change the content of the questionnaire and view the results. 2.
Template - A template questionnaire can be copied into any other course. This
is an ideal way to provide complex questionnaires as a starting point.
Template questionnaires cannot be used as questionnaires on their own.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jamie - Sorry its taken so long to get back to you... I'm going to answer both of your last posts at once. First off, the questionnaire module is based on phpESP, an Open Source survey tool. Most of the table structures are phpESP's and are thus inherited. I took this tool and made it work with Moodle. To do this, I took some liberties with the meanings of several of the fields. There are three 'types' of questionnaires you can create: 1) Private - a standard Moodle activity. The questionnaire and its results are only available within the defining course. 2) Public - this instance of the questionnaire can be used in other courses. Its results can be seen only within the defining course. 3) Template - this instance of the questionnaire cannot be used at all, except to be copied to another questionnaire. Any course can copy this instance. When you create a questionnaire, you can create any one of these three types, and you can can create them in three different ways. 1) Create new - start from scratch and use the phpESP interface to add a new questionnaire and its questions. 2) Copy existing - copy an existing questionnaire into a new instance and use it as is, or change it as needed. You can copy any questionnaire owned by the defining course and any template questionnaire in other courses. 3) Use public - in this case, you cannot do anything else with the questionnaire. You are assigining an instance of a public questionnaire to this activity. Your participants will be able to fill out the questionnaire, but only the teachers of the defining course will be able to see the results. As to your next set of questions, with the update to the module, I changed the way the 'owner' field is used. The 'ower' field is a phpESP field that doesn't have a direct Moodle translation. It used to be owner by 'root', which was the phpESP admin account, and any Moodle administrator would have full pivileges. Now, it contains the id of the course that created it. When you do an upgrade, a script is run that updates all existing questionnaires and assigns them a course owner. You should not manually change these fields unless you know what you are doing. Similarly, the 'realm' field is a phpESP construct that implements designer groups in phpESP. I now use that field to distinguish between 'private', 'public' and 'template'. Hope this helps. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can one access survey results
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you using the newest version of the questionnaire mod? If so, you shouldn't use the phpESP interface anymore anyway. (the rest of this post will assume that you are) The newest version is set up to just this. What you can do is create a questionnaire in a master course and make it public. When you create the questionnaire in other courses, use it as the content - it will be in the list of public surveys. The survey cannot be changed in the other courses, nor can the results be viewed (which is a problem to you). So, in the master course, enrol the teachers from the other courses as teachers and they can view the results of the survey there. Another option is to designate the master survey as a template. Then they can use the same questionnaire, but they can also change it and see the results. But, each questionnaire's results will be unique to that course. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can one access survey results
ResponsesInList.Text: So, you want one public survey to be used across multiple courses so that the data all pertains to the same survey. But, you want the teachers in a course to be able to see the responses by the students in their course, and no other courses. Is this correct? Right now, that isn't possible. Only teachers of the course that owns the survey can see the responses, and they can see them all. Teachers of courses that are using the survey, but not owning it, cannot see any responses (unless they are also teachers of the owning course). As a partial solution, change the survey to a template and make one copy of it for each course. It won't be as easy to see all responses from all courses - you'll have to download the CSV results from each survey and combine them - but you will have the security you require. I'll look at adding these functions to the questionnaire module. I could see how they could be useful. What I would do is allow a public survey to be configured such that teachers of a course using it could be allowed to see the results or prevented, depending on the setting. This may take a while to implement though. mike
